vmm_data
The vmm_data class provides some common functions required by any data payload.
User-defined payload can be derived from this class to make use of these functions. The
standard library provides the following macros to use these functions.
Macros Usage
1. VMM_DATA (user payload class)
Use this macro to define a payload class.
2. VMM_DATA_CTOR (user payload class){ …}
Use this macro to define a constructor when the payload is derived from vmm_data.
However, if your payload has multiple base classes, provide your own constructor.
3. VMM_DATA_MEMBER_BEGIN (user payload class)
Call this macro inside a user payload class definition. This macro is mandatory and
should be used before using the following macro.
4. VMM_DATA_MEMBER_BASE_CLASS (base class)

Call this macro for each and every base class of user payload class with the name of
the base class as its argument.
The macros from 5-13 are used based on the type of the member variable
name of the user payload class.
The following arguments are used with these macros:
◦ type: Gives the type of the member variable.
◦ member: Member variable name.
◦ length: Length of the array.
◦ do_what: Is an enum with values DO_PRINT, DO_COPY, DO_COMPARE, DO_PACK,
DO_UNPACK, and DO_ALL. Depending on this value, the variable is involved in the
common functions.
◦ do_how: Is an enum with the following values:
▪ DO_NOCOPY, DO_REFCOPY, DO_DEEPCOPY
▪ HOW_TO_COPY (OR of all DO_*COPY)
▪ DO_NOCOMPARE, DO_REFCOMPARE, DO_DEEPCOMPARE
▪ HOW_TO_COMPARE (OR of all DO_*COMPARE)
▪ DO_NONE (OR of all DO_NO*)
▪ DO_REF (OR of all DO_REF*)
▪ DO_DEEP (OR of all DO_DEEP*)
◦ format: The member variable is printed based on this format. For example, <<hex,
<<dec, and so on. This argument can also be left blank.
5. VMM_DATA_MEMBER_SCALAR (type, member, do_what, format )
Use this macro for any C++/SystemC scalar data types and std::string, but not for
char pointers.
6. VMM_DATA_MEMBER_SCALAR_ARRAY (type, member, length, do_what, format )
Use this macro for C++/SystemC arrays of scalar types and arrays of std::string.
7. VMM_DATA_MEMBER_SCALAR_PTR (type, member, length, do_what, do_how,
format)

Use this macro for any C++/SystemC pointers and std::string pointers. You should
allocate sufficient space for these pointers.
8. VMM_DATA_MEMBER_CHAR_PTR (type, member, do_what, format )
This macro can be used for C++/SystemC char pointers.
9. VMM_DATA_MEMBER_ENUM (type, member, do_what, format )
This macro can be used for enum types.
10. VMM_DATA_MEMBER_ENUM_ARRAY (type, member, length, do_what, format )
This macro can be used for an array of enums.
11. VMM_DATA_MEMBER_VMM_DATA (type, member, do_what, format )
Use this macro for any member objects of type vmm_data and its derivatives.
12. VMM_DATA_MEMBER_VMM_DATA_ARRAY (type, member, do_what, format )
Use this macro for any member which is an array of objects of type vmm_data and its
derivatives.

vmm_log
The vmm_log feature in VMM-SC provides an exception reporting facility to report an
exceptional situation. This facility is provided with the help of macros.
Macros
• VMM_VERBOSE
• VMM_DEBUG
• VMM_TRACE
• VMM_NOTE
• VMM_WARNING
• VMM_ERROR
• VMM_FATAL
The usage of all the above macros is the same as in VMM-SV.
Controlling Log Report

1. SET_SEVERITY(severity)
Call this macro to set the severity. The expected values are as follows:
◦ ERROR_MSG_TYPE: Prints only VMM_ERROR messages.
◦ WARNING_MSG_TYPE: Prints VMM_WARNING and VMM_ERROR messages.
◦ NOTE_MSG_TYPE: Prints VMM_WARNING, VMM_ERROR, and VMM_NOTE messages.
◦ TRACE_MSG_TYPE: Prints VMM_WARNING, VMM_ERROR, VMM_NOTE, and VMM_TRACE
messages.
◦ DEBUG_MSG_TYPE: Prints VMM_WARNING, VMM_ERROR, VMM_NOTE, VMM_TRACE, and
VMM_DEBUG messages.
VERBOSE_MSG_TYPE: Prints all messages.
By default, the severity is set to NOTE_MSG_TYPE.
2. STOP_AFTER_N_ERRORS(limit)
Call this macro to set a limit on the number of reports (ERROR types) that can cause
simulation to call sc_stop () .
For example, STOP_AFTER_N_ERRORS(10);
This macro sets the default error count to 10.
vmm_opts
VMM-SC allows configuring VMM transactors, VMM components, and verification
environments using vmm_opts. Configuration parameters can be set using the following
three different sources in order of decreasing priority:
1. Command-line options
2. Command-file options
3. Set_* methods
The command-line and command-file options are only supported in the SV interop flow. In
pure VMM-SC, these options are not supported.

SystemC or SystemVerilog is suitable for a specific project requirement.
The transfer of packet data between SystemC and SystemVerilog is achieved by the TLI
adaptors available as a separate package.
The following important components for a verification environment are listed:
• Transaction data classes to specify the payload data
• Multiple verification components implemented as transactors
• Transaction-level interfaces to connect various transactors
• One or more sub-blocks instantiating lower-level transactors
• Top-level verification environment
• Multiple test cases
VMM provides base classes to implement each verification component and guidelines to
implement robust and reusable testbenches. A few other base classes and utilities like
vmm_opts are provided for ease of use and controlling the testbench behavior from the
test-case level. VMM-SC provides a message service utility for issuing message reports
from the testbench.
A verification environment developed in VMM-SC can be used to verify a transaction-level
reference model. This can also be reused to verify the pin-level RTL. The pin-level RTL
can be in SystemC, Verilog-HDL, VHDL, or a combination of these HDLs.

Defining Transaction Data Objects Using vmm_data
VMM-SC provides a vmm_data base class for defining the packet data. User extensions
of the vmm_data class. This specifies the member fields of the payload data class. The
shorthand macros available with vmm_data provide an implementation of basic functions
such as byte_pack, byte_unpack, print, compare, and copy. These are required for
most payload classes.
You can also use the OSCI-TLM2 tlm_generic_payload class as a payload class in a
VMM-SC environment.
Example 80 Transaction Class Defined Using vmm_data
VMM_DATA(my_payload)
{
VMM_DATA_CTOR(my_payload){};
int addr;
int data;

VMM_DATA_MEMBER_BEGIN(my_payload)
VMM_DATA_MEMBER_BASE_CLASS(vmm_data)
VMM_DATA_MEMBER_SCALAR(int,addr,DO_ALL,<<hex)
VMM_DATA_MEMBER_SCALAR(int,data,DO_ALL,<<hex)
VMM_DATA_MEMBER_END(my_payload)
};
Example 80 shows the transaction data class extended from vmm_data. There
are two member variables, addr and data. The use of shorthand macros,
'vmm_data_member_scalar for each member variable provides the implementation of
member functions. For example, byte_pack, byte_unpack, and others.
For the complete list and functionality of the methods implemented by the shorthand
macros, see the VMM User Guide.
Issuing Message Reports Using VMM Log Macros
The macros provided in VMM-SC match the different severity-level macros provided in
VMM (Verification Methodology Manual) SystemVerilog. In pure VMM-SC, the messages
are internally issued by sc_report_handler. The messages are issued on standard
output by default. If the sc_report_handler is set to issue the messages into another log
file, the VMM log messages are also redirected to the same log file.

Communication Between Transactors
VMM-SC does not specifically provide any transaction-level interface. The OSCI-TLM 2.0
is the recommended transaction-level interface that you should use to connect various
verification components. You can also use other transaction-level interfaces like TLM1.0 or
sc_fifo.
Defining Verification Environment Using vmm_group
A verification environment or sub-environment instantiates, connects, and controls the
underlying lower-level transactors. A verification environment is implemented in VMM-SC
by extending the vmm_group or vmm_subenv class.

The vmm_group and vmm_subenv classes have the same phases as those in the
vmm_xactor. The vmm_group is an implicitly phased environment class. The phases of
the children of the vmm_group class are also called implicitly in a top-down or bottom-up
manner. That is depending on the phase.
The vmm_subenv provides both implicit and explicit phase methods. In implicit phasing, the
children of vmm_subenv are not called implicitly. The particular phase method of the child
must be called in the appropriate phase method of vmm_subenv.
For more details on vmm_group and vmm_subenv, see the VMM User Guide.
Example 86 Verification Environment Using vmm_group
class env: public vmm_group
{
initiator* initiator0;
target* target0;

in_socket->b_transport( *trans, delay );

}
}
Coordinating Simulation Using vmm_timeline
Use the vmm_timeline class to coordinate simulation through a user-defined timeline.
A verification environment can have a single timeline controlling the top-level verification
components. This can also have multiple timelines in different verification sub-
environments connected hierarchically to a top-level timeline.
The top-level timeline is instantiated in the verification top, which is usually an sc_module
extension. This verification top instantiates a top-level timeline. This instantiates the
verification environment and connects the timeline to the verification environment. This
also executes the timeline by calling the run_phase() method of vmm_timeline.
For more details on vmm_timeline, see the VMM User Guide.
Example 88 The Usage of vmm_timeline to Coordinate Simulation
class sc_top: public sc_module
{
sc_top(sc_module_name name):sc_module(name)
{

t1->run_phase();
sc_start(50000,SC_NS);
return 0;
}

You can synchronize VMM-SC transactors with VMM-SV transactors using the interop
solution (that is, you can synchronize the phases in the VMM-SC and VMM-SV worlds).
The interop use model depends on whether vmm_timeline or vmm_simulation is a top
level. It is recommended to use vmm_simulation as a top level.
Interconnects in Interop Flow
The interop flow interconnects to communicate between the two languages (SC and SV).
For this purpose you have two interconnect classes, one in SC and the other in SV.

• Interconnect class in SC: vmm_interop
• Interconnect class in SV: vmm_interop
Interconnect class in SC: vmm_interop:
Use this SC class to call phases in SV-SC interop mode using the following static
methods:
1. run_phase(interop_dir dir, vmm_timeline* top_timeline):
This method is called when you have vmm_timeline as a top level and need to run SV
and SC phases in sync.
The first argument is an enum which takes the direction. Valid values are as follows:
◦ vmm_interop::SV_DRV (when the direction is SV->SC)
◦ vmm_interop::SC_DRV (when the direction is SC->SV)
The second argument is a top-level timeline.
2. run_tests (interop_dir dir, string tests):
This method is called when you have vmm_simulation as a top level and want to run
SV and SC phases in sync.
The first argument is an enum which takes the direction. Valid values are as follows:
◦ vmm_interop::SV_DRV (when the direction is SV->SC)
◦ vmm_interop::SC_DRV (when the direction is SC->SV)
The second argument is vmm_test name, which needs to run. By default, it runs all
tests registered.
Interconnect class in SV: vmm_interop:
This SV class is used to call phases in SV-SC interop mode using the following static
methods:
1. run_phase (interop_dir dir, vmm_timeline top_timeline):
This method is called when you have vmm_timeline as a top level and want to run SV
and SC phases in sync.
The first argument is an enum which takes the direction. Valid values are as follows:
◦ vmm_interop::SV_DRV (when the direction is SV->SC)
◦ vmm_interop::SC_DRV (when the direction is SC->SV)
The second argument is a top-level timeline.

2. run_tests(interop_dir dir, string tests):
This method is called when you have vmm_simulation as a top level and want to run
SV and SC phases in sync.
The first argument is an enum which takes the direction. Valid values are as follows:
◦ vmm_interop::SV_DRV (when the direction is SV->SC)
◦ vmm_interop::SC_DRV (when the direction is SC->SV)
The second argument is vmm_test name, which needs to run. By default, it runs all
tests registered.

This chapter contains the following features:
• Executing Multiple Tests in SystemC Testbench Flow
Executing Multiple Tests in SystemC Testbench Flow
VCS enables you to have multiple top-level tests (sc_module) in the testbench (SystemC-
on-top) and allows you to compile all the tests at once and then you can select the test you
want to run during runtime.
In addition, VCS also provides you a capability to write all the new tests together even
after creating the executable (simv). VCS then enables you to compile only the new tests
and run the simulation by selecting one of the compiled tests.
This feature enables the runtime selection of a test scenario in a SystemC testbench
(SystemC on top designs). Each test scenario is defined in its own function. The name of
the function can be anything including sc_main. The rest of the design remains constant.
Quick compile turnaround time can be achieved for different test scenarios by compiling
each top level SystemC test as a separate shared library and selecting the test to execute
during runtime.
Perform the following steps to execute multiple tests in SystemC testbench flow:
1. Build the SystemC-on-top design, where initial testbench (bootstrap test) is instantiated
in sc_main. Also, the option -sysc=shared and -sysc=show_sc_main should be
passed during the elaboration. This bootstrap test is the test that you can modify for the
different tests based on the requirement.
//sc_main.cpp
extern "C" int sc_main(int, char **) {
vhdl1 m1("vhdl1");
vlog1 m2("vlog1");
sc_sub m3("sub");

Chapter 18: SystemC Features
Executing Multiple Tests in SystemC Testbench Flow
4. To select alternate tests, a runtime option is required. There are two different ways that
you can use to select an alternate test. One is using -Mdir name and the other is to
specify the complete path to the shared lib. Both are used with the flag -syscconf.
simv -syscconf=test1:basic_test
simv -syscconf=test1:test1
simv -syscconf=<your path>/test2/sysc/libtest2_sysc.so:test2
1. The HDL part of the design should remain the same in the alternate testbenches as in
the bootstrap test. The instance names of different testbenches should also be same
as in the bootstrap test.
2. This feature is supported only on RHEL32 platforms: RHEL32, RHEL64, suse32, and
suse64.
3. Modifying the testbench is not allowed with process save/restore.
• Verdi interactive debugging is not supported; only post-process debug is supported.
• A VPD file containing SystemC must be created with PVPD flow and explicit UCLI
‘dump’ commands.
• Creating a VPD file with $vcdpluson is not supported.
• All SystemC instances must be located in the main partition, if inout (bidirectional) ports
are used in a SystemC/HDL interface model.

Bidirectional Converter Support with UPF
System-Verilog does not allow designers to connect a signal to a port if their types are
incompatible. For example, VCS issues "Port-Connection Type Mismatch" error if a wreal
net is connected to a logic port. For the ease of use (under -xlrm enable_converter
option), VCS supports automatic insertion of converter module to bridge up a signal with
a port of incompatible types. You need to provide converter modules and converter-rules
through VCS opt-config file.
For unidirectional conversion (such as logic-to-real or real-to-logic), converter modules
can be developed easily. However, if the dataflow is bidirectional, then developing such
converter is challenging.
Bidir-Island in Presence of UPF
In the presence of UPF, the low-power network-gates (such as ISOLATION, SRSN, SPA
and so on) may get inserted at the power-domain boundaries. These network-gates may
break the net-port connectivity in the design.
Hence, at bidir-island determination time the RNM algorithm should honor the presence
of the low-power network-gates. Based on the presence of these network-gates, there
could be multiple bidir-islands in the design instead of a single island that used to be there
without UPF. The following diagram shows example of Bidir-Islands with UPF.

Overriding Connectmodule
ams_cm
Enables the override of connect rules and connect module parameters in the Verilog-AMS-
SPICE flow.
Using this command, you can override the following:
• General parameters of one or more connect module instances
• Connect module insertion mode (split | merge)
• Connect rule for connect module insertion
This command does not change any disciplines in the design (for this, use
ams_set_discipline).
This command is functional only when the Verilog-AMS-SPICE flow is enabled
using the VCS -ams option. If the Verilog-AMS-SPICE flow is not enabled, this
command is ignored and a warning message is output.
ams_cm connect_rule_module_parameter_name=parameter_value
[mode=split | merge]
[crules=connect_module_library_name.connect_rule_name]
[library=library_name]
[cell=cell_name [node=node_name]]
[inst=inst_name [node=node_name]
[node=hier_name]
connect_rule_module_parameter_name=parameter_value
Specifies the connect rule or connect module parameter and the value to which it is set.
The parameter_value can be either real or a string parameter. If you specify override

information for a nonexistent parameter of a connect rule or connect module, then that
override is ignored.
mode=split | merge
Specifies the connect module insertion mode. The default is merge.
crules=connect_module_library_name.connect_rule_name
Specifies the connect rules. The default for the .connect_rule_name extension is
snps_crules.
Multiple connect rules cannot be specified for the same ams_cm command, but
multiple connect rules can be referenced with separate ams_cm commands.
library=library_name
Specifies the name of the logical library for which the connect module is inserted or
connected globally.
cell=cell_name [node=node_name]
Specifies the cell or cell/node names for which the connect module is inserted or
connected. The node name is optional; if it is not specified, the command is applied to all
nodes of the selected cell.
inst=inst_name [node=node_name]
Specifies the hierarchical instance path or instance/node names for which the connect
module is inserted or connected. The node name is optional; if it is not specified, the
command is applied to all nodes of the selected cell.
node=hier_name
Specifies the hierarchical node name for which the connect module is inserted or
connected.
The following examples show different uses of the ams_cm command:
ams_cm vsup=3.3;
This example globally overrides the vsup parameter value (3.3) for all connect modules
connected or inserted throughout the design.
ams_cm vsup=3.2 node=ClockTop.I3.y;

This example overrides the vsup parameter value (3.2) for any connect modules
connected or inserted on node ClockTop.I3.y.
There could be multiple connect modules inserted on the node ClockTop.I3.y
depending on whether the connect module insertion mode is set to split or
merge.
Example 3
ams_cm vsup=3.222 cell=dflop;
This example overrides the vsup parameter value (3.222) for all connect modules
connected or inserted for any cell named dflop in the design.
Example 4
ams_cm vsup=3.333 inst=ClockTop2.I3;
This example overrides the vsup parameter value (3.333) for all connect modules
connected or inserted for the instance ClockTop2.I3 in the design.
Example 5
ams_cm vsup=3.3;
ams_cm vsup=3.222 inst=ClockTop2.I3.I5;
ams_cm vsup=3.444 node=ClockTop2.I3.net18;
This example:
• Globally overrides the vsup parameter value (3.3) for all connect modules connected
or inserted throughout the design.
• Then overrides the vsup parameter value (3.222) for all connect modules connected or
inserted for the instance ClockTop2.I3.I5 in the design.
• Then overrides the vsup parameter value (3.444) for any connect modules connected
or inserted on node ClockTop2.I3.net18.
Example 6
ams_cm vsup=3.3;
ams_cm crules=snpsConnectLib.snps_ana_crules vddnet=top.vdd1
inst=ClockTop.I3;
This example:
• Globally overrides the vsup parameter value (3.3) for all connect modules connected
or inserted throughout the design.
Then overrides the vddnet parameter for dynamic supply on instance ClockTop.I3 in
the design using the connect rules in sn

Example 7
ams_cm mode=split;
This example globally changes the connect mode to split.

Improved MSV Parameter Override and Optimizations in
Verilog-AMS Flow
Simulating mixed-signal SystemVerilog/Verilog-AMS designs involves cosimulation where
VCS identifies and isolates analog parts for processing by an analog engine. Parameter
overrides for connect module instances and analog components in Verilog-AMS (VAMS)
modules are partitioned to the analog simulator in a partition file. A current challenge in
this process is the inefficient method of providing parameter override information through a
partition file, which requires the analog engine to process numerous long paths, creating a
performance bottleneck during the analog elaboration phase.

Improved MSV Parameter Override and Optimizations in Verilog-AMS Flow
VCS provides the following optimizations that improve mixed-signal elaboration
performance. These optimizations efficiently partition analog parameter override
information from VCS and transfer it to the analog simulator:
• Improved Partitioning for Verilog-AMS Parameter Values
• Improved Partitioning of SPICE Primitive Parameter Values
• Improved Partitioning Format for Sharing Hierarchical Information
Improved Partitioning for Verilog-AMS Parameter Values
VCS resolves all parameters at the compilation stage. In previous releases, the final
analog parameter values are transferred to the analog simulator in a hierarchical format
through a partition file. This may result in performance issues for the analog engine.
To improve simulation performance, VCS partitions the most common parameter value
is partitioned in a "folded" manner (optimization technique) as an instance parameter
override within the partition file. For scenarios requiring hierarchical information, a
flattened hierarchical format is provided. Enable this feature by using the -adopt
sp_param_part_enh compile option.
To optimize performance, parameter information is partitioned via a hierarchical parameter
partition file. Consider the following testcases:
Example 101 Top Module
electrical e1, e2;
wire w1, w2;
mid m1();
mid m2();
mid m3();
Example 102 VAMS Module with Parameter Override
module mid ();
wire pi1, pi2, pi3 ;
wire po1, po2, po3 ;

ams_cdef_net
Connects an electrical net to an analog power or ground electrical net. When the netlist
for the design does not contain the connectivity for the power and ground network, this
command is used to create that connection.
This command is used with the ams_supply and ams_cdef_inst commands to
allow power-aware connect modules in the design.
ams_cdef_net -cell cell_name [-lib library_name]
-net {net_name [, net_name] …}
-default_supply {attribute_name => net_name};
Specifies the cell name.
-lib library_name
Specifies the library name. This is the VCS compiled library.
-net {net_name [, net_name] …}
Specifies a list of net names that are connected to the net specified by the
-default_supply argument. These nets are declared inside the specified cell.
-default_supply {attribute_name => net_name}
Specifies the name of the net associated with the list in the -net argument.

The following example shows one use of the ams_cdef_net command:
• This example electrically connects the net vdd2 in the cell blk02 to the net top.vdd.
ams_cdef_net -cell blk02 -net {vdd2} -default_supply {vdd2_tag =>
top.vdd};
ams_cdef_inst
Overrides connectivity to power and ground nets given from ams_cdef_net commands.
This command is used when specific instances in the designs have different power and
ground connections.
This command is used with the ams_supply and ams_cdef_net commands to
allow power-aware connect modules in the design.
The ams_cdef_inst command accepts the name of a local net, or the name of a global
net specified through a hierarchical path.
The following figure displays a cell developed in isolation of a top level design.

ams_cdef_inst
[ -lib < library_name | WORK > ]
[ -inst { { instance_name }* } ]
-supply { { attribute_name [: new_attribute_name]
=> name_of_the_local_net|name_of_the_global_net }* }
Defines the name of a cell or module to be used for scoping.
-lib library_name
Defines the name of a VCS logical compilation library to be used for scoping. If this option
is not specified, the default value WORK is used.
-inst { { instance_name }* }
Comma-separated list of instance names within a selected cell and library combination.
If the instance name is not specified, the command applies to all instances within the
selected cell.
-supply { { attribute_name [: new_attribute_name]
=> name_of_the_local_net|name_of_the_global_net }* }
Defines the local net or the port of a cell specified with -cell argument or a global net
for establishing a connection to a list of nets specified earlier. The attribute_name
option is used as an identifier of a previously created connection using the ams_cdef_net
command. The connection previously defined by the attribute_name option is overridden
using the new definitions provided in this option. The [: new_attribute_name] option is
used to change the name of the attribute as visible downward in the design hierarchy.
The following example shows one use of the ams_cdef_net and ams_cdef_inst
commands:
• This example electrically connects the net vdd2 in the cell blk02 to the net top.vdd
for all instances of blk02 in the design with the exception of instances i1 instantiated
within the cell blk02. For such instances, net vdd2 is connected to top.vdd1.
ams_cdef_net -cell blk02 -net {vdd2} -default_supply
{vdd2_tag => top.vdd};

{vdd2_tag => top.vdd1};
ams_supply

Associates the analog supply information with digital port signals in the Verilog-AMS flow.
This command is used for Verilog-AMS modules that have digital signal ports and analog
supply ports.
Note: This command works with connect modules that use the snps_cm_power and
snps_cm_ground attributes as internal electrical supplies.
This command is used with the ams_cdef_net and ams_cdef_inst commands to allow
power-aware connect modules in the design.
ams_supply -cell cell_name [-lib library_name]
-digital_port {digital_port_name [, digital_port_name] …}
-supply {port_power => power_port_name, port_ground => ground_port_name};
Specifies the cell name.
-lib library_name
Specifies the library name. This is the VCS compiled library.
-digital_port {digital_port_name, digital_port_name, …}
Specifies a list of digital port names that are associated with the supply set.
-supply {port_power => power_port_name, port_ground => ground_port_name}
Specifies the names of the power and ground nets that are associated with the list of
digital port signals mentioned in the -digital_port argument.
The following examples show different uses of the ams_supply command:
• This example associates the logic ports y and a to the power port vdd and ground port
gnd

logical din;
electrical aout;

(* snps_cm_power = "snps_global.vdd0"*) electrical vdd_local ;
(* snps_cm_ground = "snps_global.vss0"*) electrical vss_local ;

In the above example, two electrical nets vdd_local and vss_local are declared in the
connect module ‘L2E’ and they have snps_cm_power and snps_cm_ground attributes
respectively. Hence, inside this connect module vdd_local is considered as the power
net, and vss_local as the ground net. These (local) supply nets ('vdd_local' and
'vss_local') are used to model the digital-analog conversion inside this connect module.
Characteristics of snps_cm_power and snps_cm_ground attributes in a connect module:
• A connect module may contain at most one net with the snps_cm_power attribute.
• A connect module may contain at most one net with the snps_cm_ground attribute.
• A single net cannot have both the attributes.
• The nets with snps_cm_power and snps_cm_ground attributes must be electrical nets.
• The nets with these attributes are not port nodes.
Connect modules (CMs) form the boundary between analog and digital domains. The
correct behavior of a CM often depends on its power and ground supply information, which
influences thresholds and conversion logic.
VCS extends the existing ams_cdef_net_cm command to allow inheritance of supply nets
for CM power and ground pins when no supply is explicitly derived from the connected
digital ports. This enhancement supports 'look-above' (hierarchical) supply inheritance.
By enabling the -inherited_supply feature within ams_cdef_net_cm, connect modules
can now inherit power and ground supplies directly from the design hierarchy when no
explicit supply information is available on connected digital ports. This allows connect
modules to correctly reflect real design power conditions even in flows where supply
information is applied at higher levels or through inherited connection mechanisms.
The -inherited_supply option of the ams_cdef_net_cm command is supported only
when specified in the VCS optconfig file.
This enhancement ensures that supply resolution follows below priority order:
• Existing port based supply associations are used when present.
• Otherwise, supply values inherited from the design hierarchy are applied.
• Default supplies continue to serve as a fallback, preserving backward compatibility.
This improvement reduces the need for manual workarounds, simplifies connectivity in
large designs, and delivers more predictable analog‑digital conversion behavior without
impacting existing flows.

Command Syntax
The following is the updated command syntax of ams_cdef_net_cm:
ams_cdef_net_cm
-cell <connect_module_name>
[-lib <library_name | WORK>]
-cm_net { <net_name>* }
-default_supply {
{ snps_cm_power => <global_net> }
{ snps_cm_ground => <global_net> }
}
-inherited_supply {
<power_attribute_name> => <global_net>
}
• The -cell option defines a name of a cell or module to be used for scoping.
• The -lib option defines a name of a VCS logical compilation library to be used for
scoping. If this option is not specified, the default value WORK is used.
• The -cm_net option is comma-separated list of net names within a selected cell and
library combination.
• The -default_supply option defines a hierarchical name of the global net used to
establish a connection to a list of nets specified earlier.
• The snps_cm_power and snps_cm_ground arguments are reserved keywords that
designate electrical nets within the connect modules with assigned equivalent Verilog
(V2K) attributes.
• The -inherited_supply option associates a connect‑module power or ground
net with a power attribute, enabling the net to inherit its effective supply value via the
standard ams_cdef_inst -supply mechanism.
• The -inherited_supply option enables the connect module to:
◦ Use a port based supply override if present.
◦ Otherwise, inherit the supply value from an ams_cdef_inst -supply override that
applies to the connected hierarchy.
◦ If neither is available, fall back to the default supply.
• Use the -inherited_supply option when:
◦ Connect modules do not receive supply overrides through digital ports.
◦ Supply values are assigned using ams_cdef_inst -supply on parent instances.
◦ Consistent hierarchical supply propagation is required.

The ams_cdef_inst -supply override must be specified in the scope of the connect
module instance, the net connected to it, or at a higher hierarchical level.
Resolution Order
The following is the supply resolution precedence for a connect module instance:
1. Supply associated with connected digital ports (look-aside connectivity)
2. Inherited supply via power attribute override using ams_cdef_inst
3. Default supply specified using -default_supply in ams_cdef_net_cm

nets respectively using the ams_cdef_net_cm commands. Consequently, vddcm is
designated as the power net and vsscm as the ground net. These local supply nets are
used to model the digital-to-analog conversion within the connect module.

Support for User Accessible DRS
Support for User Accessible DRS
In order to model a Digital Mixed Signal (DMS) behavior with bidirectional ports, it is
mandatory to differentiate the “external drivers” from the “internal drivers” of a port. This
technology is referred a Driver/Receiver Segregation (DRS), which is default in Verilog-
AMS. The idea is the same as in the concept of DRS in Verilog AMS. DRS requires that
ordinary drivers and loads of a mixed signal be segregated through the digital in/out port
of a connect module. Ordinary drivers/loads, also called as external drivers/loads, are
drivers/loads outside the connect module. In contrast, connect drivers/loads, or the internal
drivers/loads are drivers/loads inside the connect module. DRS supports the following:
• All the connect loads will see the resolved value of the external drivers.
• All the external loads will see the resolved value of the connect drivers.
You must add a V2K attribute SNPS_ENABLE_DRS on a scalar wire/nettype port to enable
DRS on that port.
This provides an easy way for the user to enable DRS on a specific scalar wire or Nettype
in/out port.
The following is an example:
module l2r_bidir(l, e);
(*SNPS_ENABLE_DRS*) inout l; // enable DRS on this port
(*SNPS_ENABLE_DRS*) inout e; // enable DRS on this port

inout e;
wreal4state e;
parameter real Threshold =1.65;

reg e2l_val = 1'bz;
real l2e_val = `wrealZState;

always @(l)
l2e_val = (l === 1'bz) ? `wrealZState :
(l === 1'bx) ? `wrealXState :
l * 2.0 * Threshold;

UPF Support for SPICE-on-Top Design Configurations

always @(e)
e2l_val = (e === `wrealZState) ? 1'bz :
(e === `wrealXState) ? 1'bx :
(e > Threshold ) ? 1 :
0;
1. You can only add the attribute SNPS_ENABLE_DRS on a scalar wire or nettype inout port
of a module that is not a connect module.
2. Embedded DRS is not allowed, that is, you cannot have the attribute
SNPS_ENABLE_DRS on two hierarchically connect port nodes one of which is an
ancestor of the other.
3. You cannot connect a bidirectional switch gate or a spice instance to a port with the
attribute SNPS_ENABLE_DRS hierarchically.
UPF Support for SPICE-on-Top Design Configurations
In SPICE-on-top design topologies, the top level of a design is modeled in analog
languages (such as Spice/Spectre). Digital blocks are instantiated under the Spice. In
Spice, the supplies are typically created in the subckt definition only, while supply network
for digital blocks is present in the UPF file. In such a design configuration, the supply may
be generated from Spice which may then be connected to the UPF supply network to
propagate supplies to digital blocks of the design.
The following commands are used to set the connectivity between the external driver and
the UPF supply net:
upf_port_connect
Syntax:
upf_port_connect -cell <Cell_name> -inst<inst_name> (<upf_port> =>
<spice_port>) ;
upf_port_connect -cell TopDig
-inst X1 (VDDL=>vdd12);
upf_port_map

Globally Merged Auto-Inserted-Connect Module (AICM) Optimization
When the ports do not match by name to the UPF created supply ports, then the
recommendation is to use the following upf_port_map option:

Globally Merged Auto-Inserted-Connect Module (AICM)
Optimization
In the Verilog-AMS flow, the interfaces between analog and digital blocks are realized by
the automatic insertion of connect modules. These insertions are guided by Verilog-AMS
connect-insertion statements. A single connect module instance may be inserted between
a net and a set of ports (where the net was originally connected to) if the connect-mode of
the corresponding connect-insertion statement is specified as ‘merged’.

Globally Merged Auto-Inserted-Connect Module (AICM) Optimization
Besides, merged mode insertion takes place only when the net and the set of mixed-signal
port connections are in the same module. If there is another mixed-signal port connection
that is in a different module, then the same connect module instance is not shared with
the other port connection as well although the high-conn of the other port connection is
hierarchically connected to the same net.
This feature extends the merged mode connect module insertion across multiple mixed-
signal port connections that may be present in different modules when the high-conn of
these port connections are all hierarchically connected to the same net.
Merged Mode Connect Module Insertion as Per Verilog-AMS LRM
As per Verilog-AMS LRM, a single connect module is inserted between a high-conn net
and a set of mixed-signal port connections if the ‘merged’ insertion mode is specified in the
respective connect-insertion statement.

Support for the Bind Feature in Mixed-Signal Simulation
Support for the Bind Feature in Mixed-Signal Simulation
In the Eldo SPICE netlist format, the .bind command is used to map a sub-circuit with
another sub-circuit. VCS supports this command in the Mixed Signal Verification (MSV)
flow as well.
The syntax of the .bind command is as follows:
.bind inst=< full_instance_name> from_subckt=< subckt_name>
to_subckt=<subckt_name> default_mapping=< mapping_method>
The command options are:
• inst: Specifies the full name of the instance thats needs sub-circuit definition
replacement. Wildcard is not supported.
from_subckt: Specifies the original sub-circuit definition.
to_subckt: Specifies the new sub-circuit definition that is used to replace the sub-
circuit given in from_subckt.
default_mapping: Specifies the mapping method. Only the BY_POSITION method is
supported. The BY_NAME method is not supported
• When using the command, check if the node names of the replacement sub-
circuit and the original sub-circuit match.
• VCS reports an error and stops the simulation if there is a mismatch in node
names or count.
System Functions to Access Analog Voltage and Port Current
Mixed-signal simulation supports different techniques for accessing analog signals within a
mixed analog-digital design:
• Verilog language cross module referencing (XMR)
• $hdl_xmr_force and $hdl_xmr_release in Verilog, and hdl_xmr_force and
hdl_xmr_release in VHDL
• $snps_get_volt and $snps_get_port_current Verilog system functions
• UCLI get command

System Functions to Access Analog Voltage and Port Current
VCS supports three system functions, $msv_is_analog_node, $msv_get_voltage, and
$msv_get_current, for accessing analog voltage and current values from analog nodes
within a mixed-signal simulation. These system functions have more benefits over the
other AMS XMR solutions listed above.
For example, you can use a string variable as an argument for the path to the probed
node, which you cannot do in the $snps_* functions. Similarly, the $msv_get_voltage
and $msv_get_current system functions return a real number value that represents the
voltage or current, unlike the $hdl_xmr commands.
Prerequisite
To use the $msv_is_analog_node, $msv_get_voltage, and $msv_get_current system
functions, specify the -lca option while running VCS.
The syntax of the $msv_is_analog_node, $msv_get_voltage, and $msv_get_current
system functions is as follows:
Syntax Description
$msv_is_analog_node ( node_path) Returns 1 if node_path points to an analog node
(electrical, branch, SPICE node, and so on).
Otherwise, returns 0.
$msv_get_voltage ( node_path) Returns the voltage for an analog node as a real
value. If node_path is not an analog node, the
system function generates the following error
message and returns 0.0.
Error: failed to find analog object
'node_path' in top-level scope
$msv_get_current ( node_path) Returns the current for an analog node as a real
value. If node_path is not an analog node, the

VCS supports supply routing via Verilog-AMS netlist through inherited connection and
associates this supply with the connect module instances and the SPICE or Verilog-AMS
blocks that need this information for simulation purposes. However, in several Verilog-AMS
designs, attribute-based syntax, embedded into the RTL source is used to achieve the

Supply Sensitivity and Ground Sensitivity for a Connect Module
A connect module is used to convert between analog and digital values at an analog/
digital boundary. For analog to digital conversion, it typically depends on some threshold
value that in turn usually depends on the power-supply of the analog signal. On the other
hand, for digital to analog conversion, a logic value (‘0’ or ‘1’) typically translates to an
analog value depending upon the power-supply of the digital signal.

Attribute-Based Inherited Connection and Supply Sensitivity
connectmodule l2e (din, aout);
input din;
logical din;
output aout;
electrical aout;
(* snps_cm_power = "global_module.vdd" *) electrical vdd;
(* snps_cm_ground = "global_module.vss" *) electrical vss;
In the above example, two local nodes vdd and vss within connect module 12e have
power and ground information. Node vdd is supply-sensitive because it has the
snps_cm_power attribute. On the other hand, vss is the ground-sensitive node because
it has the snps_cm_ground attribute. These supply nodes (vdd and vss) may be used to
model the analog to digital or digital to analog conversions accurately.
Supply Sensitivity and Ground Sensitivity for an Ordinary Module
The snps_ams_supply_digital_port_power and
snps_ams_supply_digital_port_ground attributes can be specified on the digital ports
of an ordinary module, and these attributes can override the value of the corresponding
snps_cm_power and snps_cm_ground attributes within a connect module.
module bot (p1, p2);
(* snps_ams_supply_digital_port_power = "global_module.vddBot";
snps_ams_supply_digital_port_ground = "global_module.vssBot" *)
input p1;
In the above example, the snps_ams_supply_digital_port_power and
snps_ams_supply_digital_port_ground attributes have been provided on the
digital port p1 of the ordinary module bot. If a connect module is connected to this
port p1, then global_module.vddBot overrides the snps_cm_power attribute and
global_module.vssBot overrides the snps_cm_ground attribute of this connect module.
You can achieve the same functionality by using the ams_supply command as follows:
File: vcsAD.init
ams_supply -cell bot -digital_port {p1} -supply
{port_power=>global_module.vddBot, port_ground=>global_module.vssBot}
Inherited Connection
An inherited connection is a combination of ‘property-name’ and ‘default-property-value’. It
can be defined on a local electrical node inside an ordinary module or a connect module.
Once defined, this local node is bound to that ‘property-name’ and has the corresponding
‘default-property-value’ unless there is an instance-level override for that ‘property-name’
as explained in the following sections.

(* snps_ams_cdef_net_property_name = "mygnd";
snps_ams_cdef_net_default_value = "global_module.vssBot" *)
electrical vssLocal;
In the above example, vddLocal and vssLocal are two local electrical nodes inside the
ordinary module bot. Here, vddLocal and vssLocal are bound to the property-names
mypwr and mygnd, respectively. The snps_ams_supply_digital_port_power attribute on
port p1 points to node vddLocal, whereas the snps_ams_supply_digital_port_ground
attribute on port p1 refers to vssLocal.
The above diagram shows that through the combination of inherited-connection-property
mypwr + snps_ams_supply_digital_port_power attribute, the supply of port p1 is
connected to global_module.vddBot.
Similarly, it also shows that through the combination of inherited-connection-property
mygnd + snps_ams_supply_digital_port_ground attribute, the ground of port p1 is
connected to global_module.vssBot.
You can achieve the same functionality with the ams_supply and ams_cdef_net
commands as follows:
File: vcsAD.init
ams_supply -cell bot -digital_port {p1} -supply {port_power=>vddLocal,
port_ground=>vssLocal}
ams_cdef_net -cell bot -net {vddLocal} -default_supply
{mypwr=>global_module.vddBot}
ams_cdef_net -cell bot -net {vssLocal} -default_supply
{mygnd=>global_module.vssBot}

(* snps_ams_cdef_inst = {"gnd:mygnd"};
gnd = "global_module.vss1" *) BOT (w1, w2);

In the above example, inherited-connection properties mypwr and gnd on instance
MID1 are specified here: snps_ams_cdef_inst = {"mypwr", "gnd"} . Inherited-
connection property gnd on instance BOT is overridden here: snps_ams_cdef_inst =
{"gnd:mygnd"}. Here, gnd is also renamed to mygnd.
You can achieve the same functionality with the ams_supply, ams_cdef_net, and
ams_cdef_inst commands as follows:
File: vcsAD.init
ams_supply -cell bot -digital_port {p1} -supply {port_power=>vddLocal,
port_ground=>vssLocal}
ams_cdef_net -cell bot -net {vddLocal} -default_supply
{mypwr=>global_module.vddBot}

Support for Packed Type of Wreal/Nettype/Real/Integer
ams_cdef_net -cell bot -net {vssLocal} -default_supply
{mygnd=>global_module.vssBot}
ams_cdef_inst -cell top -inst {MID1} -supply {gnd=>global_module.vss,
mypwr=>global_module.vdd}
ams_cdef_inst -cell mid -inst {BOT} -supply
{gnd:mygnd=>global_module.vss1}
You must use the following compile-time option to enable this feature:
%vcs -adopt ams_cdef_attrib
For more information about the ams_supply, ams_cdef_net, and ams_cdef_inst
commands, refer to the Inherited-Connection-Based Supply Specification for Verilog-AMS
Designs section in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Support for Packed Type of Wreal/Nettype/Real/Integer
In Verilog-AMS, the packed vector of nettype/wreal/real/integer is used frequently. Support
for a packed vector of these types is required to compile and simulate generated netlist.
These types are inherently unpacked in nature, so you must convert the packed vector of
these types to the unpacked array internally.
VCS AMS supports packed vector of nettype (both built-in and user-defined) using the
-xlrm nettype_array XLRM option.
Two-Step Flow
vcs -sverilog -xlrm nettype_array
Three-Step Flow
vlogan -sverilog -xlrm nettype_array
The following coding styles are supported with the -xlrm nettype_array option:
• wreal [3:0] a;
• th_wire[3:0] b;
• int [3:0] c;
• real [3:0] d;

Configuring the Converters Through ams_cm Command
The -xlrm nettype_array option only enables support for packed arrays of
the listed constructs. It does not enable support for the constructs themselves.
Data types int and real are built-in data types of SystemVerilog, whereas
wreal and th_wire are not. You can enable wreal net support (see the
“Support for Wreal Nets” section in the VCS User Guide) , however, it is
recommended to use native SystemVerilog user-defined nettypes instead of
wreal nets. Commonly used SystemVerilog user-defined nettypes, including
th_wire, are available in the following Synopsys MSV package:
$VCS_HOME/etc/snps_msv/snps_msv_nettype_pkg.svp
Configuring the Converters Through ams_cm Command
The ams_cm command enables parameter overrides of the datatype converters used in
analog mixed-signal designs and digital mixed-signal designs.
To fine-tune the accuracy of type conversions, it is allowed to override the parameters of a
set of auto-inserted converter instances in the design. Refer to the following figure:
Figure 66 Overriding the Parameters of a Set of Auto-inserted Converter

Configuring the Converters Through ams_cm Command
ams_cm converter_module_parameter_name=parameter_value
[library=library_name]
[cell=cell_name [node=node_name]]
[inst=instance_hierarchical_name [node=node_name]]
[node=node_hierarchical_name];
converter_module_parameter_name=parameter_value
Specifies the converter module parameter and the value to which it is set. The
parameter_value can be either real or string type. If you specify override information for a
nonexistent parameter of a converter module, then that override is ignored.
library=library_name
Specifies the name of the logical library of the cell for which the converter module is
inserted.
cell=cell_name [node=node_name]
Specifies the cell or cell/node names for which the converter module is inserted or
connected. The node name is optional; if it is not specified, all nodes of a given cell are
considered.
inst=instance_hierarchical_name [node=node_name]
Specifies the hierarchical instance name or hierarchical-instance-name/node names for
which the converter module is inserted or connected. The node name is optional; if it is not
specified, all nodes of a given instance are considered.
node=node_hierarchical_name
Specifies the hierarchical node name for which the converter module is inserted or
connected
There is no change in the existing use model for RNM simulation. To specify the ams_cm
option on the ports, use the -adopt port_based_ams_cm command.

Configuring the Converters Through ams_cm Command
• The ams_cm option in the VCS optconfig file allows you to override converter
parameters only.
• VerilogAMS flow:
◦ The ams_cm commands in the VCS optconfig file are applicable to converter
instances only (these are not applicable to any connectmodule instance).
◦ The ams_cm commands in the vcsAD.init file continue to configure the
connectmodule instances only.
The following is an exampl

module LevelShifter ( input wreal4state wr_21, output wreal4state wr_35);
//… … …
The commands used are:
vlogan -sverilog converter.v test.v
vcs top -sverilog -wreal res_def -xlrm enable_converter
+optconfigfile+cfg
./simv
The ams_cm commands in the VCS optconfig file allow you to override the converter
parameters only:
• Overriding converter insertion rule is not supported.
• Overriding converter insertion mode (merge/split) is not supported.
• SuperNet is not supported.
• Arguments of the ams_cm command do not support wildcard notation.

Parameterization of Converters Using Hierarchical Tracing
Parameterization of Converters Using Hierarchical Tracing
In Real Number Modeling (RNM) simulation, converters are inserted at port boundaries
where the port type differs from the connected signal type. Configuring these converters
requires users to specify ams_cm commands in the VCS OptConfig file. However,
the current approach only looks upward in the hierarchy to identify applicable ams_cm
commands. This limitation can lead to errors in multi-voltage designs or designs with
complex hierarchical connections.
The enhanced hierarchical tracing feature addresses this limitation by enabling a tracing
algorithm that not only looks upward for the applicable ams_cm command, but also checks
the interconnected segments in the adjacent hierarchies to handle the feedthrough
scenarios.
This feature is applicable to:
• Digital portion of the design and does not trace through analog or Unified Power
Format (UPF) portions.
• Coercion flow under the -coerce switch.
To enable traversal algorithm, add the following command to the OptConfig file:
ams_converter_parameterization=traversal;
By default, the value is set to upscoping, which uses the upward-only tracing method.
After enabling traversal algorithm, use any of the following syntaxes to define the ams_cm
command:
ams_cm inst=<hier_inst_name> node=<node_name>;
Or,
ams_cm node=<hier_node_name>;
If the ams_cm command is defined as {cell=<cell_name> node=<node>} along with
inst=<inst_name> node=<node>} or {node=<hier_node>} then inst-node/node path
takes precedence.
The following is the limitation of this feature:
• Bit-specific ams_cm commands are not supported.

Donut Configuration Support in RTVS
Donut Configuration Support in RTVS
The Real-Time-View-Swapping (RTVS) feature enables you to dynamically switch
between SPICE and Verilog views of a cell at runtime as the simulation progresses. You
can get high simulation accuracy by selecting the SPICE view for certain time windows.
For other time periods, its Verilog view is simulated to get high simulation performance.
This feature extends the RTVS feature by supporting instantiations of SPICE sub-circuit
under the RTVS Verilog view and Verilog module under the RTVS SPICE view.

Dependency on Verdi
This feature has the following dependencies on Verdi:

Dumping of Attributes Not Understood by VCS
Dumping of Attributes Not Understood by VCS
In previous releases, VCS did not understand some of the netlisted modules written in
Verilog-AMS or SystemVerilog languages that have attributes defined with a syntax that is
not compliant with Verilog-AMS or SystemVerilog LRM.
Starting with this release, VCS performs the following:
• Reports all the attributes that are not understood by VCS in a text file, and ignores
them during compilation. VCS also generates warning messages for every occurrence
of the attribute that are not understood by VCS.
• Supports execution of a general-purpose pre-elaboration user script.
• Reads the commands generated by the user-defined script before mixed-signal
elaboration.
To enable this feature, do the following:
Two-Step Flow
1. Use the -lca option.
2. Use the ams_xlrm_netlist command in the optconfigfile file.
Three-Step Flow
1. Use the -lca option.
2. Use the ams_xlrm_netlist command in the optconfigfile file.
3. Use the vlogan -xlrm ams option to enable vlogan to parse unknown attributes.
The syntax of the ams_xlrm_netlist command is as follows:
ams_xlrm_netlist
-constructs attributes
[ -warning_file_format txt ] ;
-constructs attributes
Specifies type of constructs not supported by VCS that require a dedicated warnings file.
attributes constructs are covered by this specification.
-warning_file_format txt
Specifies the format of the VCS-generated warnings file.

Dumping of Attributes Not Understood by VCS
If an option is not specified, txt is the default value of the option. If an option is
specified, it must have a value.
Return Value
When VCS encounters unknown attributes, it generates a message in the log file as
Note-[MSV-XLRM-ATTR-SYNTAX] Attribute not understood by VCS
Attribute syntaxes have been found in the netlist those are not
understood by VCS.
Please see file simv.daidir/.snps_ams_xlrm_netlist.warn.txt for more
details.
Usage Examples
ams_xlrm_netlist -constructs attributes -warning_file_format txt;
This is an example of the full command.
ams_xlrm_netlist -constructs attributes;
This is an example of the minimalistic command that covers most of the use cases.
File Format Used to Dump XLRM Information
VCS dumps the attributes that it does not understand and the relevant warnings in a text
file.
simv.daidir/.snps_ams_xlrm_netlist.warn.txt
This file is created only when the attributes not understood by VCS are detected.
The warning information includes the following:
• <num>
• <file_name>
• <line_num>
• <instance_name>
• <module_type>
• <module_name>
• <node_name>

Dumping of Attributes Not Understood by VCS
• <library_name>
• <new_constructs_as_seen_in_the_netlist>
The following example shows a VCS-generated warnings file.
Example 107 simv.daidir/.snps_ams_xlrm_netlist.warn.txt
<num>:
WARNING: Following unknown attributes have been found in file <file_name>
at line <line_num> on instance <instance_name> in <module_type>
<module_name> from library <library_name>. These attributes have been
ignored.
Attributes: <new_constructs_as_seen_in_the_netlist>

<num>:
WARNING: Following unknown attribute has been found in file <file_name>
at line <line_num> on node <node_name> in <module_type> <module_name>
from library <library_name>. This attribute has been ignored.
Attribute: <new_constructs_as_seen_in_the_netlist>
Pre-Elaboration Script
VCS supports an execution of a general-purpose pre-elaboration script that users provide.
The script is invoked after source files compilation and before AMS elaboration. It is
invoked by the pre_elaboration_script command in the optconfigfile file when the
-ams option is used in VCS.
The pre_elaboration_script command is operational only when the
ams_xlrm_netlist command is run and unknown attributes are detected in the netlist.
The syntax of the pre_elaboration_script command is as follows:
pre_elaboration_script
-file relative_path_to_script
[ -abort_compilation_after_script_execution < yes | no > ] ;
-file relative_path_to_script
Specifies a relative path to an executable user script.
-abort_compilation_after_script_execution yes
VCS compilation stops when the execution of the user script is complete. This is used only
for debugging purposes.
-abort_compilation_after_script_execution no
VCS compilation continues when the execution of the user script is complete.

Support for Multiplicity Factor Parameter
If an option is not specified, no is the default value of the

, this option forces a resolved value of an
M-factor to be written into a local parameter parameter_name of datatype real within a
selected cell. It is illegal to use this option with the -local_inst key.
-local_inst {{ name_of_a_local_instance }* }
Scoping option to define a target instance within the selected cell.
-param_override parameter_name
This option enables VCS to take a value specified in an existing Verilog-AMS parameter
override statement and use it as an M-factor for a given instance.
The parameter override statement can be declared on an instance even if no such
parameter is declared within the module. You cannot specify this option without specifying
the -local_inst key.
-value value
Specifies a value of the M-factor for the selected object. If -param_override is also
specified, its value is substituted with -value value.
Return Value
Incorrect commands are reported in the VCS log file.
ams_mfactor -lib "libA" -cell "LDO" -value 15;
ams_mfactor -lib "libA" -cell {"LDO","DCDC"} -value 15;
ams_mfactor -lib "libA" -cell {"LDO","DCDC"} -param_resolved
"mfactor_eff";
ams_mfactor -lib "libA" -cell "LDO" -local_inst {"I1","I2"} -value 15;
ams_mfactor -lib "libA" -cell "LDO" -local_inst {"I1","I2"}
-param_override "multi";
In the above example,
ams_mfactor -lib "libA" -cell "LDO" -value 15 defines an M-factor 15 for all
instance within cell LDO.
ams_mfactor -lib "libA" -cell {"LDO","DCDC"} -value 15; defines an M-factor
15 for all instance within cells LDO and DCDC.
ams_mfactor -lib "libA" -cell {"LDO","DCDC"} -param_resolved
"mfactor_eff"; defines the parameter mfacto_eff of cells LDO and DCDC to be forced to
a value of an effective M-factor value in those scopes.
ams_mfactor -lib "libA" -cell "LDO" -local_inst {"I1","I2"} -value 15;
defines an M-factor 15 for instances I1 and I2 within cell LDO of library libA.

Support for Multiplicity Factor Parameter
ams_mfactor -lib "libA" -cell "LDO" -local_inst {"I1","I2"}
-param_override "multi"; defines an M-factor instance level override as a reference to
a parameter override statement located (assumed to be located) at instances I1 and I2 of
cell LDO.
V2K Alternative to ams_mfactor
Define the following two equivalent attributes (that are supposed to be defined in Verilog-
AMS or SystemVerilog netlist) to enable embedding such attributes in the netlist.
• (* snps_ams_mfactor_override = 10 *) is used to define an M-factor value of an
instance.
• (* snps_ams_mfactor_resolved *) is used to define a parameter of datatype real to
be used a storage of a resolved hierarchical M-factor value.
To get access to the value of the attribute for debugging purposes, you must use an
$mfactor function.
Example 108 Verilog-AMS module
(* snps_ams_mfactor_override = 10 *) test_mfactor I1(a,c);
(* snps_ams_mfactor_override = 2 *) test_mfactor I2(a,c);

module test_mfactor(a, c);
parameter real m=0.1;
real rs;

analog begin
rs = $mfactor * 100.0;
$strobe ("m = %g, $mfactor = %g, rs = %g", m, $mfactor, rs);
end

The following are the limitations of the name mapping between SPICE view and digital
view for XMR feature:
• Supports only XMRs written in RTL/HDL files. The XMRs specified on the UCLI
command prompt, Verdi windows, or other interfaces are not handled.
• Designed exclusively for RTVS flows and does not extend to general MSV flows.
• Extends support only to name mapping based on X-prefix, case sensitivity, port map, or
bus format of the original XMR.
Automatic Handling of Verilog Force on Mixed-Signal Nets
The force statement in SystemVerilog is a continuous procedural assignment on a net.
When you apply a force statement to a net, it overrides all other drivers to that net.
In simulation, a force statement is used in conjunction with a release statement. The
release statement ends the driver override that was applied on the net through the force
statement.
The behavior of Verilog force/release on a mixed-signal net is now enhanced such that the
Verilog force becomes the only driver for the Spice net. That is, in case of a Verilog force,
the force value is sent to the analog side, and the analog engine considers it as the only
contribution to the respective Spice net. This force value is maintained on the Spice net
until a Verilog release happens on that mixed-signal net.
With this enhancement, a force command is applied the same way as in Verilog, by fully
overriding other analog drivers. When a force is applied to a digital segment of a mixed-
signal net, this information is passed to the analog side to ‘force’ an analog segment of the
net. This tracing also works in the backward (a -> d) direction.
To enable this feature, you must use the -adopt msv_force_release compile option.
The following examples describe this feature in detail:
• Verilog Force on a Spice Net
• Verilog Force on a Digital Net Connected to Spice
• Verilog Force on a Digital Net Connected to Spice Through Select

Leaf-Level Verilog-AMS Support in the SystemVerilog-Spice Flow
Leaf-Level Verilog-AMS Support in the SystemVerilog-Spice Flow
VCS MSV supports SystemVerilog-Spice flow having a leaf-level Verilog-AMS
(VAMS) module to be used as an electrical instrument. You must use the -adopt
msv_with_leaf_vams compile option to enable the leaf-level Verilog-AMS support. This
feature only supports VAMS block at the leaf level of the hierarchy in the SV-Spice flow.

Leaf-Level Verilog-AMS Support in the SystemVerilog-Spice Flow
Figure 67 Leaf-Level Verilog-AMS Support
This feature allows leaf-level VAMS source files to be used as electrical instruments. A
leaf-level VAMS does not allow any hierarchy or analog primitives.
The following is the use model of leaf-level Verilog-AMS support in VCS two-step and
three-step flows:
Two-step flow:
% vcs +verilogamsext+.vams test.vams -sverilog test.v -adopt
msv_with_leaf_vams -ad=test.init
Three-step flow:
% vlogan -sverilog test.v
% vlogan -ams test.vams
% vcs -ad=test.init -sverilog top -adopt msv_with_leaf_vams
Consider the following files:
test.sv
reg in , out ;
initial in =0 ;

test.vams
`include "disciplines.vams"
module ana (in , out);
input in ;
output out;
electrical in , out ;
analog begin
V(out) <+ V(in) ;
end
test.init
choose xa ;
Execute the following commands:
% vcs +verilogamsext+.vams test.vams -sverilog test.sv -adopt
msv_with_leaf_vams -ad=test.init -full64

Bidirectional-Island
Bidirectional-island for an INOUT port is identified by the complete set of net segments
that are directly or indirectly connected to the port signal through port-connections and
aliases.
For example, in the following figure, there are two bidirectional-islands: Bidir-Island
#1 and Bidir-Island #2 . Both bidirectional-islands contain three different types of
interconnected net segments: wire, wrealmin, and wrealmax.
Figure 68 Multi-Voltage Design
Most Accurate Representative Type
Consider a design with a set of net segments interconnected by INOUT ports and aliases.
Let the types of these segments are NT1, NT2, …, NTn and are different from each other.
Out of these n different types, if the NTx type is most accurate, then NTx is considered as
the Most Accurate Representative (MAR) type.
Bidirectional-Island Processing: Super-Net Formation
In a bidirectional-island, all net segments of the same type are aliased to form one single
net for that respective type.
The following figure is an example of super-net formation for a bidirectional-island.

Figure 69 Super-Net Formation for a Bidirectional-Island
The bidirectional-island in Figure 69 contains three different net types: NT1, NT2, and NT3.
• NT1: This net type has two segments. These two segments are aliased to form a single
net of type NT1.
• NT2: This net type has two segments. These two segments are aliased to form a single
net of type NT2.
• NT3: This type has only one segment.
In Figure 69, after aliasing there are three nets in the bidirectional-island (one net for each
type). Also, two net segments, connected through INOUT ports having different types, are
disconnected from each other. This is shown as Disconnection-1, Disconnection-2,
and so on in Figure 69.
After MAR information is available for a bidirectional-island, the Super-Net can be formed
for this island. If NT3 is the MAR in this example, the Super-Net contains the following
unidirectional converters (unidirectional converters from each non-MAR to MAR, and vice
versa):
• Non-MAR to MAR ( NT1_to_NT3 and NT3_to_NT1)
• MAR to Non-MAR ( NT2_to_NT3 and NT3_to_NT2)

Scope-Based Type-Coercion Use Cases
The scope-based type-coercion is implemented in the following use cases:
Refer to the following example to understand these uses cases.
Use Case 1: Additive Nature of ams_coercion Commands
ams_coercion -mode ON -inst { top.mid1 };
ams_coercion -mode ON -inst { top.mid2 };
The two commands are equivalent to the following single command:
ams_coercion -mode ON -inst { top.mid1, top.mid2 };
Use Case 2: Transitive Nature of ams_coercion Command
ams_coercion -mode OFF -inst { top.mid1 };
Type-coercion is turned OFF for the instance top.mid1 and the hierarchy below.
Use Case 3: Lower-Level ams_coercion Command Overrides the Command From its
Upper Level
ams_coercion -mode OFF -cell mid;
ams_coercion -mode ON -cell bot;
ams_coercion -mode ON -inst { top.mid1.leaf1 };
The first command disables type-coercion for all instances of the mid cell and its sub-
hierarchy, except for the following two scenarios:
• When the second command enables type-coercion for all instances of the bot cell
( top.mid1.bot1 and top.mid2.bot1), thereby overriding the higher level first
command for this particular scope.
• When the third command enables type-coercion specifically for the instance
top.mid1.leaf1, thereby overriding the higher level first command for this particular
scope.
Use Case 4: Instance Level Commands Take Priority Over Cell Level Commands

ams_coercion -mode OFF -cell mid;
ams_coercion -mode ON -inst { top.mid1 };
The first command disables type-coercion for all instances of the mid cell and their sub-
hierarchy.
The second command explicitly enables type-coercion for the instance top.mid1,
overriding the cell level command.
Use Case 5: Conflicting ams_coercion Commands
ams_coercion -mode ON -cell mid_mod;
ams_coercion -mode OFF -cell mid_mod;///Error
A conflict arises when contradictory commands are issued for the same cell. In this case,
an error is generated to prevent ambiguity.
Use Case 6: Usage of the -override Option
• Scenario 1: Instance Level -override Command
ams_coercion -mode OFF -cell leaf;
ams_coercion -mode ON -inst { top.mid1 } -override;
The second command overrides the first, enabling type-coercion for the top.mid1
hierarchy, including instances of the leaf cell within it (for example, top.mid1.leaf1).
However, type-coercion remains disabled for other instances of the leaf cell (For
example, top.mid2.leaf1)

Optimizing Verilog-AMS Auto-Inserted ConnectModules (AICMs)
Using Built-in Interface Elements
In mixed-signal designs, connectmodules (also called Interface Elements or IEs) convert
signals between different disciplines—for example, from a digital logic value to an analog
electrical value (voltage/current) and vice versa. These conversions are guided by the
Verilog-AMS (VAMS) Language Reference Manual (LRM) connect-insertion rules.
In the VCS VAMS flow, interfaces between analog and digital blocks are realized by
automatically inserting connectmodules during the elaboration phase. VCS detects
mismatched ports on the same node and inserts the appropriate ConnectModule(CM)
based on connect rules.

Connectmodules can be inserted in:
• Merged Mode (default): If a single net of one discipline (for example, analog) connects
to multiple ports of another discipline (for example, digital), VCS inserts only one
instance of the connectmodule. All destination ports share the converted signal from
this single instance.
• Split Mode: Each mismatched port gets its own connectmodule instance. This mode is
less common and generally less efficient.

VCS supports optimization of the VAMS auto-inserted connectmodule instances using
built-in interface elements. You can use the -adopt aicm_opt_ie compile option as
follows to enable this feature. This feature improves the simulation performance of the
VAMS designs.
% vlogan -full64 -ams test.vams -sverilog
% vcs -full64 top -sverilog -ams \
-ad=test.init \
-adopt aicm_opt_ie \
-ams_discipline logical \
-ams_iereport
The following sections describe this feature in detail:
• Properties of Synopsys Built-in Interface Elements
• Optimization Criteria
• Analog Island Optimization
Properties of Synopsys Built-in Interface Elements
The following are the properties of the Synopsys built-in interface element:
• Managed by VCS/PrimeSim
• Support only built-in digital data types
• Independent of Verilog-AMS discipline definitions
• Faster execution and smaller memory footprint compared to VAMS connectmodules
• Inserted in Merged mode only to maximize performance
• Conversion functionality is controlled via:
◦ The ie and resistance-map commands in the vcsAD.init file.
◦ Automatic VDD tracing managed by VCS.
• Driver Receiver Segregation (DRS) happens at the digital port of a connectmodule
to segregate connect-driver from connect-receiver. Bi-directional (inout) built-in IEs
support DRS functionality (that is, analog simulator determines the final value of the
mixed-signal net).

Optimization Criteria
The following criteria must be met to optimize VAMS connectmodule instances using built-
in interface elements:
• The analog-digital boundary data type must be supported by the interface element.
• CM insertion mode must be merged, not split.
• CM instance must be auto-inserted (not manual).
• Mutual Exclusion Rules:
◦ A net cannot have both an IE and a CM. A mixed-signal can either have a
connectmodule or interface element, not both.
◦ If any connection on a mixed-signal net fails the criteria, optimization does not occur
for that net.

Dynamic Reconfiguration at Runtime
As designs grow in size, memory consumption and simulation speed become crucial
factors in design verification. In general, tests and stimulus are targeted and generated for
specific parts of a design. These tests and stimulus exercise a large portion of the design
while the rest of the design becomes inactive during simulation. Dynamic reconfiguration
at runtime provides a flexible mechanism to substitute portions of a design hierarchy with
empty models at runtime. This feature enables different design configurations to be used
for simulations without recompiling the design.

In Figure 76, instances U2, U4, and U5 are inactive during the simulation. These instances
and their sub-hierarchies are replaced by an empty module at runtime.
The dynamic reconfiguration at runtime feature is described in the following sections:
• Support with VCS Native Low Power
• Dynamic Reconfiguration in a Mixed Signal Flow
• Support for Cross-Module References of Multidimensional Arrays
• Restrictions
This section describes the use model for dynamic reconfiguration. It provides the steps
to specify an alternate module that is instantiated in place of the original sub-hierarchy.

This ensures that designs do not reach an unknown state when you replace portions of the
hierarchy at runtime.
1. Compile-time
At compile time, specify the list of modules that has the potential of not being
elaborated at runtime. In addition, for each such module, provide an alternate module,
which gets bound if an instance is not elaborated. This alternate module must be
provided during the design compilation phase. During compilation, these alternate
modules are treated as top-level modules by VCS because they are not explicitly
instantiated in the design.
In this document, the module that can be deleted is referred to as the “original module”.
The alternate module is referred to as the “substitute module”.
To specify the original module and the substitute module, the configuration file
mechanism in VCS is enhanced with the following entry.
replace module {<original module>} with module {<substitute module>};
Configuration files can be specified to VCS with the +optconfigfile
+<config file name> arguments.
2. Runtime
At runtime, specify the actual instance paths that should not be elaborated by VCS
during runtime simulation. The hierarchical path names should be specified in a file.
The path of the file path can be provided to simv using the following option:
-dynaconfig <file name>
Replacing a Module Instance
This runtime configuration file specifies the hierarchical names of the module instances
t

module test(input bit bm,logic lm,output bit bto,logic lto);
M

bit bt,bto,bt1;
logic lt,lto,lt1;
M
test test_inst( .bm(bt),.lm(lt),.bto(bto),.lto(lto));
test test_inst1( .bm(bt1),.lm(lt1),.bto(bto1),.lto(lto1));
M

module test_sbst(input bit bm,logic lm,
output bit bto,logic lto);

top

The compile-time configuration file lists the modules whose instances you might replace
along with their corresponding substitute modules.
In this test case, the compile-time configuration file is named as config.txt:
//config.txt

replace module {test} with module {test_sbst};
This configuration file specifies the possible replacement of an instance of module test
with an instance of module test_sbst.
The compile-time command-line is as follows:
% vcs basic.v +optconfigfile+config.txt

Support with VCS Native Low Power
VCS displays the following information message from dynamic reconfiguration:
DYNAMIC RECONFIG> Replacing test With test_sbst Enabled
You have enabled replacing instances of module test with instances of module
test_sbst at runtime.
So at runtime, you must first write another configuration file specifying, by hierarchical
name, the module instances you want to replace. In this test case, the configuration file is
named as runconfig.txt:
//runconfig.txt

top.test_inst
This configuration file specifies that you want the module instance with the hierarchical
name top.test_inst to be replaced. The other instance of module test, with the
hierarchical name top.test_inst1, is not replaced.

Support with VCS Native Low Power
During the design compilation phase, you must provide both the original and substitute
alternate module source files along with the configuration file, and specify the UPF file
using the -upf option, as shown below:
% vcs +optconfigfile+ compile_config_file_name \
top_module_of_design.v \

Dynamic Reconfiguration in a Mixed Signal Flow
original_module.v substitute_module.v \
-upf original_module.upf
With respect to the VCS Native Low Power (NLP), the following simulation behavior
applies:
• Power-down semantics: Power-down corruption would be instrumented for both the
original and substitute modules. Though the power-down corruption instrumentation is
done for substitute modules, you must not see any corruption behavior at runtime.
• Isolation semantics: Isolation would not get instrumented for the substitute modules
except when you specify the isolation as parent or fanout. You must not observe any
isolation on the ports/pins of the substituted modules except when the isolation location
is parent or fanout.
• Retention semantics: No retention would be instrumented for the substitute modules.
You must not observe any registers being retained in the substituted module.
The following restrictions apply if you use dynamic reconfiguration flow with VCS NLP:
• Though the substituted modules are simulated without Low power semantics, still
runtime low power messages related to the power domain are generated.
• If power domain related control signals like switch, isolation control are present in the
original module and got replaced with the substitute module, then all those control
signals gets “Z” value, and related runtime low power messages are generated
accordingly.
Dynamic Reconfiguration in a Mixed Signal Flow
You can use dynamic reconfiguration in a mixed signal verification, but only if the analog
(SPICE or Verilog-A) part of the mixed signal design is entirely in the active, stimulated,
and unchanged part of the design.

entirely in the active, stimulated and unchanged part of the design.

and sem1 are not active or stimulated in a series of tests and are purely digital. As long as
you are not replacing the analog part of the design, you can use dynamic reconfiguration
at runtime to replace these sub-hierarchies with empty substitute modules.

Dynamic Reconfiguration in a Mixed Signal Flow
• Cross-module references (XMRs) from analog side of mixed signal boundary to the
replaced side of the dynamic reconfiguration boundary are not supported.
• Analog tunnel re-analysis cannot happen when a Verilog module is replaced at runtime
using dynamic reconfiguration. All the connectivity analysis happens at compile-time
and therefore runtime changes from dynamic reconfiguration is not reflected in this
analysis.
The use model for using the dynamic reconfiguration at runtime feature in a mixed signal
design is a combination of the use models for dynamic reconfiguration and mixed signal
verification. The following are the steps in the combined use model:
1. Write substitute empty module definitions to replace the top-level modules of the sub-
hierarchies that are inactive for a series of tests.
2. Write a compile-time configuration file for dynamic reconfiguration that specifies:
◦ the original module definitions of the top-level module instances in the inactive sub-
hierarchies
◦ the substitute empty module definitions that replace the originals at runtime
3. Write a setup file for the analog part of the mixed signal design.
4. Compile the digital part of the design, specifying three things:
◦ compiling for dynamic reconfiguration with the compile-time configuration
file specified with the following option: +optconfigfile+compile-
time_config_file_name
◦ compiling for mixed signal simulation and specifying the setup file with the following
option: -ad=setup_file
◦ the source files for the module definitions in the design and the source files for the
empty substitute modules
