The feature has the following limitations:
• MDAs for interface type object across partial elaboration are not supported.
• Only top-down absolute XMRs in substitute modules are allowed to access object in
the fixed part of the design.
• Original module of partial elaboration hierarchy can have reference to the upward XMR
or the module XMR. These XMRs are valid if no replacement happens at simulation
time. If the substitute module has upward XMR, then VCS generates compile-time
error.
• XMRs with target inside partial elaboration hierarchy do not have value if the module is
replaced at simulation time. If original module is used at simulation time, then values of
XMR are updated.
• The substitute module that do not have any instance in fixed part of the design are
instantiated as a dummy top-level instance at simulation time.
• Only XMRs to scalars. vectors, and MDA across the dynamic reconfiguration boundary
are allowed. All other complex types result in compile-time XMR error conditions.
If replacement happens any XMR reading from the replaced hierarchy returns Z (high
impedance). Even if the replacement module instance matches with the XMR path, the
XMR does not get resolved in the new instance.
• The ports of the original and substitute modules must be the same in terms of:
◦ Direction
◦ Size (bit-width and number of dimensions)
◦ Data type
There is no requirement that the corresponding ports have the same name.

• Strength declarations, registered nets, and ref ports are not allowed on modules
on the dynamic reconfiguration boundary. This boundary has the following module
definitions:
◦ Original modules whose instances might be replaced at runtime
◦ Substitute modules
• In VCS mixed-HDL designs, module definitions on the boundary must be Verilog or
SystemVerilog and have none of the following hierarchically under them:
◦ VHDL code cannot be hierarchically under a replacement module.
◦ SystemC module
◦ An analog part of a mixed-signal design
◦ A DirectC call, but PLI and VPI calls across the boundary are allowed.
• Parameter values are evaluated at for compile-time. Parameter passing across the
boundary is allowed but VCS does not assign the parameter values in the replaced
instances.
• The module definitions for substitute modules must be part of the design’s source
code. VCS does not create empty modules for you.

VCS NLP Features
This chapter describes the following VCS Native Low Power (VCS NLP)

reset option acts either as a set or reset
of the isolation cell based on the clamp value set by the -async_clamp_value option
(clamp value is 0 for reset and 1 for set)
• The net_name is the name of the control signal which acts as the set or reset. Its type
is similar to -isolation_signal and can be either port, pin, or net. The sensitivity is
specified using the high or low keyword.
• The -async_clamp_value option specifies whether the -async_set_reset option acts
as a set or reset.
• When -async_clamp_value is 0, net_name acts as a reset of the isolation cell.
• When -async_clamp_value is 1, net_name acts as a set of the isolation cell.
• Specifying -async_clamp_value is optional. The clamp value can also be set using a
port attribute.
• The -async_set_reset and -async_clamp_value options can be specified with
-update. They can occur in any order.
Using Port Attribute
If you do not want the control pin to act as a set or reset while specifying the strategy, you
can use the UPF_async_clamp_value port attribute. In this case, the same control pin
may get connected to some cells which have set and other cells which have reset pin.
set_port_attributes -ports {p1} -attribute {UPF_async_clamp_value 0/1 }
This attribute is applicable when -async_set_reset option is specified. For an isolation
strategy with -async_set_reset option and without a -async_clamp_value option, VCS
NLP uses the specified clamp value in the port attribute.
If there is a conflict between -async_clamp_value and the UPF_async_clamp_value
attribute, a warning message is issued and the UPF_async_clamp_value attribute is used
for behavior.

Support to Allow Internal Direction for Supply Port
Error and Warning Conditions
The following are the error and warning conditions:
• An error message is issued when -async_set_reset is specified and -clamp_value
is not a latch.
• An error message is issued when net_name is specified, but sensitivity <high|low> is
not specified.
• An error message is issued when net_name does not exist in the design.
• A warning message is issued when -async_set_reset is specified and there is
no -async_clamp_value specified in the set_isolation command or through the
set_port_attributes command (as specified in the UPF_async_clamp_value port
attribute). The -async_set_reset option is ignored.
• A warning message is issued when -async_clamp_value is specified, but there is no
-async_set_reset option. The -async_clamp_value option is ignored.
Also, when the UPF_async_clamp_value attribute is specified, but there is no
-async_set_reset option, the attribute is ignored.

Support for use_retention_as_primary for Isolation Semantics
Support for use_retention_as_primary for Isolation Semantics
VCS NLP supports the set_retention -use_retention_as_primary option. When this
option is specified, the retention supply powers the output driver of the register. That is, the
primary supply of the output pin of the retention register is the retention supply.
set_retention retention_name
-domain domain_name
[ -use_retention_as_primary]
set_retention RET1 -domain PD1 -use_retention_as_primary
map_retention_cell -domain PD1 -lib_cells {SDFRET*} RET1
This enhancement allows you to model a retention cell with output related to backup
supply. Specifying the -use_retention_as_primary option instructs VCS NLP to use a
retention cell whose output pin is related to the retention supply (rather than the domain
primary).
Figure 88 Library Cell Used When -use_retention_as_primary is Specified

Support for use_retention_as_primary for Isolation Semantics
• When the -use_retention_as_primary option is not specified, for paths which
originate from the output of the retention, the primary supply of the domain is
considered as the driver_supply.
• When the -use_retention_as_primary option is specified, for paths which originate
from the output of the retention, the retention_supply of the retention strategy is
considered as the driver_supply of the path.
• The -use_retention_as_primary option changes the driver supply of ports that are
sinks of the inserted retention register. Such changes could affect the interpretation of
the -source filters of the set_isolation strategies that apply to those ports.
Corruption and Isolation Semantics
Following are the corruption semantics:
• When - use_retention_as_primary opti

set_retention RET1 -domain PD_MID -retention_supply SS1 \
-elements {O1}
set_retention RET2 -domain PD_MID -retention_supply SS1 \
-elements {O2} -use_retention_as_primary

set_isolation ISO1 -domain PD_MID -source SS1
set_isolation ISO2 -domain PD_MID -source PD_MID.primary

Isolation cell based on strategy ISO1 is inserted on the net driven by the retention

Support for Atomic Power Domains
VCS NLP supports atomic power domains as per 1801-2018 version of the UPF LRM.
As per the LRM, extent of an atomic power domain can be modified, that is, updating
the options -elements {} and -exclude_elements {} of an atomic power domain is
allowed.
You must use the -atomic option of the create_power_domain command to define an
atomic power domain. Following is the syntax for creating an atomic power domain:
create_power_domain <name> -atomic
[-elements element_list]
[-exclude_elements exclude_list]
[…]

Support for Atomic Power Domains
• To define an atomic power domain, you must specify the -atomic option during the first
definition of that power domain. Specifying the -atomic option later with -update is not
allowed, it results in an error and dropping of that constraint.
• For any cell in the extent of atomic power domain to be added to any other power
domain, the cell or its ancestor must be excluded from the atomic power domain.
• In the rest of this section, any mention of the phrase power domain implies non-atomic
power domain.
Supported Usage
The following points describe the supported usage of the -atomic option:
• An empty power domain can be defined as atomic.
• A power domain on macro, ETM, or black box can be defined as atomic.
• A power domain on leaf cells can be defined as atomic.
• You can update the extent of an atomic power domain, that is, updating -elements {}
and -exclude_elements {} is allowed.
• An element excluded from atomic power domain can be added to either atomic or non-
atomic power domain. There is no restriction that an element excluded from atomic
should be added only to atomic power domains.
• There is no restriction that root cells of atomic power domains should be part of same
voltage area. They can be part of different voltage areas too.
Error Checks
The following error checks are added:
Error Check-1
VCS NLP will not allow any instance in the descendant subtree of an atomic power
domain to be included in the extent of another power domain, unless that instance name
is, or is in the descendant subtree of an instance which is excluded from that atomic
domain. Violating this results in an error message (see Example 2).

The function must have only one input of type real and its return value must be of type
UPF::supply_net_type.

Marking a Cell or Module As Power Aware by Considering the Direction and Type of Its PG
Pins
Marking a Cell or Module As Power Aware by Considering the
Direction and Type of Its PG Pins
VCS NLP is enhanced to perform a strict DB PG pin matching for a cell or module
by considering the direction and type of its PG pins in Liberty and Verilog model, and
appropriately mark the
IsPowerAwareModuleCell
IsPowerAwareModuleCell attribute as true or false in the
mvsim_native_reports/library_mapping.rpt file. It performs the following checks to
mark a cell or module as power aware:
• If Liberty declares a PG pin with direction : in, it should be direction inout or input in
the Verilog model for the cell or module to be classified as power aware.
• If Liberty declares a PG pin with direction : out, it should be direction inout or output
in the Verilog model for the cell or module to be classified as power aware.
• If the direction of a PG pin in Liberty is unknown, VCS NLP checks for its pg_type.
If pg_type is internal power or ground, it cannot match to an input port, but can match
to either of the output, inout, reg, wire, supply0, supply1, and supply_net_type.
If pg_type is primary power or ground, it can match to any port (input, output, or
inout), reg, wire, supply0, supply1, or supply_net_type.
To enable this feature, use the
-power=strict_db_match
-power=strict_db_match compile-time option.
Simulation behavior depends on whether the Verilog model is power aware or non-power
aware. This feature allows you to correct the Verilog model or make any other required
changes to get accurate simulation behavior of a DB cell or model.
Consider the following Verilog and UPF files:

reg A,B;
reg [2:0] myBus_1,myBus_2;
wire E;
wire crtl;

Support for the SPA -applies_to Option without -elements
According to the UPF 3.0 LRM, specifying the -elements option with the
set_port_attributes -applies_to command is not mandatory. Starting with this
release, VCS NLP accepts the -applies_to option of set_port_attributes command
without the -elements option. This feature makes VCS NLP to align with the UPF 3.0
LRM.
The following table describes usage examples and the new behavior:
SPA Command New Behavior
set_port_attributes -ports <port list>
-applies_to < >
Filters the ports from the port list.
set_port_attributes -ports <> -applies_to <>
-exclude_elements<>
Excludes the ports specified in
-exclude_elements and filters the ports
whose direction is not consistent with
any of the directions identified by the
-applies_to option.

-exclude_ports<>
No error
set_port_attributes -ports <> -applies_to <>
-elements<>
Error.As per LRM, it shall be an error if
both -ports and -elements are specified.

-applies_to < >
Filters the ports of the macro according to
-applies_to.

<port list> -applies_to < >
Filters the ports whose direction is not

Support for Type Real Option With the sim_corruption_control
Command
VCS NLP supports type real option in the sim_corruption_control command. Following
is the syntax:
sim_corruption_control -type real
This feature allows you to disable corruption of real items and is applicable to complete
design hierarchy covered by the UPF. This feature does not have any effect other than
disabling corruption of real. For example, if the real variable values used in the behavior
models are corrupted, this feature allows you to disable corruption of these real items only.

Support for Golden UPF
Following are the limitations of this feature:
• This feature is supported only for SystemVerilog real variable type only. Wreal or any
other nettype nodes involving ‘real’ are not supported.
• This feature is supported only for pure Verilog designs. VHDL is not supported.
• The corruption is restricted to the ‘simstate’ based corruption only. Therefore, this
feature does not affect the corruption due to isolation power, SRSN/SPA power, or any
port-based corruption.
Support for Golden UPF
In the UPF flow, each stage of the flow uses a single UPF file that is modified during
synthesis and physical implementation in the following ways:
The original UPF file, written with the RTL description, is modified by the Design Compiler,
resulting in the UPF' (UPF prime) file. The UPF' file reflects the changes that occurred
during synthesis such as insertion of always-on buffers, isolation and retention cells, and
PG connections to the cells.
The UPF' file is modified by the IC Compiler, resulting in the UPF'' (UPF double prime) file.
The UPF'' file reflects the changes that occurred during physical implementation, such as
the insertion of power switch cells.
The Synopsys Galaxy Implementation Platform offers a method of maintaining the UPF
multi-voltage power intent of the design using the original “golden” UPF file throughout the
synthesis, physical implementation, and verification steps, along with supplemental UPF
files generated by the Design Compiler and IC Compiler tools. This method is called the
golden UPF flow.
% vcs <design_files> -sverilog -gupf_config power.config
% ./simv
The -gupf_config option allows you to specify the power configuration file
(power.config). Following are the contents of the power.config file:
db_search_path = "<dir1>,<dir2>,…"
db_link_library = "<file1.db>,<file2.db>,…"
set upf_name_map { {mod1 mod1.nmf} {mod2 mod2.nmf} {mod3 mod3.nmf} … }
read_upf <UPF_FILE_NAME> \
-strict_check false \
-supplemental <supplemental_UPF_file> \
-target <icc_netlist|dc_pg_netlist|dc_netlist> \
-scope <TARGET MODULE>

Support for Golden UPF
db_search_path
Global variable. Used to search for .db (liberty) files.
db_link_library
Global variable. Used to specify the list of .db files to be used in the design.
upf_name_map
Global variable. Used to specify the name of the map file for a design top module.
read_upf
This command is used to parse the Synopsys flow compatible UPF file.
The read_upf command must be specified for the top-level UPF file. The options of this
command have the following semantics:
-strict_check false
When false (as for golden UPF application to a netlist), default matching rules are used
for name lookups, if no rules are defined.
-supplemental <supplemental_UPF_file>
Specifies a supplemental UPF file to be loaded after the golden UPF file. The
supplemental UPF additionally supports create_power_domain -elements -update .
-target <icc_netlist|dc_pg_netlist|dc_netlist>
Specifies the target design.
icc_netlist — Specifies that the isolation and retention strategies, and power switches
are implemented in the incoming target netlist, and resulting cells are explicitly connected
to their supplies through the connect_supply_net commands in the incoming UPF.
VCS NLP supports ICC PG netlists where supplies are implemented and
explicitly connected in the netlist.
dc_pg_netlist — Specifies that the supplies are implemented and explicitly connected in
the incoming target DC netlist.
dc_netlist — Specifies that the isolation and retention strategies are implemented in the
incoming target netlist, and resulting cells are explicitly connected to their supplies through
the connect_supply_net commands in the incoming UPF.
-scope

• The correlated_supply_group attribute

Successive Refinement of a Supply Set State
VCS NLP allows you to define a supply set state partially and then incrementally refine it
to a fully-defined states using the -update option of the add_power_state command. To
begin with, you can initially specify the name of the state, and then incrementally add more
intent to the state using the -update option.

Successive Refinement of a Supply Set State
This feature is supported for all types of objects (supply set, domain, and group)

Example 124 test.upf
add_power_state -supply SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON}}}
add_power_state -supply SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {ground ==
{FULL_ON}}} -update
add_power_state -supply SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON
1.0}}} -update
add_power_state -supply SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {ground == {FULL_ON
0.0}}} \
-update
The above UPF is interpreted as follows. This is in line with the UPF 2.1.
add_power_state -supply SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON
1.0} && \
{ground == {FULL_ON 0.0}}}
It is illegal to update the state voltage or state type.
Case-1:
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON
1.0}}}
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON
0.0}}} -update
VCS NLP issues the following error message for case-1:
Error-[UPF_EUSSV] Error updating supply expression voltage for
such scenarios

Successive Refinement of a Supply Set State
Case-2:
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON
1.0}}}
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {OFF}}}
-update
VCS NLP issues the following error message for case-2:
Error-[UPF_EUSST] Error updating supply expression state type
Updating an Existing Logic Expression
You can use the -update option to update an existing logic expression (-logic_expr).
The following example shows how a logic expression can be updated using the -update
option:
Example 125 test1.upf
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-logic_expr {net1}}
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-logic_expr {net2}} -update
The above UPF is interpreted as follows. This is in line with the UPF 2.1.
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-logic_expr {net1 && net2}}
Updating an Existing Simstate
You can use the -update option to update an existing simstate (-simstate).
The following example shows how a simstate can be updated using the -update option:
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-simstate {NOT_NORMAL}}
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-simstate {CORRUPT}} -update

Permitting Supply Set States that do not Have a Supply Network Expression in
Group/Domain State
VCS NLP allows you to refer to a supply set state in a group irrespective of whether the
supply set state has a -supply_expr defined or not. The -supply_expr definition for
the supply set state can come later in the flow, after the group is defined. Consider the
following example:
Example 128 test4.upf
add_power_state SS1 -state ON1 {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON 0.8}}}
add_power_state SS1 -state ON2 {-simstate NORMAL}

create_power_state_group GROUP
add_power_state -group GROUP -state GS1 {-logic_expr {SS1 == ON1}}
add_power_state -group GROUP -state GS2 {-logic_expr {SS1 == ON2}}
-update
For the above UPF, group states GS1 and GS2 are created successfully.
Excluding Ports from the set_port_attributes Command
As per the UPF 3.0, a port is removed from the candidate set if the port name appears in
the -exclude_ports list.

Excluding Ports from the set_port_attributes Command
VCS NLP supports the -exclude_ports option of the set_port_attributes command.
This option provides flexibility for specifying ports for the set_port_attributes
The ports in the list of -exclude_ports are excluded from the current
set_port_attributes command.
• If a port is listed in -exclude_ports of the current set_port_attributes, its previous
set_port_attributes setting continues to apply.
• If all the objects in -exclude_ports do not exist in the design, the entire command is
an error and has no effect.
• If only some, but not all, objects in -exclude_ports do not exist in the design, the
command is applied to the existing objects, and a warning is issued for the non-existing
object.
• If both -exclude_ports and -model are specified, the specified ports of the model are
excluded during candidate set creation. When specified with -model, arguments to the
-exclude_ports option should be simple names. VCS NLP issues an error message if
rooted names are specified in this usage.
Consider the following figure:
Case-1: -exclude_ports with -ports. In the following example, top_in1 is excluded:
set_port_attributes -ports {top_in*} -exclude_ports {top_in1} -attribute
-clamp_value z

The following features are not supported:
• -elements with -exclude_elements
• -elements with -exclude_ports
• Interface/modport support
• VHDL Support
• Bit-level support for -model -exclude_ports

• iso_source
• iso_sink

upf_get_handle_by_name
VCS NLP supports the following types of handles:
• Object Handles
References to the objects in the UPF information model. These handles can be
compared using a == operator.
• Iterator Handles
Iterators to containers in the UPF information model. These handles can be reused as
iterators are scoped objects and get deleted after the iteration is complete. You must
not use the iterator handles with the == operator for comparison.
• Property Handles
References to property value wrapper. These handles are same for all integer/Boolean
properties, real, string, and supply type properties. You must not use the iterator
handles with the == operator for comparison.
Table 16 Get Handle By Name
Description Returns the handle to the object in the information model from the given path
name.
upf_get_handle_by_name
upfHandleT upf_get_handle_by_name(upfStringT pathname,
upfHandleT relative_to = null);
Example Example: Get handle to a strategy
upfHandleT scope = upf_get_handle_by_name("/top/ dut_i");
upfHandleT iso = upf_get_handle_by_name("pd", scope);
end
Arguments pathname - A string representing handle ID for an object.
relative_to - An optional handle to the object from which the relative path
name is given.
Return Value Returns the handle to the specified property or null if not found.
The path name starts with ‘/’ followed by the object or scope below power top. This API
returns following types of handles:
• Objects
• Iterators

dst - A string representing hierarchical path ID of the destination object on

This API is supported for the following objects (Native HDL Representation types):
• Power domain ( upfPdSsObjT)
• Supply set ( upfPdSsObjT)

◦ Save signal ( upfBooleanObjT)
◦ Restore signal ( upfBooleanObjT)
◦ Isolation signal ( upfBooleanObjT)
◦ Supply set function ( upfSupplyObjT)

The native HDL representation is a structure/record type in HDL that contains the following
two fields:
• A value field corresponding to the dynamic property of the object to allow continuous
monitoring of dynamic properties.
• A handle field of type upfHandleT to allow access to other properties of the object.

Searching Specified Scope and Its Descendant Hierarchy
The find_objects command searches for instances, nets, ports, supply ports, or
processes within a scope.
A leaf cell is any cell having no descendants. Standard cells and macros are always
considered to be leaf cells. Any hierarchy with the terminal_boundary attribute is also
considered as a leaf cell. For macros, a UPF_is_hard_macro attribute value of TRUE on
a model or a UPF_is_soft_macro attribute value of TRUE on an instance indicates that it
shall be treated as a leaf cell.
VCS NLP allows you to search the specified scope and its entire descendant hierarchy
without considering the terminal_boundary/UPF_is_soft_macro marking using the
-traverse_macros option. Following is the syntax:
find_objects scope
-pattern search_ pattern
[-object_type <model | inst | port | supply_port | net | process>]
[-direction <in | out | inout>]
[-transitive [<TRUE | FALSE>]]
[-regexp | -exact]
[-ignore_case]
[-non_leaf | -leaf_only]
[ -traverse_macros]
• When you specify the -traverse_macros option, the traversal stops at a standard cell
and hard macro boundaries.
• If the -traverse_macros option is specified, then -transitive TRUE is implicitly
specified.
• The -traverse_macros option is supported only for -object_type model | inst
• VCS NLP issues a warning message when you specify object type ( -object_type)
other than model | inst . For example:
find_objects . -pattern in1 -object_type port -traverse_macros

Instrumentation for pg_function Attribute
The instrumentation for pg_function attribute takes the following scenarios into
consideration:
• Scenario-1: PG pin is power aware and wire type with HDL drivers
In this case, the wire value is used to drive the stage, and voltage is driven by MUX as
inferred from the liberty file.
• Scenario-2: PG pin is power aware and wire type with no HDL drivers
In this case, the PG pin gets the supply_net_type value from the inferred MUX, and
the wire value is a VCT version of the supply_net_type value.

Simulation Control Commands Support
• Scenario-3: PG pin is power aware and supply_net_type with HDL drivers
In this case, the inferred MUX is not instrumented and the supply_net_type value is
used as is.
• Scenario-4: PG pin is power aware and supply_net_type with no HDL drivers
In this case, the supply_net_type value is driven by inferred MUX instrumentation.
• Scenario-5: PG pin is not power aware
In this case, the supply_net_type node is added and the supply_net_type value is
driven by inferred MUX instrumentation.

Using the sim_corruption_control Command
The sim_corruption_control command allows you to turn off corruption semantics for
specific set of design elements. This command allows behavioral modules (for example,
real number modules) to operate correctly in a low power environment. This command is
only applicable for functional verification.
The following is the syntax of the sim_corruption_control command:
sim_corruption_control
[-elements element_list]
[-model model_name]
When -elements is specified, the elements shall be a list of variables, registers, signals
of the specified hierarchical instances. If the element is an instance, then by default the
command applies to all objects defined in that instance and all dependent subtrees.
Wildcards are supported with this option.
When -model is specified, only names that are declared in the model can be referenced
in the -elements option, and all names are interpreted relative to the topmost scope of
the model. You must use this option along with the -elements option, otherwise VCS NLP
issues an error message.

Simulation Control Commands Support
When -elements is specified along with -model, then the specified elements should be
local to the model.

Support for UPF Power-Aware Converters
The following sections describe the support for UPF power-aware converters:
• Introduction
Converter modules convert signal values from one type to another. There will be no
specification of liberty for converter modules. A converter module has two scalar ports of
two different types (input and output). A converter is instantiated between a port and the
signal that is connected at the high-conn of the port connection.
One of the major challenges during simulation in presence of UPF is to correctly simulate
the converter modules that are inserted by the tool at real-logic boundaries. For a logic-to-
real converter, when a logic signal information is sent to a block, the corresponding supply
(that is, power, ground) associated with that logic signal should play a role to determine
the real number value.

Support for UPF Power-Aware Converters
On the other hand, for a real-to-logic converter, when the real output pin changes its value,
the corresponding supply associated with this pin should be considered to convert the real
number value to corresponding logic value.
VCS supports UPF power-aware converters. The following sections describe how the
converter modules behave in presence of the power sources defined in UPF.
This feature is enabled by default. However, you must specify all the relevant options
that are required for inserting converter modules. For more information, refer to the VCS
Converters section in the VCS User Guide.
If you want to disable the feature, use the following compile-time option:
%vcs -power=disable_supply_aware_converter

Isolation Insertion on Heterogeneous Fanout Paths
The following points describe the support for isolation insertion on heterogeneous fanout
paths:
• This feature improves the granularity of the set_isolation -sink/-
diff_supply_only option. Also, this support changes the isolation conflict resolution
by allowing two isolation strategies to have the same options other than -sink/-
diff_supply_only.
• VCS NLP can insert isolation cells wherever they deem fit as long as they do not
violate the isolation constraints. Also, heterogeneous fanout support does not insert
isolation cells as less as possible.
• The heterogeneous fanout isolation cells can be inserted at any hierarchy boundary
provided that they reside at the power domain specified by the strategy (and do not
cross the power domain).
• Each path is isolated by its highest precedence strategy (assuming all filters are
satisfied) only, otherwise it is not isolated.
• If isolation insertion is not possible due to the location violating the filters, a lower-
precedence strategy is not applied (-diff_supply_only/self, no filters/parent/self).
• The following warning message is issued when the highest precedence strategy is not
applied due to the location violating the -diff_supply_only/-source/-sink filters.
Warning-[UPF_ISO_HETEROGENEOUS_FANOUTS] Isolation skipped due to
hetero fanout
• The heterogeneous fanout isolation cells from the -applies_to input strategy can be
closer to the output of the power domain boundary than the input.
• An error message is issued if both conservative_diff_supply_isolation and
hetero_fanout_isolation are enabled. Following is the sample error message:
Error-[UPF_ATTRS_CONFLICT] Conflicting design attributes specified
./test.upf, 4
Attribute 'conservative_diff_supply_only_isolation' conflicts with
attribute 'hetero_fanout_isolation' specified at ./test.upf, 2.
Please remove one of the conflicting attributes.
• The -diff_supply_only option adds a criteria to filter isolation at sinks. Therefore, the
heterogeneous fanout isolation cell insertion results can be changed with this option.

• The strategy iso2 (no_iso) is applicable on paths A->C and A->D.

be applied since it would violate the -no_isolation requirement on paths A->C and A-
>D.
• A warning message is issued for the path A->B since it remains unisolated.
VCS NLP compile-time reports are dumped by default inside the mvsim_native_reports
directory. For large designs, a lot of information is dumped in each of these reports
resulting in large file sizes. However, you may not need all the reports for diagnostic
purposes. Therefore, this leads to performance degradation and resource utilization.
You can use the -power_report=<switch> compile option to control the dumping of
reports. You can use this option to enable or disable the reports that are dumped in the low
power analysis stage based on your requirement.
This feature improves compile performance for large designs by dumping only the required
reports. Also, you can the disable dumping of all reports by default in the regression mode.

The following topics describe this feature in detail:
• Enabling and Disabling Dumping of Individual Reports
• Enabling and Disabling Report Groups
• Precedence Details
• Supported Reports
• Examples
The following is the use model:
% vcs design.v -upf design.upf -sverilog -power_report=<switch>
All reports will have a separate switch name that can be passed to -power_report=
prefixed with either the - sign to disable the report or the + sign to enable the report.
If an invalid switch name is provided, VCS NLP issues a warning message with
the NLP-UNKNOWN-PWR-RPT-OPT tag. If multiple switch names are provided and
one of them is an invalid option, then the warning message is printed only for
the invalid option. The remaining switches are processed without any issues.
Enabling and Disabling Dumping of Individual Reports
This section describes how to enable and disable the dumping of individual reports
using switch. Following is the use model to enable/disable the dumping of the individual
reports:
% vcs -power_report=+/-<report_name>
Examples:
-power_report=+db_inside_db
Enables the dumping of the db_inside_db.rpt files inside the mvsim_native_reports
directory during compilation.
-power_report=-db_inside_db
Disables the dumping of the db_inside_db.rpt files inside the mvsim_native_reports
directory during compilation.

Multiple reports can be enabled/disabled to control individual report dumping. For
example,
-power_report=-srsn_spa_association-upf_supply_net-upf_supply_port
Disables the dumping of the srsn_spa_association.rpt, upf_supply_net.rpt,
and upf_supply_port.rpt files inside the mvsim_native_reports directory during
compilation.
-power_report=new_isolation_association-upf_supply_source
Dumps the new_isolation_association.rpt report that is disabled by default and
disables the upf_supply_source.rpt report that is dumped by default.
Enabling and Disabling Report Groups
The -power_report=<switch> option also provides the feature to enable/disable a group
of reports by passing a single switch. The reports are classified under the following groups
to enable/disable a group of reports:

Using the group feature, you do not have to pass individual reports to the switch. Instead,
the group name can be passed. Following is the use model:
% vcs -power_report=+/-<group_name>
Examples:
-power_report=-all_diag
Disables the dumping of all the diagnostic reports which are dumped by default.
-power_report=stats or -power_report=+stats

Semantics of the create_logic_net Command
The create_logic_net command creates a wire type net in the scope of the command.
This command accepts a simple name for a net. If the same name net already exists,
then VCS checks its type. If the type of existing net is one of logic, reg, or wire, then it is
the implementation of the UPF net specified in the command. The existing net must be a
scalar of a compatible type (logic, reg, or wire).

Table 45 create_logic_net Command
Purpose Define a logic net
Syntax create_logic_net net_name
Arguments net_name. Specifies a simple name.
Return value Return an empty string if successful. If not, issue a TCL_ERROR.
If the net type is not compatible or is not a scalar, then VCS reports an error message
when the command is processed d

CL_ERROR.

If the same name scalar port exists in the design with a compatible type (logic, reg, wire),
then VCS uses it as the implementation of the UPF logic port. If the type is incompatible or
the port is not scalar, VCS issues an error message.
If the port existing in the design has a different direction compared to the UPF, then the
direction of the UPF overrides the existing port direction. The direction of the existing port
in design changes to the UPF-specified direction. VCS issues a warning message for a
change in direction.
If the same name scalar net exists in the design with the compatible type (logic, reg, or
wire), then VCS uses that net as the lowconn of the UPF logic port. VCS issues a warning
message for reusing a design port in the UPF.
With the creation of Logic Port, an implicit Logic Net of the same name as the port is
implicitly created. If after UPF reading, the Logic Port is not connected to a Logic Net on
lowconn, then the implicitly created net shall be connected to the Logic Port implicitly. Due
to this implicit Logic Net creation, the Logic Port can be used in any UPF command where
a hierarchical net is used as captured in Table 48.
The Logic Port created by this command can be used in any successive command that

er, it might take a few cycles for signals to be stabilized and could still be X.
Therefore, if the assertions start immediately on wake-up, it can still cause failures.
The -control_expr option provides another way, where you can delay enabling the
assertions until signals are stabilized after power-up.
When this option is specified, the sim_assertion_control command is controlled
by the Boolean value of the expression. If the expression evaluates to TRUE, the
command is active and when it evaluates to FALSE, the command goes inactive. When
the command is active, the assertions controlled by sim_assertion_control are
disabled.
sim_assertion_control -type suspend -control_expr a&&b
For the above command, assertion control is active with type KILL for all power
domains when the control expression a&&b becomes TRUE. When activated, all
assertions in those domains get suspended and are resumed when the control
expression a&&b becomes FALSE.
The sim_assertion_control command can be specified globally or on a particular
domain. The global specification can be overridden by a domain-level specification.
Consider the following commands:
1. sim_assertion_control -type reset -domain {PD1}
2. sim_assertion_control -type suspend
3. sim_assertion_control -type reset -domain {PD2}
The first and third commands enable the assertion control on PD1 and PD2. The second
command specifies the assertion control type as suspend globally on all domains, but
this does not override the domain-level specification in the other two commands as the
domain-level specification takes priority over the global specification.
The same override semantics are applied even in the presence of -control_expr.
Some commands can use domain state, and some can use -control_expr for
controlling assertions. Consider the following commands:
1. sim_assertion_control -type reset -domain {PD1}
2. sim_assertion_control -type suspend -control_expr {a == 1'b1}
3. sim_assertion_control -type reset -domain {PD2} -control_expr {b ==
1'b1}
In the above example, assertions in PD1 are controlled by domain state (command
1) and assertions in PD2 are controlled by expression b == 1'b1 (command 3).
Assertions in all other domains are controlled with the expression a == 1'b1
(command 2).

Support for the sim_assertion_control -control_expr Command
Following are the limitations of the sim_assertion_control -control_expr command
support:
• Using UPF logic nets or logic ports in -control_expr is not supported.
• Using power state expressions in -control_expr is not supported.

event simulated in that cycle. The sum of counts, therefore,
may exceed the total number of low EPC cycles
• Only VCS 64-bit is supported.
• SDF and specify block delays are not mapped. They are shown as UNMAPPED SDF
EVENT.
• Structural delays (that is, delays in continuous assignments) may not be mapped to
source. They are shown as UNMAPPED EVENT .
• AMS is not supported.

Reducing Compile Time for FGP Analysis
• Profiles only Verilog events and skips VHDL delay events.

Reducing Compile Time for FGP Analysis
You can use the -fgp=hier option to reduce the compile time and compile memory. This
option is particularly useful for gate-level simulation (GLS) designs.
Use the -fgp=hier option at compile time. For example,
% vcs -fgp=hier <other compile options>
• Dynamic reconfiguration is not supported.
• The -fgp=multisocket option is not supported.

VCS Performance Tuning Using Dynamic
Performance Optimizer (DPO)
VCS performance is an important aspect that impacts the verification and project time
lines. Traditionally, simulation performance has been a function of CPU performance,
memory efficiency, and serial algorithm. VCS has multiple options to improve the simulator
performance depending on certain characteristics of the design environment that is being
compiled and simulated. These options allow you to identify performance bottlenecks
and tune the command-line arguments and/or coding styles to extract best possible
performance.
Dynamic Performance Optimizer (DPO) is an intelligent automated approach that
enables necessary diagnostics during VCS compile and simulation and leverages AI to
recommend the appropriate set of options for enabling maximum performance without
manual intervention.
DPO supports performance analysis of the full regression or multiple tests per simv.
Enabling DPO With VCS
DPO is enabled by adding the -dpo option to the vcs compile command line. DPO specific
options are enabled using the -dpo_opts <option=value> option. For the complete list
of DPO options, see DPO Options.
-dpo is ignored when specified inside arguments passed to -f/-F/-file. This
option should explicitly be passed on the vcs command line.
DPO Flow
Typical DPO flow involves the following two steps:
Step-1: Learn and Merge
Learn — This step performs analysis and stores learnings/recommendations in the
database. The -dpo_opts mode=learn option at the compile time enables Learn mode.

DPO Options
Merge — This step merges the learnings across the designs/tests. This step is mandatory
for applying the learnings. For more information, refer to Merging Learn Databases.
Step-2: Apply
Apply — Learnings/Recommendations are fetched from the merged database and applied
automatically. This step is enabled by default when the -dpo_opts mode option is not
specified or when the -dpo_opts mode=apply option is explicitly specified.
The Apply mode is valid only when a merged learn database is available.
The recommended usage is to run all designs/tests in Learn mode once and then merge
the learnings. You can switch to Apply mode for all subsequent runs.

You can use the test_type dpo option to override the default priority order of picking

of priority is used.
uvm – Selects the test name from +UVM_TESTNAME if it is specified, otherwise default order
of priority is used.
ovm – Selects the test name from +OVM_TESTNAME if it is specified, otherwise default order
of priority is used.
cm_test – Selects the test name from -cm_test if it is specified, otherwise default order of
priority is used.
cm_name – Selects the test name from -cm_name if it is specified, otherwise default order of
priority is used.
• If test_type is specified and if the relevant argument is missing, the default order is
considered.
• If test_type is not specified, the default order is considered.
• Specifying -dpo_opts test_name in simulation command line overrides all above,
omitting test_type.

Sample Content of the dpo_reco_detail.csv File
Detail recommendation file is useful to review the recommendation per test. The
_AT_LEAST_ONE_ entry in the testname or test_variant column of the dpo_reco.csv
file indicates that not ALL simulation tests or variants of the tests have the same
recommendation.
Enabling the recommendation in such scenarios might potentially lead to errors during the
apply phase compile or simulation. You must review the detail recommendation file that
captures the recommendations per test and decide if a particular recommendation should
be enabled. Sample content of the dpo_reco_detail.csv file is as follows:
## DPO RECOMMENDATION FILE HEADER
## Created at 18:52:42 on Monday 26-July-2021
## VCS Version S-2021.09

## PLEASE NOTE ##
##,#1,Purpose of this file is only to provide detailed information on the
recommendations for user review.
##,#2,"To enable or disable a recommendation, please make the changes to
'enable (Y/N)' column entry in 'dpo_reco.csv' file."

app,action,options,design_tag,testname,test_variant,recommendation,stage,
benefit,cost,category,reason

test2,1,No,vcs,"['RT', 'CT']",None,Assertion,Remove heavy assertion
debug flag for regressions

Reviewing and Enabling Recommendations
lint,REMOVE,"[['-assert','enable_diag']]",dpo_design,
test1,1,Yes,vcs,"['RT', 'CT']",None,Assertion,Remove heavy assertion
debug flag for regressions

to improve sim performance
Enable/Disable Recommendations in Apply Mode
You must review the dumped CSV file after the learn phase and modify the value
of column enable (Y/N) to have either Y or N. If you want to enable a particular
recommendation, then the value of the field enable (Y/N) must be set to Y. If it is set to N,
then the App considers it as a disabled recommendation.
These feedbacks can be passed to App using either of the following:
• Through the DPO configuration file using the -dpo_opts cfg option. Specify the
recommendations CSV file pointer with App configuration parameter reco_file.
• Through the following DPO option reco_file:
-dpo_opts reco_file=<path_to_reco_csv_file>
◦ Priority is given to the -dpo_opts reco_file option.
◦ If no -dpo_opts reco_file or config options are passed in the Apply phase,
recommendations that are ON by default are applied.
Following is the sample content of DPO configuration file. You can specify reco_file
either at app_configs (applies reco_file globally) or at app as follows:
app_configs:
reco_file : <dpo_reco.csv>
lint:
reco_file : <dpo_reco.csv>
upfopt:
reco_file : <dpo_reco.csv>
The reco_file entry under the app section gets higher priority over the entry under the
app_configs section. For an entry under the app section, only the recommendations
specific to the App are picked from the CSV file.
Dumping recommendations for user review and update is currently enabled for
the lint and upfopt Apps only.

Configuration File
Configuration File
Optional configuration file can be specified by using the -dpo_opts cfg=<config file
path> option to set the necessary DPO specific logging modes, and App parameters to
override any default values for Apps.
The following sections describe this feature in detail:
• Configuration File Syntax
• Supported Message Logging Modes
• Supported App Configuration Variables
Configuration File Syntax
Following is the configuration file syntax (YAML format ^^):
app_configs:
<Message Logger variables>
< app1_name>:
<app specific config variables>
<config>: <path to app specific config file with
config variables> **
<app2_name>:
<app specific config variables>
<config>: <path to app specific config file with
config variables> **
All variables are specified in the key: value format.
^^ YAML mandates four white spaces for every indentation. Do not use <tab>.
** You can also choose to specify the variable values in an App-specific configuration file
(YAML format).
Sample Configuration File
Following is the sample configuration file:
Example 133 Sample Configuration File
log_output: file
log_level: error
plilearn:
ELAPSED_TIME_THRESHOLD: 600
fgp:
config: /home/cfg_files/fgp_config.yaml

Configuration File
Following is the sample fgp_config.yaml file:
MAX_NUM_THREADS: 6
Supported Message Logging Modes
Messaging is primarily configurable using log_level to choose the severity and
log_output to choose the target for logging. Specify logging related variables in the
app_configs: section of the configuration file. Following is the syntax:
log_level: <info/warning/error> (info is default)
• info: Report messages with info, warning, error severity
• warning: Report messages with warning and error severity
• error: Report messages with error severity
log_output: <stdout/file/quiet> (file is default)
Table 56 Supported Message Logging Modes
Mode Target
file (default) info/warning/error to stdout and dpo_workdir log files
stdout info/warning/error to stdout only
quiet info/warning/error to dpo_workdir log files only
Messages logged to stdout are also captured in the user-specified vcs/simv
log files.

DB Migration Utility
The DB migration utility (dpo_db_migrate) allows you to update the existing learn db
(from older version) to the current version without the need to re-learn.
Following is the use model:
dpo_db_migrate [-h] [-d DB_DIR] [-f filelist] [-l logfile]
-d - Specifies the comma separated list of DB directories
-f - Specifies the list of DB directories in a file
-l - Specifies the log file

Plilearn App
• By default, the migrated databases are available in the original directory. DPO saves
the old databases at the database directory level in a new directory <basename>.old/.
All the old .db files are renamed with an extension .db.old.
• If DB migration tool ran on a DB, which has already migrated to the supported version,
DPO issues an info message and will not run any migration.
• When the existing DB version is older than the currently supported tool version, the tool
automatically migrates up.
Plilearn App
The plilearn app supports the following four modes or types of PLI Learn supported by
VCS:
+vcs+learn+pli Enables the module level PLI learn.
+vcs+learn+pli+instpli Enables the instance level PLI learn.
+vcs+learn+pli+sigpli Enables signal PLI learn at the module level.
+vcs+learn+pli+sigpli
+vcs+learn+pli+instpli
Enables signal PLI learn at the instance level.
You can configure the required PLI Learn mode for a design run using the following dpo
option:
-dpo_opts cfg=dpo_plilearn.cfg
PLI_LEARN_MODE is the configuration variable that decides the type of PLI Learn mode for
a design run. It accepts the following valid values:
MODULE_PLI [Default mode] Generates module PLI tab file.
INSTANCE_PLI Generates instance PLI tab file.
MODULE_SIGNAL_PLI Generates module signal PLI tab file.
INSTANCE_SIGNAL_PLI Generates instance signal PLI tab file.
The dpo_plilearn.cfg file contains the following content:
app_configs:
log_level: info

Automg App
log_output: stdout
plilearn:
PLI_LEARN_MODE: MODULE_SIGNAL_PLI
The default PLI_LEARN_MODE is MODULE_PLI. When the PLI Learn mode is not specified in
the cfg file, then the DPO plilearn app generates the module pli tab file.
Incremental Learn Support

cutes the vcs/simv commands and
updates the status using dpo_automg --update $DPO_REGID --status $run_status
--workdir $AUTOMG_WORKDIR .
--bc_file <bc_file_path> is a pointer to the BCID setup file if already being used in
the reference environment.
--mh_file <mh_file_path> is a pointer to the MHID setup file if already being used in
the reference environment.
The following is the use model:
1. User run script capturing PASS/FAIL status
-dpo_optsapps=automgvcs <other vcs options> -dpo -dpo_opts apps=automg
-lca
simv <other simv options>
MY_STATUS=<user defined pass criteria to return PASS/FAIL>
$VCS_HOME/bin/dpo_automg --update $DPO_REGID --status $MY_STATUS
--workdir <automg workdir path>

Automg App
Sample run_script:
#!/bin/csh
rm -rf csrc simv simv.daidir ucli.key vcs.cfg

vcs test.sv -sverilog -dpo -dpo_opts apps=automg -lca
-l vcs.log
simv -l simv.log
grep 000abcd88000000a simv.log
if ($status == 0) then
set MY_STATUS="PASS"
set MY_STATUS="FAIL"
endif
echo $MY_STATUS
$VCS_HOME/bin/dpo_automg --update $DPO_REGID --status $MY_STATUS
--workdir <automg workdir path>
2. Initialize DPO automg app
% dpo_automg --reference_version <passing stream> --run_script <path
to script that launches the run and passes the status of the run back
to DPO> --init
Following is the sample command:
% dpo_automg --reference_version 2020.12 --run_script ./bm_run.csh --
init
It generates a wrapper script that launches run_script with different BCID and MHID
setups.
3. Launch the wrapper script
% sh $PWD/automg_workdir/automg_wrapper.sh
It calls run_script automatically for every iteration.

Migration Helper App
Migration Helper App
You can use the Migration Helper (mg_help)app during release migration when you
encounter compile errors in the current VCS release, but passing in the older VCS
release. The DPO mg_help app allows you to quickly identify the necessary BCIDs during
release migration and migrate with ease.
Following is the use model:
% vcs -dpo -dpo_opts apps=mg_help <other vcs options>
If the mg_help app finds any applicable BCIDs, it lists the BCID, provides
recommendation, and generates a BCID file, for example:
[DPO][MG_HELP] [INFO] Recommended BCIDs: 'ASSOC_ARRAY_DELETE_METHOD'
[DPO][MG_HELP] [INFO] RECOMMENDATION: Applicable BCIDs are listed in
'//mg_help_test/mg_help_synopsys_bc.setup' file. Please point the
environment variable SNPS_SIM_BC_CONFIG_FILE to the file and re-compile.
[DPO][MG_HELP] [INFO] Please refer to '//mg_help_test/mg_help_bc.log'
for more information regarding BCIDs.
Once recommendation is manually applied and compile is successful, the mg_help app
issues the following message:
[DPO][MG_HELP] [INFO] NO RECOMMENDATION: VCS compile is successful.
Once the compilation is successful, the subsequent compiles need not enable the
mg_help app.

Next Generation Parallel Compiler
To improve compile time for a large RTL or GLS design in VCS, use the Next Generation
Parallel Compiler feature with the -parallelcomp option. This method provides significant
compile time reduction through advanced parallelization techniques. Parallel Compile,
• Creates balanced partitions for maximum parallel efficiency.
• Uses lightweight elaboration engines for faster incremental builds.
• Scales automatically as design size increases.
As parallel compile (-parallelcomp) extends partition compile (-partcomp), designs that
use -parallelcomp also inherit the following partition-compile benefits:
• Supports incremental compilation (only modified partitions recompiled).
• Enables shared partition libraries using -partcomp_sharedlib.
• Enables autopartitioning of the design.
• Supports cross-module references (XMRs).
• Supports relocatable databases for sharing compiled partitions.
Parallel Compile enables faster scratch compilation, reduced incremental compile time,
and better memory scalability for large RTL or GLS designs.
Use the -parallelcomp compile option to enable the parallel compiler. Following is the
usage:
vcs -parallelcomp <other_options>
The -parallelcomp option compiles 4 partitions in parallel by default. In larger designs
where the number of partitions is high, the user can override the default 4 parallel
processes by using -parallelcomp=jN, where, N is the required number of parallel
compilations. You can choose N number based on the cores available in the grid. In
addition to this, parallel compile has improved global analysis time and faster elaboration
during the subsequent compilation stages.

The following messages in the log file describes the parallel compile flow.
%vcs test.v -sverilog -parallelcomp=j8

Generating new partition '_vcs_pc_package_' at

'./partitionlib/_vcs_pc_package__97cUje'.

8 parallel processes will be used.
Profile Report
The -parallelcomp option generates the profile report at the end of compilation which
contains information about the time/memory taken by global phases and individual
partitions. This enables the profiling of time spent in each step of a compilation. Following
is the usage:
vcs test.sv -full64 -sverilog -parallelcomp

Chapter 27: Next Generation Parallel Compiler
Profile Report
Following is the sample profile report:
Reals): Shows the real time consumed for each "Job" in seconds.
Peak(MB): Shows the peak memory used by each “Job”.
Global_Analysis: Shows time and memory taken by serial global phase.
Partition: Shows time and memory taken by individual partitions. These are compiling in
parallel.
Stitching: Shows time and memory spent in stitching the partitions as well as spent in
global structural optimizations.
All_Partitions: Shows the summary of time and memory for the parallel processes.
In multi-core, memory shown is peak observed on that system. In distributed compile,
memory is peak across all parallel processes.
TOTAL: Shows the total time and peak memory of the entire compilation.
The -parallelcomp=no_autopart option disables the autopartitioning of design and
enables the user-defined partitioning. If there is no user-defined partitioning, VCS allows
three default partitions that contain packages, interfaces, and modules respectively.
The -parallelcomp option is backward compatible with most of the partition compile
options. For more information, refer to the Partition Compile section in the VCS User

The following are the limitations of the parallel compiler:
• AMS is not supported.
• Type operator is not supported in elaboration context.
• MDA of interface/instances is not supported.
• -add_seq_delay in optconfigfile is not supported.

• A compilation error Error-[SV-DOSIF] Delay or synchronization in function
is generated when a time-consuming task is invoked from within a function. For cross-
partition tasks, however, the error is deferred until runtime.

Distributed Compilation
Every next generation, the increase in size of SOCs impacts the time and memory it takes
to build them.
VCS partition compile technology helps resolve this issue by dividing the big SOCs into
smaller partitions and compiling them in parallel. It scales well by increasing the number
of partitions as SOC size increases, keeping per partition compile time and memory pretty
much the same with every next generation. However, this parallelism is ultimately limited

Dynamic Test Loading (DTL) is an approach to load and run any test dynamically at any

VCS introduces a simplified use model of DTL (2-step) flow, referred to as DTL single-step

serial algorithms. However, with multicore processors and new vector instruction sets,
simulation productivity has improved.
With more cores and better vector capabilities, HyperSim helps design teams to use

• Emulation-like behavior to increase event density and improve parallel efficiency.
• A modern parallel engine that schedules and balances simulation tasks during runtime.
• The ability to detect passive simulation elements, such as DPI monitors, and run them
on separate cores.
• The ability to run modern testbench components, such as U

Enabling Congruent Mode to Improve Parallelization
The event-driven simulation of Verilog can cause race conditions at the RTL level. This
happens when several parallel processes update signals at the same simulation time,
without a set order. This can lead to results that do not match real hardware behavior.
To avoid this, design teams use nonblocking assignments for sequential logic and blocking
assignments for combinational logic. They also add timing offsets or use structured
clocking to separate data and clock events. These methods ensure predictable simulation
and easier debugging.
Sometimes, adding delays between clock and data to prevent races can slow down
parallel performance. This is because extra time steps are needed to transfer data.
VCS HyperSim congruent mode solves this by removing delays from inferred flip-flops and
latches. It keeps the simulation race-free by sampling the old data value when clock and
data change together. This increases events at clock edges and improves parallelization.
To enable congruent mode for more constructs such as continuous assignment, use the
-hypersim compile-time option.
Remove the -hypersim=bringup_mode option, as it overrides congruent mode.
To disable congruent mode on specific modules, you can use the following configuration
file syntax:
module {<module_name_or_comma_separated_list_of_module_names>}
{noJagCongruency}
Then, add the configuration file with the following compile-time option:
+optconfigfile+<cfg_file_name>
Enabling Passive Mode
Passive elements are parts of your design that only read the simulation state. They do not
change or write to the simulation state.

A module that has only input ports and does not have any output ports is called a passive
element. If the module does not change any value during simulation, either through cross-
module references, or by using a PLI application, it is also considered passive.
The following is an example of a passive module:
module (input a);
always @(a) $display(a);
HyperSim can detect and automatically mark passive modules based on how they are
used.
By default, all DPI functions are considered non-passive. This is because their behavior
in C code is unknown. If you have a DPI function which is passive, you must mark it as
passive in the configuration file.

Deviation From Regular Simulation
The passive thread uses a separate scheduler that is not linked to the main simulation.
The simulation time for the passive thread is different and is always at least one timestamp

behind the main simulation time. This can cause the following differences from a regular
simulation:
• Order of Simulation Log
The simulation logs from the passive thread and the main thread can overlap and are
not sorted by simulation time. For example, a display at time t in the passive thread
might appear after a display at time t+5 in the main thread.
• Difference in Finish Time
If the passive thread stops because of an error, the main thread might continue running
past the error time. As a result, the simulation finish time and the error time might not
be the same.
Enabling Testbench Mode
Modern testbench methods, such as UVM, are widely used. UVM gives design and
verification teams a strong and standard way to work. It supports projects from small IP
blocks to large SoCs. UVM helps teams reuse code by using modular components. It also
makes it easier to create test stimulus with constrained random methods. This leads to
better coverage and higher-quality silicon.
In the default HyperSim flow, UVM-based testbench activities run on the main thread. The
main thread waits until all testbench actions are complete.
With HyperSim testbench mode, testbench activities can run on a separate thread.
DUT activities can run on other threads at the same time. This can improve simulation
performance, especially if the testbench workload is less than 20 percent of the total.
To enable the testbench mode, use the following compile-time option:
-hypersim=tb
HyperSim testbench mode uses one CPU core. For example, if you set
-hypersim=num_threads:3, HyperSim uses 4 cores in total. One core is for
the main thread, one for the testbench thread, and the other two for parallel

Limitations of HyperSim
HyperSim has the following limitations:
• HyperSim does not support the dynamic reconfiguration feature.
• HyperSim does not support SDC.
• The HyperSim testbench flow does not support the save-restore feature.
• HyperSim does not support the reverse debug feature.
• The HyperSim passive flow is disabled in the DTL flow.
• The +vcs+loopreport option disables the HyperSim passive flow.
• HyperSim does not support analog or mixed-signal (AMS) flows.
• Remove the -hypersim=num_threads* option from the runtime options to use
simprofile for simulation profiling.
• Expect the compile time to increase by up to 1.5 times during a scratch compile.
• HyperSim does not support the +allmtm option.
• HyperSim and FGP are both multi‑core technologies. However, HyperSim offers a
wider set of features compared to FGP, as described in the HyperSim: Hyper-Scaling
Simulation Performance section.

single-step flow of DTL and can be enabled using the -dtl option.

Dynamic Performance Optimizer (DPO) is an intelligent automated approach that
enables necessary diagnostics during VCS compile and simulation and leverages AI to
recommend the appropriate set of options for enabling maximum performance without
manual intervention. DPO supports performance analysis of the full regression or multiple
tests per simv.

app.

Performance Optimizer (DPO)”, in the VCS LCA Features Guide.

VCS supports SystemVerilog SPICE design configuration with VCS-XA in partition compile
flow. You can create partitions in two ways:

default, VCS creates one partition for SPICE.

This chapter describes the simulation flows supported by VCS. You can use the following
flows to simulate your design using VCS:
• Three-step Flow
• Two-step Flow

Simulating a design using three-step flow involves three basic steps:
• Analysis
• Elaboration
• Simulation
VCS uses these three steps to compile any design irrespective of the HDL, HVL, and other
supported technologies used. For information on supported technologies, see Simulator
Support with Technologies .
For information on the data types supported across the language boundary for both ports
and generics or parameters, see the VCS Simulation Coding and Modeling Style Guide.
For information on licensing options, see Options for Licensing .
Analysis is the first step to simulate your design. In this phase, you analyze your VHDL,
Verilog, SystemVerilog, and OpenVera files using vhdlan or vlogan accordingly. The
following section includes a few example command lines to analyze your design files:
Analyzing VHDL files:
% vhdlan [ vhdlan_options] file1.vhd file2.vhd

For details, see the Using vhdlan section.
Analyzing Verilog files:
% vlogan [ vlogan_options] file1.v file2.v
For details, see the Using vlogan section.
Analyzing SystemVerilog files:
% vlogan -sverilog [ vlogan_options] file1.sv file2.sv file3.v
For the complete usage model, see Using SystemVerilog.
In the analysis phase, VCS checks the design for the syntax errors. In this phase, VCS
generates the intermediate files required for elaboration and saves these files in the
design or work library pointed to by your default logical library. For information on library
mapping, see “The Concept of a Library in VCS” . You can instruct VCS to save these
intermediate files in a different library using the -work option with the vhdlan or vlogan
executables.
Before you analyze your design using vhdlan or vlogan, ensure that the library mappings
are defined in the synopsys_sim.setup file, and that the specified physical library for
the logical library exists. If the physical directory does not exist, VCS exits with an error
message.
VCS provides vhdlan and vlogan executable to analyze VHDL and Verilog design files,
respectively. The following sections describe the usage of these two executables and
some of the commonly used options.
Using vhdlan

intermediate files in the design or work library. The syntax for the vhdlan executable is as

Optimizing Testbenches for Debugging
Improve VCS simulation performance by selectively enabling or disabling testbench
debugging features such as VCD and FSDB file writing, using conditional compilation,
runtime plusarg control, or a combination of both techniques.
Debugging operations like $monitor, $display, $dumpvars, and $fsdbDumpvars
significantly degrade simulation speed, particularly file-writing operations that generate
VCD or FSDB simulation history files. Use conditional compilation with `ifdef and +define
+macro to exclude debugging system tasks at compile time for maximum simulation
performance. Alternatively, use the $test$plusargs system function for runtime control
without recompilation, at the cost of reduced optimization since VCS must prepare for
worst-case runtime scenarios. Combine both techniques for granular control over when
simulation history files are written during different stages of the design development cycle.
Testbenches typically execute debugging features, for example, displaying text in certain
situations as specified with the $monitor or $display system tasks. Another debugging
feature, which is typically enabled in testbenches, is writing simulation history files during
simulation so that you can view the results after simulation.
Among other things, these simulation history files record the simulation times at which the
signals in your design change value. These simulation history files can be either ASCII
Value-Change-Dump (VCD) files that you can input into a number of third-party viewers, or
binary FSDB files that you can input into Verdi.

The vcdiff Utilityvcdiff utility
The vcdiff utility compares two dump files and reports any differences it finds. The dump
file can be of type VCD, EVCD, or VPD.
The vcdiff utility cannot compare dump files of different types.
Dump files consist of two sections:
• A header section that reflects the hierarchy (or some subset) of the design that was
used to create the dump file.
• A value change section, which contains all of the value changes (and times when those
value changes occurred) for all of the signals referenced in the header.
The vcdiff utility first compares the header sections and reports any signals/scopes that
are present in one dump file, but absent in other. Then, the vcdiff utility compares the
value change sections of the dump files for signals that appear in both dump files. This
utility determines value change differences based on the final value of the signal in a time
step.
Syntaxvcdiff utilitysyntax
The syntax of the vcdiff utility is as follows:
vcdiff first_dump_file second_dump_file
[-noabsentsig] [-absentsigscope scope] [-absentsigiserror]
[-allabsentsig][-absentfile filename][-matchtypes] [-ignorecase]
[-min time] [-max time] [-scope instance] [-level level_number]

[-include filename] [-ignore filename] [-strobe time1 time2]
[-prestrobe] [-synch signal] [-synch0 signal] [-synch1 signal]
[-when expression] [-xzmatch] [-noxzmatchat0]
[-compare01xz] [-xumatch] [-xdmatch] [-zdmatch] [-zwmatch]
[-showmasters] [-allsigdiffs] [-wrapsize size]
[-limitdiffs number] [-ignorewires] [-ignoreregs] [ignorereals]
[-ignorefunctaskvars][-ignoretiming units] [-ignorestrength]

Auto-partitioning
You enable auto-partitioning when you use the
-partcomp compile-time option. This
is the default and recommended mode of partitioning. Auto-partitioning automatically
partitions the design and the testbench. To specify the partitions yourself apart from the
auto-partitioning see section Specifying Partitions Manually.
Use the following compile-time options to control auto-partitioning:
•
Applies auto-partitioning to both modules and SystemVerilog packages.
•
-partcomp=autopart_low-partcomp=autopart_low[partcomp=autopart_low]
-partcomp=autopart_low
Applies auto-partitioning to both modules and packages with a low threshold, which
results in smaller and more numerous partitions.
•
-partcomp=autopart_high-partcomp=autopart_high[partcomp=autopart_high]
-partcomp=autopart_high
Applies auto-partitioning to both modules and packages with a high threshold, which
results in larger and fewer partitions. Larger and fewer partitions take more time to
compile or elaborate than smaller and more numerous partitions.
•
-partcomp=autopart_high-partcomp=autopart_high[partcomp=autopart_high]
-partcomp=autopart_huge
Applies auto-partitioning to both modules and packages with threshold higher than
-partcomp=autopart_high, which results in much larger and very fewer partitions.
•
-partcomp=autopart_relaxh-partcomp=autopart_relax[partcomp=autopart_relax]
-partcomp=autopart_relax
Applies auto-partitioning in relax mode. Use -partcomp=autopart_relax option when
-partcomp=autopart_high gives less balanced partitions. It relaxes the partitioning
with a high threshold to get maximum gain in turnaround time.
•
-partcomp=autopartdb-partcomp=autopartdb[partcomp=autopartdb]
-partcomp=autopartdbg

Creates the

Once the partition config file is generated, it can be modified to add/delete any

Specifying Partitions in an +optconfigfile File
You specify a partition in this file with a line beginning with the keyword partition.
The keyword cell specifies that the partition is for all instances of the module name or
program block name that follows.
Example 46 Partition Compile +optconfigfile Configuration File
// +optconfigfile configuration file cfg.txt
partition cell test;
partition cell multiplier;
This configuration file specifies:
• one partition for program block test
• one partition for both instances of module multiplier
The default and unspecified partition contains the top-level module top and module adder.
Compile the design and testbench with the -partcomp option and specifying the
configuration file with the +optconfigfile option, for example:
% vcs
-partcomp top.v test.v add_mult.v \ +optconfigfile+config.txt
[other options]

Specifying Partitions in a VHDL Configuration File
VHDL and VHDL-on-top, mixed-HDL designs require a VHDL configuration file to specify
the partitions (see Example 47). The syntax and semantics of the configuration file are
the same as for a regular VHDL configuration file, with the addition of the new keyword partition
partition.
partition compileVHDL configuration
Example 47 VHDL Configuration File for Partition Compile
//file topcfg.vhd
library work;
USE STD.textio.all;
USE IEEE.STD_LOGIC_TEXTIO.all;
use IEEE.STD_LOGIC_1164.all;
use work.all;
configuration topcfg of top is
for top_arch
for partition i1: child use entity work.child(module);
end for;
end for;
The partition keyword with for all and for other clauses of a VHDL
configuration is not allowed in Partition Compile.
Analyze the VHDL configuration file along with other VHDL source files using the vhdlan
command. For example:
% vhdlan top.vhd topcfg.vhd

Adaptive Scheduling Using fastpartcomp
Adaptive scheduling helps you to work out the optimal value for fastpartcomp.In this

Turbo Compile Flow
Verification engineers change only the verification environment (testbench or tests) and
the DUT remains constant. Many engineers are involved in the design and verification of
small to large designs. Some of the common scenarios are:
• Changes are local to the testbench or the verification environment, but not in the
• Changes are local to a design, but not in the testbench or the verification environment.
Each change can lead to huge compile time. Partition compile creates partitions of the
design and the testbench that are compiled separately and enables faster compilation of
design and verification environment during incremental compile.
The incremental compile flow with partition compile does not trigger the compilation of
unused or unchanged common portions of the design or tests. Incremental compilation
is faster because it shares the compiled data from other portions of the design. Hence it
reduces compile-time and disk space consumption across multiple tests.
Also, incremental compilations can be done in parallel to further speed up the compile
turnaround time across multiple tests or multiple users in SOC designs.
At the same time, the compile areas need to be relocatable, as anything can be moved
anywhere to reduce NFS access for users.
All these can be achieved using Turbo Compile Flow with Partition Compile. It helps to
create a relocatable database along with the benefits of incremental compile with partition
compile flow.

The Partition Compile Two-Step Flow
1. Synopsys recommends using autopartitioning using the -partcomp option. This is
the default mode in partition compile flow. For more details, see the Auto-partitioning
2. You can create a partition configuration file to generate different partitions than
autopartitioning to fine-tune the performance. T

mpile flow is as follows:
% vcs -partcomp top [other options]
To specify additional partitions, use the +optconfigfile option as follows:
% vcs -partcomp top +optconfigfile+cfg.txt [other options]

For more details, refer to Step 2 of Two-Step flow.
Commonly Used Partition-Compile Options
You can use the following options for partition compile flow:-dir=<dir_name>
-dir/-partcomp_dir=<dir_name>
Generates partition information in the specified directory.-sharedlib
-sharedlib/-partcomp_sharedlib=<dir_name>
Reuses the existing partition information from the specified partition database and

Limiting Partitions
You can use the following options to limit the module and package partitions in partition
compile flow:
-partcomp=modpart_limit:N
Limits the module partitions to the specified number.
-partcomp=pkgpart_limit:N
Limits the package partitions to the specified number.
The modpart_limit and pkgpart_limit are considered as guidelines by the
VCS partitioner. The tool can still create slightly more or slightly less partitions
based on the module or package sizes and inter-dependencies.

vhdl_objs_dir

Relocation Methods with Partition Compile
VCS allows you to move the simulation executable to the location of your choice. With the
relocated database, you can get the benefit of a faster compile turnaround time by reusing
the existing partitions and compiling (relocatable compilation) or running the simulation
(relocatable simulation) in a new directory.
The following are the two methods to relocate the database in partition compile - turbo
compile flow:
• Using -simcopy Compile Time Options
• Using simcopy Utility

By default, VCS allows calling non-blocking tasks such as tasks without delay, event
control or wait statements, from within a function. For blocking task calls, an error
message is issued.
In the partition compile flow, the blocking and non-blocking nature of a task call may not
always be determined at compile-time. Compilation may complete without errors when
calling a blocking task from within a function.
You can use the -partcomp=LRM_1800_2012 compile-time option to enable checking of
stricter SystemVerilog compliant rule. When the option is specified, an error message is
issued in the partition compile flow for calling any tasks, blocking or non-blocking, from
within a function.
Scenarios Causing a Recompilation of a Partition
The following cases cause a recompilation of a partition:
• Change of a module definition in a partition, either instance- or cell-based.
• Change in VCS command-line option (addition, deletion, or sub-argument value
change).
• Change in the synopsys_sim.setup or
+optconfigfile
+optconfigfile file.
• Global design property changes like adding
$dumpvars
$dumpvars to a partition, in which case all
partitions need to be recompiled.
• Changes to the ports or parameters that affect the ports of a partition. If there is a
parent and child partition, and this change is only to the child partition, the parent need
not be recompiled.
• Changes to
$unit
$unit scope. Any change (addition of a new signal, type, module, or
interface) to a $unit causes recompilation of all the partitions associated with the
$unit.
• Changes to an interface require the recompilation of all modules connected to that
interface.
• Changes to a shared package. In this case, all the partitions sharing this package
require recompilation.
• Reanalysis of source code ( vlogan or vhdlan) with different command-line options
causes recompilation of the source code and all partitions that share the logical library.
