Support for User Accessible DRS
Support for User Accessible DRS
In order to model a Digital Mixed Signal (DMS) behavior with bidirectional ports, it is
mandatory to differentiate the “external drivers” from the “internal drivers” of a port. This
technology is referred a Driver/Receiver Segregation (DRS), which is default in Verilog-
AMS. The idea is the same as in the concept of DRS in Verilog AMS. DRS requires that
ordinary drivers and loads of a mixed signal be segregated through the digital in/out port
of a connect module. Ordinary drivers/loads, also called as external drivers/loads, are
drivers/loads outside the connect module. In contrast, connect drivers/loads, or the internal
drivers/loads are drivers/loads inside the connect module. DRS supports the following:
• All the connect loads will see the resolved value of the external drivers.
• All the external loads will see the resolved value of the connect drivers.
You must add a V2K attribute SNPS_ENABLE_DRS on a scalar wire/nettype port to enable
DRS on that port.
This provides an easy way for the user to enable DRS on a specific scalar wire or Nettype
in/out port.
The following is an example:
module l2r_bidir(l, e);
(*SNPS_ENABLE_DRS*) inout l; // enable DRS on this port
(*SNPS_ENABLE_DRS*) inout e; // enable DRS on this port

inout e;
wreal4state e;
parameter real Threshold =1.65;

reg e2l_val = 1'bz;
real l2e_val = `wrealZState;

always @(l)
l2e_val = (l === 1'bz) ? `wrealZState :
(l === 1'bx) ? `wrealXState :
l * 2.0 * Threshold;

UPF Support for SPICE-on-Top Design Configurations

always @(e)
e2l_val = (e === `wrealZState) ? 1'bz :
(e === `wrealXState) ? 1'bx :
(e > Threshold ) ? 1 :
0;
1. You can only add the attribute SNPS_ENABLE_DRS on a scalar wire or nettype inout port
of a module that is not a connect module.
2. Embedded DRS is not allowed, that is, you cannot have the attribute
SNPS_ENABLE_DRS on two hierarchically connect port nodes one of which is an
ancestor of the other.
3. You cannot connect a bidirectional switch gate or a spice instance to a port with the
attribute SNPS_ENABLE_DRS hierarchically.
UPF Support for SPICE-on-Top Design Configurations
In SPICE-on-top design topologies, the top level of a design is modeled in analog
languages (such as Spice/Spectre). Digital blocks are instantiated under the Spice. In
Spice, the supplies are typically created in the subckt definition only, while supply network
for digital blocks is present in the UPF file. In such a design configuration, the supply may
be generated from Spice which may then be connected to the UPF supply network to
propagate supplies to digital blocks of the design.
The following commands are used to set the connectivity between the external driver and
the UPF supply net:
upf_port_connect
Syntax:
upf_port_connect -cell <Cell_name> -inst<inst_name> (<upf_port> =>
<spice_port>) ;
upf_port_connect -cell TopDig
-inst X1 (VDDL=>vdd12);
upf_port_map

Globally Merged Auto-Inserted-Connect Module (AICM) Optimization
When the ports do not match by name to the UPF created supply ports, then the
recommendation is to use the following upf_port_map option:
Syntax:
use_verilog -module <module_name> upf_port_map (<upf_port> ==>
<spice_port>) ;
use_verilog -module TopDig \
upf_port_map (VDDL => sp1, VDD => sp2, VSS => sp3)

Globally Merged Auto-Inserted-Connect Module (AICM)
Optimization
In the Verilog-AMS flow, the interfaces between analog and digital blocks are realized by
the automatic insertion of connect modules. These insertions are guided by Verilog-AMS
connect-insertion statements. A single connect module instance may be inserted between
a net and a set of ports (where the net was originally connected to) if the connect-mode of
the corresponding connect-insertion statement is specified as ‘merged’.

Globally Merged Auto-Inserted-Connect Module (AICM) Optimization
Besides, merged mode insertion takes place only when the net and the set of mixed-signal
port connections are in the same module. If there is another mixed-signal port connection
that is in a different module, then the same connect module instance is not shared with
the other port connection as well although the high-conn of the other port connection is
hierarchically connected to the same net.
This feature extends the merged mode connect module insertion across multiple mixed-
signal port connections that may be present in different modules when the high-conn of
these port connections are all hierarchically connected to the same net.
Merged Mode Connect Module Insertion as Per Verilog-AMS LRM
As per Verilog-AMS LRM, a single connect module is inserted between a high-conn net
and a set of mixed-signal port connections if the ‘merged’ insertion mode is specified in the
respective connect-insertion statement.

Support for the Bind Feature in Mixed-Signal Simulation
Support for the Bind Feature in Mixed-Signal Simulation
In the Eldo SPICE netlist format, the .bind command is used to map a sub-circuit with
another sub-circuit. VCS supports this command in the Mixed Signal Verification (MSV)
flow as well.
The syntax of the .bind command is as follows:
.bind inst=< full_instance_name> from_subckt=< subckt_name>
to_subckt=<subckt_name> default_mapping=< mapping_method>
The command options are:
• inst: Specifies the full name of the instance thats needs sub-circuit definition
replacement. Wildcard is not supported.
from_subckt: Specifies the original sub-circuit definition.
to_subckt: Specifies the new sub-circuit definition that is used to replace the sub-
circuit given in from_subckt.
default_mapping: Specifies the mapping method. Only the BY_POSITION method is
supported. The BY_NAME method is not supported
• When using the command, check if the node names of the replacement sub-
circuit and the original sub-circuit match.
• VCS reports an error and stops the simulation if there is a mismatch in node
names or count.
System Functions to Access Analog Voltage and Port Current
Mixed-signal simulation supports different techniques for accessing analog signals within a
mixed analog-digital design:
• Verilog language cross module referencing (XMR)
• $hdl_xmr_force and $hdl_xmr_release in Verilog, and hdl_xmr_force and
hdl_xmr_release in VHDL
• $snps_get_volt and $snps_get_port_current Verilog system functions
• UCLI get command

System Functions to Access Analog Voltage and Port Current
VCS supports three system functions, $msv_is_analog_node, $msv_get_voltage, and
$msv_get_current, for accessing analog voltage and current values from analog nodes
within a mixed-signal simulation. These system functions have more benefits over the
other AMS XMR solutions listed above.
For example, you can use a string variable as an argument for the path to the probed
node, which you cannot do in the $snps_* functions. Similarly, the $msv_get_voltage
and $msv_get_current system functions return a real number value that represents the
voltage or current, unlike the $hdl_xmr commands.
Prerequisite
To use the $msv_is_analog_node, $msv_get_voltage, and $msv_get_current system
functions, specify the -lca option while running VCS.
The syntax of the $msv_is_analog_node, $msv_get_voltage, and $msv_get_current
system functions is as follows:
Syntax Description
$msv_is_analog_node ( node_path) Returns 1 if node_path points to an analog node
(electrical, branch, SPICE node, and so on).
Otherwise, returns 0.
$msv_get_voltage ( node_path) Returns the voltage for an analog node as a real
value. If node_path is not an analog node, the
system function generates the following error
message and returns 0.0.
Error: failed to find analog object
'node_path' in top-level scope
$msv_get_current ( node_path) Returns the current for an analog node as a real
value. If node_path is not an analog node, the

upply specification that targets a lower-level
component, overrides this data.
VCS supports supply routing via Verilog-AMS netlist through inherited connection and
associates this supply with the connect module instances and the SPICE or Verilog-AMS
blocks that need this information for simulation purposes. However, in several Verilog-AMS
designs, attribute-based syntax, embedded into the RTL source is used to achieve the
same task. This feature supports an attribute-based inherited connection solution using
the ams_supply, ams_cdef_net, and ams_cdef_inst commands.
Supply Sensitivity and Ground Sensitivity for a Connect Module
A connect module is used to convert between analog and digital values at an analog/
digital boundary. For analog to digital conversion, it typically depends on some threshold
value that in turn usually depends on the power-supply of the analog signal. On the other
hand, for digital to analog conversion, a logic value (‘0’ or ‘1’) typically translates to an
analog value depending upon the power-supply of the digital signal.

snps_cm_power attribute refers to the power-node whereas the snps_cm_ground attribute
refers to the ground-node.

Attribute-Based Inherited Connection and Supply Sensitivity
connectmodule l2e (din, aout);
input din;
logical din;
output aout;
electrical aout;
(* snps_cm_power = "global_module.vdd" *) electrical vdd;
(* snps_cm_ground = "global_module.vss" *) electrical vss;
In the above example, two local nodes vdd and vss within connect module 12e have
power and ground information. Node vdd is supply-sensitive because it has the
snps_cm_power attribute. On the other hand, vss is the ground-sensitive node because
it has the snps_cm_ground attribute. These supply nodes (vdd and vss) may be used to
model the analog to digital or digital to analog conversions accurately.
Supply Sensitivity and Ground Sensitivity for an Ordinary Module
The snps_ams_supply_digital_port_power and
snps_ams_supply_digital_port_ground attributes can be specified on the digital ports
of an ordinary module, and these attributes can override the value of the corresponding
snps_cm_power and snps_cm_ground attributes within a connect module.
module bot (p1, p2);
(* snps_ams_supply_digital_port_power = "global_module.vddBot";
snps_ams_supply_digital_port_ground = "global_module.vssBot" *)
input p1;
In the above example, the snps_ams_supply_digital_port_power and
snps_ams_supply_digital_port_ground attributes have been provided on the
digital port p1 of the ordinary module bot. If a connect module is connected to this
port p1, then global_module.vddBot overrides the snps_cm_power attribute and
global_module.vssBot overrides the snps_cm_ground attribute of this connect module.
You can achieve the same functionality by using the ams_supply command as follows:
File: vcsAD.init
ams_supply -cell bot -digital_port {p1} -supply
{port_power=>global_module.vddBot, port_ground=>global_module.vssBot}
Inherited Connection
An inherited connection is a combination of ‘property-name’ and ‘default-property-value’. It
can be defined on a local electrical node inside an ordinary module or a connect module.
Once defined, this local node is bound to that ‘property-name’ and has the corresponding
‘default-property-value’ unless there is an instance-level override for that ‘property-name’
as explained in the following sections.

(* snps_ams_cdef_net_property_name = "mygnd";
snps_ams_cdef_net_default_value = "global_module.vssBot" *)
electrical vssLocal;
In the above example, vddLocal and vssLocal are two local electrical nodes inside the
ordinary module bot. Here, vddLocal and vssLocal are bound to the property-names
mypwr and mygnd, respectively. The snps_ams_supply_digital_port_power attribute on
port p1 points to node vddLocal, whereas the snps_ams_supply_digital_port_ground
attribute on port p1 refers to vssLocal.
The above diagram shows that through the combination of inherited-connection-property
mypwr + snps_ams_supply_digital_port_power attribute, the supply of port p1 is
connected to global_module.vddBot.
Similarly, it also shows that through the combination of inherited-connection-property
mygnd + snps_ams_supply_digital_port_ground attribute, the ground of port p1 is
connected to global_module.vssBot.
You can achieve the same functionality with the ams_supply and ams_cdef_net
commands as follows:
File: vcsAD.init
ams_supply -cell bot -digital_port {p1} -supply {port_power=>vddLocal,
port_ground=>vssLocal}
ams_cdef_net -cell bot -net {vddLocal} -default_supply
{mypwr=>global_module.vddBot}
ams_cdef_net -cell bot -net {vssLocal} -default_supply
{mygnd=>global_module.vssBot}

(* snps_ams_cdef_inst = {"gnd:mygnd"};
gnd = "global_module.vss1" *) BOT (w1, w2);

In the above example, inherited-connection properties mypwr and gnd on instance
MID1 are specified here: snps_ams_cdef_inst = {"mypwr", "gnd"} . Inherited-
connection property gnd on instance BOT is overridden here: snps_ams_cdef_inst =
{"gnd:mygnd"}. Here, gnd is also renamed to mygnd.
You can achieve the same functionality with the ams_supply, ams_cdef_net, and
ams_cdef_inst commands as follows:
File: vcsAD.init
ams_supply -cell bot -digital_port {p1} -supply {port_power=>vddLocal,
port_ground=>vssLocal}
ams_cdef_net -cell bot -net {vddLocal} -default_supply
{mypwr=>global_module.vddBot}

Support for Packed Type of Wreal/Nettype/Real/Integer
ams_cdef_net -cell bot -net {vssLocal} -default_supply
{mygnd=>global_module.vssBot}
ams_cdef_inst -cell top -inst {MID1} -supply {gnd=>global_module.vss,
mypwr=>global_module.vdd}
ams_cdef_inst -cell mid -inst {BOT} -supply
{gnd:mygnd=>global_module.vss1}
You must use the following compile-time option to enable this feature:
%vcs -adopt ams_cdef_attrib
For more information about the ams_supply, ams_cdef_net, and ams_cdef_inst
commands, refer to the Inherited-Connection-Based Supply Specification for Verilog-AMS
Designs section in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Support for Packed Type of Wreal/Nettype/Real/Integer
In Verilog-AMS, the packed vector of nettype/wreal/real/integer is used frequently. Support
for a packed vector of these types is required to compile and simulate generated netlist.
These types are inherently unpacked in nature, so you must convert the packed vector of
these types to the unpacked array internally.
VCS AMS supports packed vector of nettype (both built-in and user-defined) using the
-xlrm nettype_array XLRM option.
Two-Step Flow
vcs -sverilog -xlrm nettype_array
Three-Step Flow
vlogan -sverilog -xlrm nettype_array
The following coding styles are supported with the -xlrm nettype_array option:
• wreal [3:0] a;
• th_wire[3:0] b;
• int [3:0] c;
• real [3:0] d;

Configuring the Converters Through ams_cm Command
The -xlrm nettype_array option only enables support for packed arrays of
the listed constructs. It does not enable support for the constructs themselves.
Data types int and real are built-in data types of SystemVerilog, whereas
wreal and th_wire are not. You can enable wreal net support (see the
“Support for Wreal Nets” section in the VCS User Guide) , however, it is
recommended to use native SystemVerilog user-defined nettypes instead of
wreal nets. Commonly used SystemVerilog user-defined nettypes, including
th_wire, are available in the following Synopsys MSV package:
$VCS_HOME/etc/snps_msv/snps_msv_nettype_pkg.svp
Configuring the Converters Through ams_cm Command
The ams_cm command enables parameter overrides of the datatype converters used in
analog mixed-signal designs and digital mixed-signal designs.
To fine-tune the accuracy of type conversions, it is allowed to override the parameters of a
set of auto-inserted converter instances in the design. Refer to the following figure:
Figure 66 Overriding the Parameters of a Set of Auto-inserted Converter

Configuring the Converters Through ams_cm Command
ams_cm converter_module_parameter_name=parameter_value
[library=library_name]
[cell=cell_name [node=node_name]]
[inst=instance_hierarchical_name [node=node_name]]
[node=node_hierarchical_name];
converter_module_parameter_name=parameter_value
Specifies the converter module parameter and the value to which it is set. The
parameter_value can be either real or string type. If you specify override information for a
nonexistent parameter of a converter module, then that override is ignored.
library=library_name
Specifies the name of the logical library of the cell for which the converter module is
inserted.
cell=cell_name [node=node_name]
Specifies the cell or cell/node names for which the converter module is inserted or
connected. The node name is optional; if it is not specified, all nodes of a given cell are
considered.
inst=instance_hierarchical_name [node=node_name]
Specifies the hierarchical instance name or hierarchical-instance-name/node names for
which the converter module is inserted or connected. The node name is optional; if it is not
specified, all nodes of a given instance are considered.
node=node_hierarchical_name
Specifies the hierarchical node name for which the converter module is inserted or
connected
There is no change in the existing use model for RNM simulation. To specify the ams_cm
option on the ports, use the -adopt port_based_ams_cm command.

Configuring the Converters Through ams_cm Command
• The ams_cm option in the VCS optconfig file allows you to override converter
parameters only.
• VerilogAMS flow:
◦ The ams_cm commands in the VCS optconfig file are applicable to converter
instances only (these are not applicable to any connectmodule instance).
◦ The ams_cm commands in the vcsAD.init file continue to configure the
connectmodule instances only.
The following is an exampl

module LevelShifter ( input wreal4state wr_21, output wreal4state wr_35);
//… … …
The commands used are:
vlogan -sverilog converter.v test.v
vcs top -sverilog -wreal res_def -xlrm enable_converter
+optconfigfile+cfg
./simv
The ams_cm commands in the VCS optconfig file allow you to override the converter
parameters only:
• Overriding converter insertion rule is not supported.
• Overriding converter insertion mode (merge/split) is not supported.
• SuperNet is not supported.
• Arguments of the ams_cm command do not support wildcard notation.

Parameterization of Converters Using Hierarchical Tracing
Parameterization of Converters Using Hierarchical Tracing
In Real Number Modeling (RNM) simulation, converters are inserted at port boundaries
where the port type differs from the connected signal type. Configuring these converters
requires users to specify ams_cm commands in the VCS OptConfig file. However,
the current approach only looks upward in the hierarchy to identify applicable ams_cm
commands. This limitation can lead to errors in multi-voltage designs or designs with
complex hierarchical connections.
The enhanced hierarchical tracing feature addresses this limitation by enabling a tracing
algorithm that not only looks upward for the applicable ams_cm command, but also checks
the interconnected segments in the adjacent hierarchies to handle the feedthrough
scenarios.
This feature is applicable to:
• Digital portion of the design and does not trace through analog or Unified Power
Format (UPF) portions.
• Coercion flow under the -coerce switch.
To enable traversal algorithm, add the following command to the OptConfig file:
ams_converter_parameterization=traversal;
By default, the value is set to upscoping, which uses the upward-only tracing method.
After enabling traversal algorithm, use any of the following syntaxes to define the ams_cm
command:
ams_cm inst=<hier_inst_name> node=<node_name>;
Or,
ams_cm node=<hier_node_name>;
If the ams_cm command is defined as {cell=<cell_name> node=<node>} along with
inst=<inst_name> node=<node>} or {node=<hier_node>} then inst-node/node path
takes precedence.
The following is the limitation of this feature:
• Bit-specific ams_cm commands are not supported.

Dumping of Attributes Not Understood by VCS
Dumping of Attributes Not Understood by VCS
In previous releases, VCS did not understand some of the netlisted modules written in
Verilog-AMS or SystemVerilog languages that have attributes defined with a syntax that is
not compliant with Verilog-AMS or SystemVerilog LRM.
Starting with this release, VCS performs the following:
• Reports all the attributes that are not understood by VCS in a text file, and ignores
them during compilation. VCS also generates warning messages for every occurrence
of the attribute that are not understood by VCS.
• Supports execution of a general-purpose pre-elaboration user script.
• Reads the commands generated by the user-defined script before mixed-signal
elaboration.
To enable this feature, do the following:
Two-Step Flow
1. Use the -lca option.
2. Use the ams_xlrm_netlist command in the optconfigfile file.
Three-Step Flow
1. Use the -lca option.
2. Use the ams_xlrm_netlist command in the optconfigfile file.
3. Use the vlogan -xlrm ams option to enable vlogan to parse unknown attributes.
The syntax of the ams_xlrm_netlist command is as follows:
ams_xlrm_netlist
-constructs attributes
[ -warning_file_format txt ] ;
-constructs attributes
Specifies type of constructs not supported by VCS that require a dedicated warnings file.
attributes constructs are covered by this specification.
-warning_file_format txt
Specifies the format of the VCS-generated warnings file.

Dumping of Attributes Not Understood by VCS

Pre-Elaboration Script
VCS supports an execution of a general-purpose pre-elaboration script that users provide.
The script is invoked after source files compilation and before AMS elaboration. It is
invoked by the pre_elaboration_script command in the optconfigfile file when the
-ams option is used in VCS.
The pre_elaboration_script command is operational only when the
ams_xlrm_netlist command is run and unknown attributes are detected in the netlist.
The syntax of the pre_elaboration_script command is as follows:
pre_elaboration_script
-file relative_path_to_script
[ -abort_compilation_after_script_execution < yes | no > ] ;
-file relative_path_to_script
Specifies a relative path to an executable user script.
-abort_compilation_after_script_execution yes
VCS compilation stops when the execution of the user script is complete. This is used only
for debugging purposes.
-abort_compilation_after_script_execution no
VCS compilation continues when the execution of the user script is complete.

Support for Multiplicity Factor Parameter
If an option is not specified, no is the default value of the

, this option forces a resolved value of an
M-factor to be written into a local parameter parameter_name of datatype real within a
selected cell. It is illegal to use this option with the -local_inst key.
-local_inst {{ name_of_a_local_instance }* }
Scoping option to define a target instance within the selected cell.
-param_override parameter_name
This option enables VCS to take a value specified in an existing Verilog-AMS parameter
override statement and use it as an M-factor for a given instance.
The parameter override statement can be declared on an instance even if no such
parameter is declared within the module. You cannot specify this option without specifying
the -local_inst key.
-value value
Specifies a value of the M-factor for the selected object. If -param_override is also
specified, its value is substituted with -value value.
Return Value
Incorrect commands are reported in the VCS log file.
ams_mfactor -lib "libA" -cell "LDO" -value 15;
ams_mfactor -lib "libA" -cell {"LDO","DCDC"} -value 15;
ams_mfactor -lib "libA" -cell {"LDO","DCDC"} -param_resolved
"mfactor_eff";
ams_mfactor -lib "libA" -cell "LDO" -local_inst {"I1","I2"} -value 15;
ams_mfactor -lib "libA" -cell "LDO" -local_inst {"I1","I2"}
-param_override "multi";
In the above example,
ams_mfactor -lib "libA" -cell "LDO" -value 15 defines an M-factor 15 for all
instance within cell LDO.
ams_mfactor -lib "libA" -cell {"LDO","DCDC"} -value 15; defines an M-factor
15 for all instance within cells LDO and DCDC.
ams_mfactor -lib "libA" -cell {"LDO","DCDC"} -param_resolved
"mfactor_eff"; defines the parameter mfacto_eff of cells LDO and DCDC to be forced to
a value of an effective M-factor value in those scopes.
ams_mfactor -lib "libA" -cell "LDO" -local_inst {"I1","I2"} -value 15;
defines an M-factor 15 for instances I1 and I2 within cell LDO of library libA.

Support for Multiplicity Factor Parameter
ams_mfactor -lib "libA" -cell "LDO" -local_inst {"I1","I2"}
-param_override "multi"; defines an M-factor instance level override as a reference to
a parameter override statement located (assumed to be located) at instances I1 and I2 of
cell LDO.
V2K Alternative to ams_mfactor
Define the following two equivalent attributes (that are supposed to be defined in Verilog-
AMS or SystemVerilog netlist) to enable embedding such attributes in the netlist.
• (* snps_ams_mfactor_override = 10 *) is used to define an M-factor value of an
instance.
• (* snps_ams_mfactor_resolved *) is used to define a parameter of datatype real to

To get access to the value of the attribute for debugging purposes, you must use an

(* snps_ams_mfactor_override = 10 *) test_mfactor I1(a,c);
(* snps_ams_mfactor_override = 2 *) test_mfactor I2(a,c);

parameter real m=0.1;
real rs;

analog begin
rs = $mfactor * 100.0;
$strobe ("m = %g, $mfactor = %g, rs = %g", m, $mfactor, rs);

The following are the limitations of the name mapping between SPICE view and digital
view for XMR feature:
• Supports only XMRs written in RTL/HDL files. The XMRs specified on the UCLI
command prompt, Verdi windows, or other interfaces are not handled.
• Designed exclusively for RTVS flows and does not extend to general MSV flows.
• Extends support only to name mapping based on X-prefix, case sensitivity, port map, or
bus format of the original XMR.
Automatic Handling of Verilog Force on Mixed-Signal Nets
The force statement in SystemVerilog is a continuous procedural assignment on a net.
When you apply a force statement to a net, it overrides all other drivers to that net.
In simulation, a force statement is used in conjunction with a release statement. The
release statement ends the driver override that was applied on the net through the force
statement.
The behavior of Verilog force/release on a mixed-signal net is now enhanced such that the
Verilog force becomes the only driver for the Spice net. That is, in case of a Verilog force,
the force value is sent to the analog side, and the analog engine considers it as the only
contribution to the respective Spice net. This force value is maintained on the Spice net
until a Verilog release happens on that mixed-signal net.
With this enhancement, a force command is applied the same way as in Verilog, by fully
overriding other analog drivers. When a force is applied to a digital segment of a mixed-
signal net, this information is passed to the analog side to ‘force’ an analog segment of the
net. This tracing also works in the backward (a -> d) direction.
To enable this feature, you must use the -adopt msv_force_release compile option.
The following examples describe this feature in detail:
• Verilog Force on a Spice Net
• Verilog Force on a Digital Net Connected to Spice
• Verilog Force on a Digital Net Connected to Spice Through Select

Leaf-Level Verilog-AMS Support in the SystemVerilog-Spice Flow
Leaf-Level Verilog-AMS Support in the SystemVerilog-Spice Flow
VCS MSV supports SystemVerilog-Spice flow having a leaf-level Verilog-AMS
(VAMS) module to be used as an electrical instrument. You must use the -adopt
msv_with_leaf_vams compile option to enable the leaf-level Verilog-AMS support. This
feature only supports VAMS block at the leaf level of the hierarchy in the SV-Spice flow.

Leaf-Level Verilog-AMS Support in the SystemVerilog-Spice Flow
Figure 67 Leaf-Level Verilog-AMS Support
This feature allows leaf-level VAMS source files to be used as electrical instruments. A
leaf-level VAMS does not allow any hierarchy or analog primitives.
The following is the use model of leaf-level Verilog-AMS support in VCS two-step and
three-step flows:
Two-step flow:
% vcs +verilogamsext+.vams test.vams -sverilog test.v -adopt
msv_with_leaf_vams -ad=test.init
Three-step flow:
% vlogan -sverilog test.v
% vlogan -ams test.vams
% vcs -ad=test.init -sverilog top -adopt msv_with_leaf_vams
Consider the following files:
test.sv
reg in , out ;
initial in =0 ;

test.vams
`include "disciplines.vams"
module ana (in , out);
input in ;
output out;
electrical in , out ;
analog begin
V(out) <+ V(in) ;
end
test.init
choose xa ;
Execute the following commands:
% vcs +verilogamsext+.vams test.vams -sverilog test.sv -adopt
msv_with_leaf_vams -ad=test.init -full64

Bidirectional-Island
Bidirectional-island for an INOUT port is identified by the complete set of net segments
that are directly or indirectly connected to the port signal through port-connections and
aliases.
For example, in the following figure, there are two bidirectional-islands: Bidir-Island
#1 and Bidir-Island #2 . Both bidirectional-islands contain three different types of
interconnected net segments: wire, wrealmin, and wrealmax.
Figure 68 Multi-Voltage Design
Most Accurate Representative Type
Consider a design with a set of net segments interconnected by INOUT ports and aliases.
Let the types of these segments are NT1, NT2, …, NTn and are different from each other.
Out of these n different types, if the NTx type is most accurate, then NTx is considered as
the Most Accurate Representative (MAR) type.
Bidirectional-Island Processing: Super-Net Formation
In a bidirectional-island, all net segments of the same type are aliased to form one single
net for that respective type.
The following figure is an example of super-net formation for a bidirectional-island.

Figure 69 Super-Net Formation for a Bidirectional-Island
The bidirectional-island in Figure 69 contains three different net types: NT1, NT2, and NT3.
• NT1: This net type has two segments. These two segments are aliased to form a single
net of type NT1.
• NT2: This net type has two segments. These two segments are aliased to form a single
net of type NT2.
• NT3: This type has only one segment.
In Figure 69, after aliasing there are three nets in the bidirectional-island (one net for each
type). Also, two net segments, connected through INOUT ports having different types, are
disconnected from each other. This is shown as Disconnection-1, Disconnection-2,
and so on in Figure 69.
After MAR information is available for a bidirectional-island, the Super-Net can be formed
for this island. If NT3 is the MAR in this example, the Super-Net contains the following
unidirectional converters (unidirectional converters from each non-MAR to MAR, and vice
versa):
• Non-MAR to MAR ( NT1_to_NT3 and NT3_to_NT1)
• MAR to Non-MAR ( NT2_to_NT3 and NT3_to_NT2)

Scope-Based Type-Coercion Use Cases
The scope-based type-coercion is implemented in the following use cases:
Refer to the following example to understand these uses cases.
Use Case 1: Additive Nature of ams_coercion Commands
ams_coercion -mode ON -inst { top.mid1 };
ams_coercion -mode ON -inst { top.mid2 };
The two commands are equivalent to the following single command:
ams_coercion -mode ON -inst { top.mid1, top.mid2 };
Use Case 2: Transitive Nature of ams_coercion Command
ams_coercion -mode OFF -inst { top.mid1 };
Type-coercion is turned OFF for the instance top.mid1 and the hierarchy below.
Use Case 3: Lower-Level ams_coercion Command Overrides the Command From its
Upper Level
ams_coercion -mode OFF -cell mid;
ams_coercion -mode ON -cell bot;
ams_coercion -mode ON -inst { top.mid1.leaf1 };
The first command disables type-coercion for all instances of the mid cell and its sub-
hierarchy, except for the following two scenarios:
• When the second command enables type-coercion for all instances of the bot cell
( top.mid1.bot1 and top.mid2.bot1), thereby overriding the higher level first
command for this particular scope.
• When the third command enables type-coercion specifically for the instance
top.mid1.leaf1, thereby overriding the higher level first command for this particular
scope.
Use Case 4: Instance Level Commands Take Priority Over Cell Level Commands

ams_coercion -mode OFF -cell mid;
ams_coercion -mode ON -inst { top.mid1 };
The first command disables type-coercion for all instances of the mid cell and their sub-
hierarchy.
The second command explicitly enables type-coercion for the instance top.mid1,
overriding the cell level command.
Use Case 5: Conflicting ams_coercion Commands
ams_coercion -mode ON -cell mid_mod;
ams_coercion -mode OFF -cell mid_mod;///Error
A conflict arises when contradictory commands are issued for the same cell. In this case,
an error is generated to prevent ambiguity.
Use Case 6: Usage of the -override Option
• Scenario 1: Instance Level -override Command
ams_coercion -mode OFF -cell leaf;
ams_coercion -mode ON -inst { top.mid1 } -override;
The second command overrides the first, enabling type-coercion for the top.mid1
hierarchy, including instances of the leaf cell within it (for example, top.mid1.leaf1).

Optimizing Verilog-AMS Auto-Inserted ConnectModules (AICMs)
Using Built-in Interface Elements
In mixed-signal designs, connectmodules (also called Interface Elements or IEs) convert
signals between different disciplines—for example, from a digital logic value to an analog
electrical value (voltage/current) and vice versa. These conversions are guided by the
Verilog-AMS (VAMS) Language Reference Manual (LRM) connect-insertion rules.
In the VCS VAMS flow, interfaces between analog and digital blocks are realized by
automatically inserting connectmodules during the elaboration phase. VCS detects
mismatched ports on the same node and inserts the appropriate ConnectModule(CM)
based on connect rules.

Connectmodules can be inserted in:
• Merged Mode (default): If a single net of one discipline (for example, analog) connects
to multiple ports of another discipline (for example, digital), VCS inserts only one
instance of the connectmodule. All destination ports share the converted signal from
this single instance.
• Split Mode: Each mismatched port gets its own connectmodule instance. This mode is
less common and generally less efficient.

VAMS designs.
% vlogan -full64 -ams test.vams -sverilog

The following sections describe this feature in detail:
• Properties of Synopsys Built-in Interface Elements
• Optimization Criteria
• Analog Island Optimization
Properties of Synopsys Built-in Interface Elements
The following are the properties of the Synopsys built-in interface element:
• Managed by VCS/PrimeSim
• Support only built-in digital data types
• Independent of Verilog-AMS discipline definitions
• Faster execution and smaller memory footprint compared to VAMS connectmodules
• Inserted in Merged mode only to maximize performance
• Conversion functionality is controlled via:
◦ The ie and resistance-map commands in the vcsAD.init file.
◦ Automatic VDD tracing managed by VCS.
• Driver Receiver Segregation (DRS) happens at the digital port of a connectmodule
to segregate connect-driver from connect-receiver. Bi-directional (inout) built-in IEs
support DRS functionality (that is, analog simulator determines the final value of the
mixed-signal net).

Optimization Criteria
The following criteria must be met to optimize VAMS connectmodule instances using built-
in interface elements:
• The analog-digital boundary data type must be supported by the interface element.
• CM insertion mode must be merged, not split.
• CM instance must be auto-inserted (not manual).
• Mutual Exclusion Rules:
◦ A net cannot have both an IE and a CM. A mixed-signal can either have a
connectmodule or interface element, not both.
◦ If any connection on a mixed-signal net fails the criteria, optimization does not occur
for that net.

Dynamic Reconfiguration at Runtime
As designs grow in size, memory consumption and simulation speed become crucial
factors in design verification. In general, tests and stimulus are targeted and generated for
specific parts of a design. These tests and stimulus exercise a large portion of the design
while the rest of the design becomes inactive during simulation. Dynamic reconfiguration
at runtime provides a flexible mechanism to substitute portions of a design hierarchy with
empty models at runtime. This feature enables different design configurations to be used
for simulations without recompiling the design.

and their sub-hierarchies are replaced by an empty module at runtime.
The dynamic reconfiguration at runtime feature is described in the following sections:
• Support with VCS Native Low Power
• Dynamic Reconfiguration in a Mixed Signal Flow
• Support for Cross-Module References of Multidimensional Arrays
• Restrictions
This section describes the use model for dynamic reconfiguration. It provides the steps
to specify an alternate module that is instantiated in place of the original sub-hierarchy.

This ensures that designs do not reach an unknown state when you replace portions of the
hierarchy at runtime.
1. Compile-time
At compile time, specify the list of modules that has the potential of not being
elaborated at runtime. In addition, for each such module, provide an alternate module,
which gets bound if an instance is not elaborated. This alternate module must be
provided during the design compilation phase. During compilation, these alternate
modules are treated as top-level modules by VCS because they are not explicitly
instantiated in the design.
In this document, the module that can be deleted is referred to as the “original module”.
The alternate module is referred to as the “substitute module”.
To specify the original module and the substitute module, the configuration file
mechanism in VCS is enhanced with the following entry.
replace module {<original module>} with module {<substitute module>};
Configuration files can be specified to VCS with the +optconfigfile
+<config file name> arguments.
2. Runtime
At runtime, specify the actual instance paths that should not be elaborated by VCS
during runtime simulation. The hierarchical path names should be specified in a file.
The path of the file path can be provided to simv using the following option:
-dynaconfig <file name>

During the design compilation phase, you must provide both the original and substitute

% vcs +optconfigfile+ compile_config_file_name \

Dynamic Reconfiguration in a Mixed Signal Flow
original_module.v substitute_module.v \
-upf original_module.upf
With respect to the VCS Native Low Power (NLP), the following simulation behavior
applies:
• Power-down semantics: Power-down corruption would be instrumented for both the
original and substitute modules. Though the power-down corruption instrumentation is
done for substitute modules, you must not see any corruption behavior at runtime.
• Isolation semantics: Isolation would not get instrumented for the substitute modules
except when you specify the isolation as parent or fanout. You must not observe any
isolation on the ports/pins of the substituted modules except when the isolation location
is parent or fanout.
• Retention semantics: No retention would be instrumented for the substitute modules.
You must not observe any registers being retained in the substituted module.
The following restrictions apply if you use dynamic reconfiguration flow with VCS NLP:
• Though the substituted modules are simulated without Low power semantics, still
runtime low power messages related to the power domain are generated.
• If power domain related control signals like switch, isolation control are present in the
original module and got replaced with the substitute module, then all those control
signals gets “Z” value, and related runtime low power messages are generated
accordingly.
Dynamic Reconfiguration in a Mixed Signal Flow
You can use dynamic reconfiguration in a mixed signal verification, but only if the analog
(SPICE or Verilog-A) part of the mixed signal design is entirely in the active, stimulated,
and unchanged part of the design.

Dynamic Reconfiguration in a Mixed Signal Flow
• Cross-module references (XMRs) from analog side of mixed signal boundary to the
replaced side of the dynamic reconfiguration boundary are not supported.
• Analog tunnel re-analysis cannot happen when a Verilog module is replaced at runtime
using dynamic reconfiguration. All the connectivity analysis happens at compile-time
and therefore runtime changes from dynamic reconfiguration is not reflected in this
analysis.
The use model for using the dynamic reconfiguration at runtime feature in a mixed signal
design is a combination of the use models for dynamic reconfiguration and mixed signal
verification. The following are the steps in the combined use model:
1. Write substitute empty module definitions to replace the top-level modules of the sub-
hierarchies that are inactive for a series of tests.
2. Write a compile-time configuration file for dynamic reconfiguration that specifies:
◦ the original module definitions of the top-level module instances in the inactive sub-
hierarchies
◦ the substitute empty module definitions that replace the originals at runtime
3. Write a setup file for the analog part of the mixed signal design.
4. Compile the digital part of the design, specifying three things:
◦ compiling for dynamic reconfiguration with the compile-time configuration
file specified with the following option: +optconfigfile+compile-
time_config_file_name
◦ compiling for mixed signal simulation and specifying the setup file with the following
option: -ad=setup_file
◦ the source files for the module definitions in the design and the source files for the
empty substitute modules
The vcs command line has the following syntax:
% vcs +optconfigfile+ compile-time_config_file_name \ -ad=setup_file
top_module_of_design.v original_module.v \ substitute_module.v

The feature has the following limitations:
• MDAs for interface type object across partial elaboration are not supported.
• Only top-down absolute XMRs in substitute modules are allowed to access object in
the fixed part of the design.
• Original module of partial elaboration hierarchy can have reference to the upward XMR
or the module XMR. These XMRs are valid if no replacement happens at simulation
time. If the substitute module has upward XMR, then VCS generates compile-time
error.
• XMRs with target inside partial elaboration hierarchy do not have value if the module is
replaced at simulation time. If original module is used at simulation time, then values of
XMR are updated.
• The substitute module that do not have any instance in fixed part of the design are
instantiated as a dummy top-level instance at simulation time.
• Only XMRs to scalars. vectors, and MDA across the dynamic reconfiguration boundary
are allowed. All other complex types result in compile-time XMR error conditions.
If replacement happens any XMR reading from the replaced hierarchy returns Z (high
impedance). Even if the replacement module instance matches with the XMR path, the
XMR does not get resolved in the new instance.
• The ports of the original and substitute modules must be the same in terms of:
◦ Direction
◦ Size (bit-width and number of dimensions)
◦ Data type
There is no requirement that the corresponding ports have the same name.

VCS NLP Features
This chapter describes the following VCS Native Low Power (VCS NLP)

reset option acts either as a set or reset
of the isolation cell based on the clamp value set by the -async_clamp_value option
(clamp value is 0 for reset and 1 for set)
• The net_name is the name of the control signal which acts as the set or reset. Its type
is similar to -isolation_signal and can be either port, pin, or net. The sensitivity is
specified using the high or low keyword.
• The -async_clamp_value option specifies whether the -async_set_reset option acts
as a set or reset.
• When -async_clamp_value is 0, net_name acts as a reset of the isolation cell.
• When -async_clamp_value is 1, net_name acts as a set of the isolation cell.
• Specifying -async_clamp_value is optional. The clamp value can also be set using a
port attribute.
• The -async_set_reset and -async_clamp_value options can be specified with
-update. They can occur in any order.
Using Port Attribute
If you do not want the control pin to act as a set or reset while specifying the strategy, you
can use the UPF_async_clamp_value port attribute. In this case, the same control pin
may get connected to some cells which have set and other cells which have reset pin.
set_port_attributes -ports {p1} -attribute {UPF_async_clamp_value 0/1 }
This attribute is applicable when -async_set_reset option is specified. For an isolation
strategy with -async_set_reset option and without a -async_clamp_value option, VCS
NLP uses the specified clamp value in the port attribute.
If there is a conflict between -async_clamp_value and the UPF_async_clamp_value
attribute, a warning message is issued and the UPF_async_clamp_value attribute is used
for behavior.

Support to Allow Internal Direction for Supply Port
Error and Warning Conditions
The following are the error and warning conditions:
• An error message is issued when -async_set_reset is specified and -clamp_value
is not a latch.
• An error message is issued when net_name is specified, but sensitivity <high|low> is
not specified.
• An error message is issued when net_name does not exist in the design.
• A warning message is issued when -async_set_reset is specified and there is
no -async_clamp_value specified in the set_isolation command or through the
set_port_attributes command (as specified in the UPF_async_clamp_value port
attribute). The -async_set_reset option is ignored.
• A warning message is issued when -async_clamp_value is specified, but there is no
-async_set_reset option. The -async_clamp_value option is ignored.
Also, when the UPF_async_clamp_value attribute is specified, but there is no
-async_set_reset option, the attribute is ignored.
Support to Allow Internal Direction for Supply Port
In some flows, at one point in the design process, it is useful to seamlessly swap between
a liberty model and a UPF based model. In this case, a key goal is that the top level UPF
should not be modified.
You can use a top level virtual net to connect ports of liberty models with direction :

processing the explicit references in -ports and -exclude_ports and the implicit
references in -elements and -exclude_elements.
• For each port to be attributed, precedence resolution is done based on the precedence
rules described in the LRM for the set_port_attributes command, but with the
following exception:
Instead of issuing error when two settings with the same precedence but different value
are set on a given port, the latest setting that is applied is used.
• If a port that is part of a bus is attributed with -literal_supply, all the ports of the bus
are attributed with -literal_supply with the same value, otherwise an error is issued
and the setting is ignored.
Reporting
The -literal_supply option affects the supplies for source/sink analysis and
also adds a SRSN type of gate for simulating correct power semantics. The
spa_literal_supply_association.rpt report is useful for debugging various scenarios
where an issue is seen with the simulation.
Following is the report format
{
{ <hierarchical name of the port> <port/net driven by literal> <supply
set/net> }
{ <hierarchical name of the port> <port/net driven by literal> <supply
set/net> }
}

Support for use_retention_as_primary for Isolation Semantics
VCS NLP supports the set_retention -use_retention_as_primary option. When this
option is specified, the retention supply powers the output driver of the register. That is, the
primary supply of the output pin of the retention register is the retention supply.
set_retention retention_name
-domain domain_name
[ -use_retention_as_primary]
set_retention RET1 -domain PD1 -use_retention_as_primary
map_retention_cell -domain PD1 -lib_cells {SDFRET*} RET1
This enhancement allows you to model a retention cell with output related to backup
supply. Specifying the -use_retention_as_primary option instructs VCS NLP to use a
retention cell whose output pin is related to the retention supply (rather than the domain
primary).
Figure 88 Library Cell Used When -use_retention_as_primary is Specified

Support for use_retention_as_primary for Isolation Semantics
• When the -use_retention_as_primary option is not specified, for paths which
originate from the output of the retention, the primary supply of the domain is
considered as the driver_supply.
• When the -use_retention_as_primary option is specified, for paths which originate
from the output of the retention, the retention_supply of the retention strategy is
considered as the driver_supply of the path.
• The -use_retention_as_primary option changes the driver supply of ports that are
sinks of the inserted retention register. Such changes could affect the interpretation of
the -source filters of the set_isolation strategies that apply to those ports.
Corruption and Isolation Semantics

Support for Atomic Power Domains
VCS NLP supports atomic power domains as per 1801-2018 version of the UPF LRM.
As per the LRM, extent of an atomic power domain can be modified, that is, updating
the options -elements {} and -exclude_elements {} of an atomic power domain is
allowed.
You must use the -atomic option of the create_power_domain command to define an
atomic power domain. Following is the syntax for creating an atomic power domain:
create_power_domain <name> -atomic
[-elements element_list]
[-exclude_elements exclude_list]
[…]

Support for Atomic Power Domains
• To define an atomic power domain, you must specify the -atomic option during the first
definition of that power domain. Specifying the -atomic option later with -update is not
allowed, it results in an error and dropping of that constraint.
• For any cell in the extent of atomic power domain to be added to any other power
domain, the cell or its ancestor must be excluded from the atomic power domain.
• In the rest of this section, any mention of the phrase power domain implies non-atomic
power domain.
Supported Usage
The following points describe the supported usage of the -atomic option:
• An empty power domain can be defined as atomic.
• A power domain on macro, ETM, or black box can be defined as atomic.
• A power domain on leaf cells can be defined as atomic.
• You can update the extent of an atomic power domain, that is, updating -elements {}
and -exclude_elements {} is allowed.
• An element excluded from atomic power domain can be added to either atomic or non-
atomic power domain. There is no restriction that an element excluded from atomic
should be added only to atomic power domains.
• There is no restriction that root cells of atomic power domains should be part of same
voltage area. They can be part of different voltage areas too.
Error Checks
The following error checks are added:
Error Check-1
VCS NLP will not allow any instance in the descendant subtree of an atomic power
domain to be included in the extent of another power domain, unless that instance name
is, or is in the descendant subtree of an instance which is excluded from that atomic
domain. Violating this results in an error message (see Example 2).

Marking a Cell or Module As Power Aware by Considering the Direction and Type of Its PG
Pins
Marking a Cell or Module As Power Aware by Considering the
Direction and Type of Its PG Pins
VCS NLP is enhanced to perform a strict DB PG pin matching for a cell or module
by considering the direction and type of its PG pins in Liberty and Verilog model, and
appropriately mark the
IsPowerAwareModuleCell
IsPowerAwareModuleCell attribute as true or false in the
mvsim_native_reports/library_mapping.rpt file. It performs the following checks to
mark a cell or module as power aware:
• If Liberty declares a PG pin with direction : in, it should be direction inout or input in
the Verilog model for the cell or module to be classified as power aware.
• If Liberty declares a PG pin with direction : out, it should be direction inout or output
in the Verilog model for the cell or module to be classified as power aware.
• If the direction of a PG pin in Liberty is unknown, VCS NLP checks for its pg_type.
If pg_type is internal power or ground, it cannot match to an input port, but can match
to either of the output, inout, reg, wire, supply0, supply1, and supply_net_type.
If pg_type is primary power or ground, it can match to any port (input, output, or
inout), reg, wire, supply0, supply1, or supply_net_type.
To enable this feature, use the
-power=strict_db_match
-power=strict_db_match compile-time option.
Simulation behavior depends on whether the Verilog model is power aware or non-power
aware. This feature allows you to correct the Verilog model or make any other required
changes to get accurate simulation behavior of a DB cell or model.

Support for Type Real Option With the sim_corruption_control
Command
VCS NLP supports type real option in the sim_corruption_control command. Following
is the syntax:
sim_corruption_control -type real
This feature allows you to disable corruption of real items and is applicable to complete
design hierarchy covered by the UPF. This feature does not have any effect other than
disabling corruption of real. For example, if the real variable values used in the behavior
models are corrupted, this feature allows you to disable corruption of these real items only.

Support for Golden UPF
Following are the limitations of this feature:
• This feature is supported only for SystemVerilog real variable type only. Wreal or any
other nettype nodes involving ‘real’ are not supported.
• This feature is supported only for pure Verilog designs. VHDL is not supported.
• The corruption is restricted to the ‘simstate’ based corruption only. Therefore, this
feature does not affect the corruption due to isolation power, SRSN/SPA power, or any
port-based corruption.
Support for Golden UPF
In the UPF flow, each stage of the flow uses a single UPF file that is modified during
synthesis and physical implementation in the following ways:
The original UPF file, written with the RTL description, is modified by the Design Compiler,
resulting in the UPF' (UPF prime) file. The UPF' file reflects the changes that occurred
during synthesis such as insertion of always-on buffers, isolation and retention cells, and
PG connections to the cells.
The UPF' file is modified by the IC Compiler, resulting in the UPF'' (UPF double prime) file.
The UPF'' file reflects the changes that occurred during physical implementation, such as
the insertion of power switch cells.
The Synopsys Galaxy Implementation Platform offers a method of maintaining the UPF
multi-voltage power intent of the design using the original “golden” UPF file throughout the
synthesis, physical implementation, and verification steps, along with supplemental UPF
files generated by the Design Compiler and IC Compiler tools. This method is called the
golden UPF flow.
% vcs <design_files> -sverilog -gupf_config power.config
% ./simv
The -gupf_config option allows you to specify the power configuration file
(power.config). Following are the contents of the power.config file:
db_search_path = "<dir1>,<dir2>,…"
db_link_library = "<file1.db>,<file2.db>,…"
set upf_name_map { {mod1 mod1.nmf} {mod2 mod2.nmf} {mod3 mod3.nmf} … }
read_upf <UPF_FILE_NAME> \
-strict_check false \
-supplemental <supplemental_UPF_file> \
-target <icc_netlist|dc_pg_netlist|dc_netlist> \
-scope <TARGET MODULE>

Support for Golden UPF

Global variable. Used to search for .db (liberty) files.
db_link_library
Global variable. Used to specify the list of .db files to be used in the design.
upf_name_map
Global variable. Used to specify the name of the map file for a design top module.
read_upf
This command is used to parse the Synopsys flow compatible UPF file.
The read_upf command must be specified for the top-level UPF file. The options of this
command have the following semantics:
-strict_check false
When false (as for golden UPF application to a netlist), default matching rules are used
for name lookups, if no rules are defined.
-supplemental <supplemental_UPF_file>
Specifies a supplemental UPF file to be loaded after the golden UPF file. The
supplemental UPF additionally supports create_power_domain -elements -update .
-target <icc_netlist|dc_pg_netlist|dc_netlist>
Specifies the target design.

are implemented in the incoming target netlist, and resulting cells are explicitly connected

VCS NLP supports ICC PG netlists where supplies are implemented and
explicitly connected in the netlist.
dc_pg_netlist — Specifies that the supplies are implemented and explicitly connected in
the incoming target DC netlist.
dc_netlist — Specifies that the isolation and retention strategies are implemented in the
incoming target netlist, and resulting cells are explicitly connected to their supplies through
the connect_supply_net commands in the incoming UPF.

VCS NLP allows you to define a supply set state partially and then incrementally refine it

This feature is supported for all types of objects (supply set, domain, and group)

Permitting Supply Set States that do not Have a Supply Network Expression in
Group/Domain State
VCS NLP allows you to refer to a supply set state in a group irrespective of whether the
supply set state has a -supply_expr defined or not. The -supply_expr definition for
the supply set state can come later in the flow, after the group is defined. Consider the
following example:
Example 128 test4.upf
add_power_state SS1 -state ON1 {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON 0.8}}}
add_power_state SS1 -state ON2 {-simstate NORMAL}

create_power_state_group GROUP
add_power_state -group GROUP -state GS1 {-logic_expr {SS1 == ON1}}
add_power_state -group GROUP -state GS2 {-logic_expr {SS1 == ON2}}
-update
For the above UPF, group states GS1 and GS2 are created successfully.
Excluding Ports from the set_port_attributes Command
As per the UPF 3.0, a port is removed from the candidate set if the port name appears in
the -exclude_ports list.

Excluding Ports from the set_port_attributes Command
VCS NLP supports the -exclude_ports option of the set_port_attributes command.
This option provides flexibility for specifying ports for the set_port_attributes
The ports in the list of -exclude_ports are excluded from the current
set_port_attributes command.
• If a port is listed in -exclude_ports of the current set_port_attributes, its previous
set_port_attributes setting continues to apply.
• If all the objects in -exclude_ports do not exist in the design, the entire command is
an error and has no effect.
• If only some, but not all, objects in -exclude_ports do not exist in the design, the
command is applied to the existing objects, and a warning is issued for the non-existing
object.
• If both -exclude_ports and -model are specified, the specified ports of the model are
excluded during candidate set creation. When specified with -model, arguments to the
-exclude_ports option should be simple names. VCS NLP issues an error message if
rooted names are specified in this usage.
Consider the following figure:
Case-1: -exclude_ports with -ports. In the following example, top_in1 is excluded:
set_port_attributes -ports {top_in*} -exclude_ports {top_in1} -attribute
-clamp_value z

The following features are not supported:
• -elements with -exclude_elements
• -elements with -exclude_ports
• Interface/modport support
• VHDL Support
• Bit-level support for -model -exclude_ports
The following attributes are not supported:
• iso_source
• iso_sink
• repeater_power_net
• repeater_ground_net
The
set_retention
set_retention command is enhanced to support the -exclude_elements option in
the UPF. You must use the
-power=ret_exclude
-power=ret_exclude compile option to enable this feature.
This feature allows you to exclude some instances, blocks, or registers from a retention
strategy.
You can use the -exclude_elements option at the time of creating a retention strategy.
set_retention retention_name
-domain domain_name

Example-4
set_retention R1 -elements { I1 I1/J1/K1 } -exclude_elements { I1/J1 }
Elements I1/J1 I1/J1/K{n} (where, n = 2, 3,) are transitively omitted from
retention R1.
In the following figure, the instances with blue color belong to retention R1:
Example-5

set_retention R1 -elements { I* } -exclude_elements { I1 }
Element I{n} (where, n = 2, 3,) belongs to retention R1 transitively.
Example-6
set_retention R1 -elements { I1/flop* } -exclude_elements { I1 }
Exclude is redundant in this case.
Example-7
set_retention R1 -elements { I1 } -exclude_elements { I1/flop1 }
set_retention R2 -elements { I1/J1/K1 }
All the elements below I1/J1/K1 belong to retention R2, otherwise belongs to retention
R1.
Example-8
set_retention R1 -elements { I1 } -exclude_elements { I1/flop1 }
set_retention R2 -elements { I1/J1/K1 I1/flop1 }
Elements I1/flop{n} (where, n = 2, 3,) belong to retention R1. However, element
I1/flop1 belongs to retention R2.
Example-9
set_retention R1 -elements { I1 } -exclude_elements { I1/flop1
I1/J1/flop1 }
set_retention R2 -elements { I1/J1 }
The following elements belong to retention R1:
• {I1/- I1/flop1}
• I1/J{n} where, n = 2, 3,
The following elements belong to retention R2:
• I1/J1
• I1/J1/flop1 (since only specified retention is impacted by this feature).
Example-10
set_retention R1 -elements { I1 } -exclude_elements { I1/flop1 }
set_retention R2 -elements { I1/J1 } -exclude_elements { I1/J1/flop1 }
The following elements belong to retention R1:
• {I1/J{n} - I1/flop1} where, n = 2, 3,

The following elements belong to retention R2:
• {I1/J1 - I1/J1/flop1}
• I1/J1/K{n} where, n = 2, 3,
Example-11
set_retention R1 -elements { I1/J* }
set_retention R2_no -elements { I1/J1 } -no_retention
No retention for I1/J1. Element I1/J(n) where, n = 2,3,… belongs to retention R1.
Example-12
set_retention R1 -elements { I1 }
set_retention R2 -elements { I1/J1 } -exclude_elements { I1/J1/K1 }
The following elements belong to retention R1:
• I1/J{n}/K{s} where, n = 2, 3,and S = 1,2,3,
The following element belongs to retention R2:
• J1/K2
In the following figure, the instances with blue color belong to retention R1 and instance
with orange color belongs to retention R2.

Setting Attributes on UPF Objects
Example-13
set_retention R1 -elements { I1 }
set_retention R2_no -elements { I1/J1 } -exclude_elements { I1/J1/K1 }
-no_retention
The following elements belong to retention R1:
• I1/J{n} where, n = 2, 3,
The following element belongs to retention R2_no:
• I1/J1/K1
Example-14
set_retention R1 -elements { I1/flop* } -exclude_elements {I1/flop1}
Except I1/flop1, all the other flops belong to retention R2.
Example-15
set_retention x -elements {a}
set_retention y -elements {a/b} -transition {false}
In this example, even if there is no -exclude_elements, the grand parenting rule is
applied. The y retention has transition as false. In this case, the hierarchy below y
retention would be assigned to retention x.
Following is the limitation of this feature:
• This feature is not supported for the VHDL designs.

upf_get_handle_by_name
VCS NLP supports the following types of handles:
• Object Handles
References to the objects in the UPF information model. These handles can be
compared using a == operator.
• Iterator Handles
Iterators to containers in the UPF information model. These handles can be reused as
iterators are scoped objects and get deleted after the iteration is complete. You must
not use the iterator handles with the == operator for comparison.
• Property Handles
References to property value wrapper. These handles are same for all integer/Boolean
properties, real, string, and supply type properties. You must not use the iterator
handles with the == operator for comparison.

Searching Specified Scope and Its Descendant Hierarchy
The find_objects command searches for instances, nets, ports, supply ports, or
processes within a scope.
A leaf cell is any cell having no descendants. Standard cells and macros are always
considered to be leaf cells. Any hierarchy with the terminal_boundary attribute is also
considered as a leaf cell. For macros, a UPF_is_hard_macro attribute value of TRUE on
a model or a UPF_is_soft_macro attribute value of TRUE on an instance indicates that it
shall be treated as a leaf cell.
VCS NLP allows you to search the specified scope and its entire descendant hierarchy
without considering the terminal_boundary/UPF_is_soft_macro marking using the
-traverse_macros option. Following is the syntax:
find_objects scope
-pattern search_ pattern
[-object_type <model | inst | port | supply_port | net | process>]
[-direction <in | out | inout>]
[-transitive [<TRUE | FALSE>]]
[-regexp | -exact]
[-ignore_case]
[-non_leaf | -leaf_only]
[ -traverse_macros]
• When you specify the -traverse_macros option, the traversal stops at a standard cell
and hard macro boundaries.
• If the -traverse_macros option is specified, then -transitive TRUE is implicitly
specified.
• The -traverse_macros option is supported only for -object_type model | inst
• VCS NLP issues a warning message when you specify object type ( -object_type)
other than model | inst . For example:
find_objects . -pattern in1 -object_type port -traverse_macros

Instrumentation for pg_function Attribute
The instrumentation for pg_function attribute takes the following scenarios into
consideration:
• Scenario-1: PG pin is power aware and wire type with HDL drivers
In this case, the wire value is used to drive the stage, and voltage is driven by MUX as
inferred from the liberty file.
• Scenario-2: PG pin is power aware and wire type with no HDL drivers
In this case, the PG pin gets the supply_net_type value from the inferred MUX, and
the wire value is a VCT version of the supply_net_type value.

Simulation Control Commands Support
• Scenario-3: PG pin is power aware and supply_net_type with HDL drivers
In this case, the inferred MUX is not instrumented and the supply_net_type value is
used as is.
• Scenario-4: PG pin is power aware and supply_net_type with no HDL drivers
In this case, the supply_net_type value is driven by inferred MUX instrumentation.
• Scenario-5: PG pin is not power aware
In this case, the supply_net_type node is added and the supply_net_type value is
driven by inferred MUX instrumentation.

Using the sim_corruption_control Command
The sim_corruption_control command allows you to turn off corruption semantics for
specific set of design elements. This command allows behavioral modules (for example,
real number modules) to operate correctly in a low power environment. This command is
only applicable for functional verification.
The following is the syntax of the sim_corruption_control command:
sim_corruption_control
[-elements element_list]
[-model model_name]
When -elements is specified, the elements shall be a list of variables, registers, signals
of the specified hierarchical instances. If the element is an instance, then by default the
command applies to all objects defined in that instance and all dependent subtrees.
Wildcards are supported with this option.
When -model is specified, only names that are declared in the model can be referenced
in the -elements option, and all names are interpreted relative to the topmost scope of
the model. You must use this option along with the -elements option, otherwise VCS NLP
issues an error message.

Simulation Control Commands Support
When -elements is specified along with -model, then the specified elements should be
local to the model.

Support for UPF Power-Aware Converters
The following sections describe the support for UPF power-aware converters:
• Introduction
Converter modules convert signal values from one type to another. There will be no
specification of liberty for converter modules. A converter module has two scalar ports of
two different types (input and output). A converter is instantiated between a port and the
signal that is connected at the high-conn of the port connection.
One of the major challenges during simulation in presence of UPF is to correctly simulate
the converter modules that are inserted by the tool at real-logic boundaries. For a logic-to-
real converter, when a logic signal information is sent to a block, the corresponding supply
(that is, power, ground) associated with that logic signal should play a role to determine
the real number value.

Support for UPF Power-Aware Converters
On the other hand, for a real-to-logic converter, when the real output pin changes its value,
the corresponding supply associated with this pin should be considered to convert the real
number value to corresponding logic value.
VCS supports UPF power-aware converters. The following sections describe how the
converter modules behave in presence of the power sources defined in UPF.
This feature is enabled by default. However, you must specify all the relevant options
that are required for inserting converter modules. For more information, refer to the VCS
Converters section in the VCS User Guide.
If you want to disable the feature, use the following compile-time option:
%vcs -power=disable_supply_aware_converter

SystemVerilog variables declared locally inside the module. The attributes of the two
variables are snps_cm_power and snps_cm_ground respectively. These two local
variables should be of type UPF::supply_net_type.

Isolation Insertion on Heterogeneous Fanout Paths
The following points describe the support for isolation insertion on heterogeneous fanout
paths:
• This feature improves the granularity of the set_isolation -sink/-
diff_supply_only option. Also, this support changes the isolation conflict resolution
by allowing two isolation strategies to have the same options other than -sink/-
diff_supply_only.
• VCS NLP can insert isolation cells wherever they deem fit as long as they do not
violate the isolation constraints. Also, heterogeneous fanout support does not insert
isolation cells as less as possible.
• The heterogeneous fanout isolation cells can be inserted at any hierarchy boundary
provided that they reside at the power domain specified by the strategy (and do not
cross the power domain).
• Each path is isolated by its highest precedence strategy (assuming all filters are
satisfied) only, otherwise it is not isolated.
• If isolation insertion is not possible due to the location violating the filters, a lower-
precedence strategy is not applied (-diff_supply_only/self, no filters/parent/self).
• The following warning message is issued when the highest precedence strategy is not
applied due to the location violating the -diff_supply_only/-source/-sink filters.
Warning-[UPF_ISO_HETEROGENEOUS_FANOUTS] Isolation skipped due to
hetero fanout
• The heterogeneous fanout isolation cells from the -applies_to input strategy can be
closer to the output of the power domain boundary than the input.
• An error message is issued if both conservative_diff_supply_isolation and
hetero_fanout_isolation are enabled. Following is the sample error message:
Error-[UPF_ATTRS_CONFLICT] Conflicting design attributes specified

VCS NLP compile-time reports are dumped by default inside the mvsim_native_reports
directory. For large designs, a lot of information is dumped in each of these reports
resulting in large file sizes. However, you may not need all the reports for diagnostic
purposes. Therefore, this leads to performance degradation and resource utilization.
You can use the -power_report=<switch> compile option to control the dumping of
reports. You can use this option to enable or disable the reports that are dumped in the low
power analysis stage based on your requirement.
This feature improves compile performance for large designs by dumping only the required
reports. Also, you can the disable dumping of all reports by default in the regression mode.

The following topics describe this feature in detail:
• Enabling and Disabling Dumping of Individual Reports
• Enabling and Disabling Report Groups
• Precedence Details
• Supported Reports
• Examples
The following is the use model:
% vcs design.v -upf design.upf -sverilog -power_report=<switch>
All reports will have a separate switch name that can be passed to -power_report=
prefixed with either the - sign to disable the report or the + sign to enable the report.
If an invalid switch name is provided, VCS NLP issues a warning message with
the NLP-UNKNOWN-PWR-RPT-OPT tag. If multiple switch names are provided and
one of them is an invalid option, then the warning message is printed only for
the invalid option. The remaining switches are processed without any issues.
Enabling and Disabling Dumping of Individual Reports
This section describes how to enable and disable the dumping of individual reports
using switch. Following is the use model to enable/disable the dumping of the individual
reports:
% vcs -power_report=+/-<report_name>
Examples:
-power_report=+db_inside_db
Enables the dumping of the db_inside_db.rpt files inside the mvsim_native_reports
directory during compilation.
-power_report=-db_inside_db
Disables the dumping of the db_inside_db.rpt files inside the mvsim_native_reports
directory during compilation.

Multiple reports can be enabled/disabled to control individual report dumping. For
example,
-power_report=-srsn_spa_association-upf_supply_net-upf_supply_port
Disables the dumping of the srsn_spa_association.rpt, upf_supply_net.rpt,
and upf_supply_port.rpt files inside the mvsim_native_reports directory during
compilation.
-power_report=new_isolation_association-upf_supply_source
Dumps the new_isolation_association.rpt report that is disabled by default and
disables the upf_supply_source.rpt report that is dumped by default.
Enabling and Disabling Report Groups
The -power_report=<switch> option also provides the feature to enable/disable a group
of reports by passing a single switch. The reports are classified under the following groups
to enable/disable a group of reports:

Using the group feature, you do not have to pass individual reports to the switch. Instead,

% vcs -power_report=+/-<group_name>
Examples:
-power_report=-all_diag
Disables the dumping of all the diagnostic reports which are dumped by default.
-power_report=stats or -power_report=+stats

Semantics of the create_logic_net Command
The create_logic_net command creates a wire type net in the scope of the command.
This command accepts a simple name for a net. If the same name net already exists,
then VCS checks its type. If the type of existing net is one of logic, reg, or wire, then it is
the implementation of the UPF net specified in the command. The existing net must be a
scalar of a compatible type (logic, reg, or wire).

Table 45 create_logic_net Command
Purpose Define a logic net
Syntax create_logic_net net_name
Arguments net_name. Specifies a simple name.
Return value Return an empty string if successful. If not, issue a TCL_ERROR.
If the net type is not compatible or is not a scalar, then VCS reports an error message
when the command is processed d

CL_ERROR.

If the same name scalar port exists in the design with a compatible type (logic, reg, wire),
then VCS uses it as the implementation of the UPF logic port. If the type is incompatible or
the port is not scalar, VCS issues an error message.
If the port existing in the design has a different direction compared to the UPF, then the
direction of the UPF overrides the existing port direction. The direction of the existing port
in design changes to the UPF-specified direction. VCS issues a warning message for a
change in direction.
If the same name scalar net exists in the design with the compatible type (logic, reg, or
wire), then VCS uses that net as the lowconn of the UPF logic port. VCS issues a warning
message for reusing a design port in the UPF.
With the creation of Logic Port, an implicit Logic Net of the same name as the port is
implicitly created. If after UPF reading, the Logic Port is not connected to a Logic Net on
lowconn, then the implicitly created net shall be connected to the Logic Port implicitly. Due
to this implicit Logic Net creation, the Logic Port can be used in any UPF command where
a hierarchical net is used as captured in Table 48.
The Logic Port created by this command can be used in any successive command that

er, it might take a few cycles for signals to be stabilized and could still be X.
Therefore, if the assertions start immediately on wake-up, it can still cause failures.
The -control_expr option provides another way, where you can delay enabling the
assertions until signals are stabilized after power-up.
When this option is specified, the sim_assertion_control command is controlled
by the Boolean value of the expression. If the expression evaluates to TRUE, the
command is active and when it evaluates to FALSE, the command goes inactive. When
the command is active, the assertions controlled by sim_assertion_control are
disabled.
sim_assertion_control -type suspend -control_expr a&&b
For the above command, assertion control is active with type KILL for all power
domains when the control expression a&&b becomes TRUE. When activated, all
assertions in those domains get suspended and are resumed when the control
expression a&&b becomes FALSE.
The sim_assertion_control command can be specified globally or on a particular
domain. The global specification can be overridden by a domain-level specification.
Consider the following commands:
1. sim_assertion_control -type reset -domain {PD1}
2. sim_assertion_control -type suspend
3. sim_assertion_control -type reset -domain {PD2}
The first and third commands enable the assertion control on PD1 and PD2. The second
command specifies the assertion control type as suspend globally on all domains, but
this does not override the domain-level specification in the other two commands as the
domain-level specification takes priority over the global specification.
The same override semantics are applied even in the presence of -control_expr.
Some commands can use domain state, and some can use -control_expr for
controlling assertions. Consider the following commands:
1. sim_assertion_control -type reset -domain {PD1}
2. sim_assertion_control -type suspend -control_expr {a == 1'b1}
3. sim_assertion_control -type reset -domain {PD2} -control_expr {b ==
1'b1}
In the above example, assertions in PD1 are controlled by domain state (command
1) and assertions in PD2 are controlled by expression b == 1'b1 (command 3).
Assertions in all other domains are controlled with the expression a == 1'b1
(command 2).

Support for the sim_assertion_control -control_expr Command
Following are the limitations of the sim_assertion_control -control_expr command
support:
• Using UPF logic nets or logic ports in -control_expr is not supported.
• Using power state expressions in -control_expr is not supported.

Each delay source/event is independently counted. Each low
EPC cycle may be counted multiple times, once per every delay
event simulated in that cycle. The sum of counts, therefore,
may exceed the total number of low EPC cycles
• Only VCS 64-bit is supported.
• SDF and specify block delays are not mapped. They are shown as UNMAPPED SDF
EVENT.
• Structural delays (that is, delays in continuous assignments) may not be mapped to
source. They are shown as UNMAPPED EVENT .
• AMS is not supported.

• Profiles only Verilog events and skips VHDL delay events.
